stem: A PMO is shifting from a predictive to an adaptive approach for delivering the organization’s projects. For this purpose, concerned employees are undergoing agile training. During one of the training sessions, a participant wonders how many people a project team should include. What is the appropriate answer to the participant’s question?

options.A: 1 to 5 members
options.B: 3 to 9 members
options.C: 10 to 15 members
options.D: There is no standard number

explanation: It’s recommended that an agile team should include to members. Since the level of communication deteriorates as the team size increases, Agile organizations favor smaller teams. For instance, it’s better to have two teams of five people than one team of ten.

stem: A project manager oversees an agile project for developing a mobile application for a fast-paced startup. The project involves a cross-functional team comprising developers, designers, and testers. As the project progresses, the project manager encounters various challenges such as technological complexities, stakeholder communication gaps, and collaboration issues. What should be the project manager’s primary focus to ensure the team remains aligned with agile principles?

options.A: Ensuring the team delivers new features as frequently as possible.
options.B: Establishing accurate and detailed plans to guide the team's work and minimize communication and quality issues.
options.C: Implementing rigorous quality control measures to ensure the application meets the highest standards of performance and usability.
options.D: Prioritizing the delivery of features that directly contribute to the client's goals and provide tangible value to end-users.

explanation:
Delivering value should always be the agile team’s top priority as it represents one of the agile manifesto principles: “working software over comprehensive documentation”. From the client’s perspective, value represents the benefit derived from using a product or a service.
Option A: Delivering features frequently enables rapid feedback and adaptation, which is indeed crucial in agile projects. However, the agile team should mainly focus on delivering value with each new feature instead of focusing only on the delivery frequency.
Option B: Creating detailed and accurate plans is a common practice in predictive projects which is not the case in this scenario. Option C: Implementing quality control measures does not directly address the mentioned challenges. Besides, agile calls for progressive elaboration and continuous improvements; the first of the agile 12 principles states: “Our highest priority is to satisfy the customer through the early and continuous delivery of valuable software.

stem: An organization hires an external agile coach as part of its transformation project. In the final report, the agile coach mentions that measures should be taken to enable agile teams to be cross-functional. How should the organization proceed with the agile coach recommendation?

options.A: Allow individuals to collectively determine the best way to accomplish the goal of the sprint.
options.B: Allow individuals to take part in guiding the product direction.
options.C: Assign individuals who possess the necessary skills to produce a functioning product.
options.D: Empower individuals to approve the potentially shippable product increment.

explanation:
A cross-functional team must possess the necessary competencies for creating a product or a service independently, without relying on other members outside of the team.
Option A: A self-organizing team is when individuals collectively determine the best way to accomplish the sprint goal.
Options B & D: The product owner is mainly responsible for guiding the product direction and approving the potentially shippable product increment.

stem: In order to promote adaptability and minimize disruptions, a project manager decides to adopt an Agile development approach that allows the project team to work in a continuous flow rather than using iteration-based cycles. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Implement daily stand-up meetings to enhance communication and collaboration.
options.B: Encourage self-organization and decision-making within the team.
options.C: Break down project deliverables into smaller, manageable increments.
options.D: Use a Kanban framework to optimize workflow and identify bottlenecks.

explanation: The Kanban method involves pulling work into the system only when the team is capable of handling it. The Kanban method prioritizes productivity and efficiency through its workflow approach. The Kanban Method is less prescriptive than some agile approaches and less disruptive. A Kanban board helps the team to further improve its effectiveness by visualizing the flow of work, making impediments easily visible. (Agile Practice Guide pages 13 & 31).

stem: A project manager is leading a software development project using an agile framework. In the current iteration, the team encounters a technical challenge related to integrating a third-party API into the system. To address this challenge, the team decided to allocate time for a spike to look into the issue. Based on the below iteration burndown chart, at which period of the iteration did the team take the spike?

options.A: A
options.B: B
options.C: C
options.D: D

explanation: A spike is a time-boxed activity aimed at addressing a technical challenge or mitigating risks. Spikes usually result in a temporary slowdown or pause in the team's velocity as they allocate time for research or exploration. Analyzing the provided burndown chart, you can observe slow progress at the beginning of the iteration followed by a light pause starting Day 2 to Day 4, followed by a resumption of the downward trend. This deviation indicates the time allocated for the spike to address the technical challenge.

stem: A project manager is leading the development of a new software project. The project manager wants to adopt an approach that produces key deliverables at various stages of the project. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Create a detailed project schedule with key milestones to track progress against the plan.
options.B: Deliver incremental results that can be added to the subsequent results.
options.C: Organize frequent review meetings with project stakeholders to gather feedback and adjust project direction.
options.D: Adopt an iterative approach in order to deliver the highest business value earlier.

explanation:
Delivering partial results at various intervals refers to the incremental approach. In this type of development approach, the project is divided into increments which are successively delivered to avoid waiting for everything to be completed in order to create a solution (PMBOK 7th edition, page 241).
Option A: Creating a detailed project schedule with key milestones means adopting a predictive approach and only delivering at the end of the project. Option C: Organizing review meetings to gather feedback and adjust project direction is a main aspect of the iterative approach. The iterative approach focuses on correctness. It typically includes multiple essays and one acceptable deliverable at the end of the project.
Option D: Delivering the highest business value earlier is the aspect of the incremental approach, not the iterative approach. The incremental approach focuses on speed, while the iterative approach focuses on correctness.

stem: By the end of the third iteration, a project manager delivered the website to the customer and signed a maintenance contract to fix any issues that might occur. On the first day of the maintenance contract period, the customer reported an error on the contact page when using a smartphone. After verifying the issue with the project team, the project manager realized that testing the contact feature on mobile was omitted. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Reopen the project and fix the error since testing the contact feature on mobile was omitted.
options.B: Ask the sponsor to submit a formal change request with an anterior date in order to be considered a part of the project.
options.C: Request from the project team to fix the issue according to the maintenance contract.
options.D: Do nothing since the error is discovered after the formal closure of the project.

explanation: An escaped defect is one that was not detected by the project team but rather discovered by the customer or end-user after the product is released. These defects are usually covered by a maintenance contract. Therefore, the project manager should request the project team to fix the issue according to the maintenance contract.

stem: The following chart was presented during a retrospective meeting. Which of the following statements is true regarding this chart?

options.A: This burnup chart shows that there is work left at the end of the sprint
options.B: This burnup chart shows that the planned work is completed before the end of the sprint
options.C: This burndown chart shows that there is work left at the end of the sprint
options.D: This burndown chart shows that the planned work is completed before the end of the sprint

explanation: This chart is a burndown chart that shows that there is work left at the end of the sprint (PMBOK 7th edition, page 108). In fact, 3 story points are left to be completed in order to finalize all the planned work for the exhibited 7-day sprint.

stem: A project manager works on a software project. During the last retrospective meeting, several topics were evoked. Which of the following topics can be discussed in such a meeting?

options.A: How to decompose a complex user story into manageable tasks
options.B: Which user stories should be prioritized in the next sprint
options.C: How to fix the regression of a product feature
options.D: Whether the standup timing is suitable for all team members

explanation:
During the sprint retrospective, the project manager should identify what went well during the sprint and what can be done differently in the next sprint. A possible topic is the timing of the standup. If team members are showing dissatisfaction with the current schedule, then the retrospective meeting is the right event to discuss the issue.
Options A & B: The sprint planning meeting is the right meeting for discussing which tasks should be prioritized in the next sprint and how to decompose user stories into manageable tasks.
Option C: Dedicated project team meetings and Backlog refinement meetings should address topics related to product development, including finding ways to fix regressions.

stem: This is the first time the project manager has adopted the scrum framework for the project execution. One of the team members asks the project manager when a Sprint is considered completed. What should be the project manager’s response?

options.A: When all product backlog items are completed
options.B: When all the tasks in the sprint are completed
options.C: When the sprint’s defined timebox ends
options.D: When all product backlog items meet the Definition of Done (DoD)

explanation:
A sprint is considered complete only when it reaches the end of its duration/timebox, which is usually 1 to 4 weeks.
Option B: In some cases, the sprint ends without finishing all of the assigned tasks, so this can’t be the criteria for sprint completion.

stem: A project manager is facing some challenges because of a key stakeholder. The project manager collaborated with this stakeholder in previous projects where the latter frequently changed the requirements and created trouble whenever those requirements were not met. How should the project manager deal with this issue?

options.A: Adopt an Agile approach
options.B: Involve the concerned stakeholder right from the start
options.C: Ask the concerned stakeholder to mend their ways
options.D: Inform management about the issue

explanation:
The project manager should involve the key stakeholder from the very beginning of the project to help reduce and uncover risks, as well as increase their “buy-in.”
Option A: While implementing an agile approach may benefit the project, it does not address the issue of stakeholder management. If the question were “What’s the appropriate approach for the project?”, then adopting an agile approach would be the right answer taking into consideration the frequently changing requirements.

stem: In a mid-sized technology company, the executive leadership has recognized the need to adapt to changing market dynamics and improve project delivery efficiency. As a result, they have initiated a company-wide transformation to adopt Agile methodologies. The project manager, assigned to lead this transformation, faces several challenges in facilitating the organization's shift to Agile practices; employees have varying levels of experience with the Agile approach, so there is resistance to change from some stakeholders who are accustomed to traditional project management approaches and are skeptical about the benefits of Agile. Additionally, the company operates in a highly regulated industry with stringent compliance requirements, which must be addressed during the Agile transformation process. What should the project manager do? (Select two)

options.A: Dismiss reservations and skepticism about this transformation since resistance to big changes is natural.
options.B: Establish a cross-functional Agile transformation team comprising representatives from different departments to ensure alignment, collaboration, and inclusivity throughout the transformation process.
options.C: Conduct a comprehensive organizational assessment to evaluate the organization’s suitability for adopting the Agile approach.
options.D: Develop a tailored Agile training program to address the diverse needs and skill levels of employees.

explanation:
Establishing a cross-functional Agile transformation team comprising representatives from different departments to ensure alignment, collaboration, and inclusivity throughout the transformation journey empowers employees to drive change initiatives and address specific challenges unique to their respective areas. It also recognizes the importance of collaboration and inclusivity in driving organizational change and encourages employees to take ownership of the Agile transformation process, leading to more sustainable and successful outcomes. Developing a tailored Agile training program is essential for addressing the diverse needs and skill levels of employees. By offering customized training sessions and ongoing support, the project manager can ensure that all employees receive the necessary knowledge and guidance to embrace Agile practices effectively. Option A: Ignoring feedback and concerns from employees and stakeholders who express reservations or skepticism about the transformation to Agile and dismissing their input as resistance to change may lead to disengagement and morale issues among team members, hindering collaboration and cooperation in the Agile transformation process.
Option C: An organizational assessment to evaluate the organization’s suitability for adopting the Agile approach might have already been done since the decision to transform to Agile was already taken.

stem: A project manager is leading a rebranding project using a predictive approach for the planning phase and an Agile approach for work execution. The project manager receives an email from a key stakeholder requesting an estimation of the project completion date. In order to estimate the completion date, the project manager takes into consideration the team’s average velocity, which is 20 story points, and the fact that the project still has 205 remaining user story points to complete. How many iterations will it take to finish the project work?

options.A: 10 iterations
options.B: 11 iterations
options.C: 12 iterations
options.D: Cannot be determined

explanation: If the team maintains an average velocity of 20 story points per iteration, it would take 11 iterations to complete the remaining 205 story points. (205 story points / 20 story points = 10.25 iterations). Since the timebox of an iteration should not be changed, the project team will need 11 iterations to complete the rest of the work.

stem: A project manager is managing a software development project. In order to ensure that the project’s agile team is cross-functional, the project manager hires an experienced designer. A few days later, the designer informs the project manager that he’s unable to do his work properly because the subscription plan of the design application he’s using doesn’t include all of the functionalities he needs. Therefore, the designer asks for an upgraded subscription plan. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Ask the designer to raise the issue during the next retrospective meeting
options.B: Tell the designer to be self-reliant by dealing with the situation and finding turnarounds
options.C: Explain to the designer that his current subscription plan is sufficient for fulfilling his assigned tasks
options.D: Reach out to the appropriate stakeholder to upgrade the designer’s subscription plan

explanation:
As a servant leader, the project manager should reach out to the appropriate stakeholder in order to upgrade the designer’s subscription plan.
Option B: In an agile work environment, the project manager should listen to the impediments faced by their team members and act to solve them. If the designer’s subscription plan cannot be upgraded, then the project manager should explain this, asking the designer to try finding turnarounds, such as using other complementary applications that offer the functionalities that he needs to perform his work.
Option C: Agile teams are self-organized, i.e. they decide how they should perform their work. Thus, forcing the designer to use a limited subscription plan is inappropriate. Furthermore, since the designer is experienced, he’s able to clearly identify his needs, therefore the scrum master or the project manager should cater to the designer’s job requirements rather than argue with the latter.
Option A: Retrospective meetings are set up to improve processes and not to remove impediments.

stem: During the sprint planning, the team decomposed a user story into four tasks. When working on the user story, a team member identified a fifth task. What should the team member do?

options.A: Update the user story and work on the new task
options.B: Report the issue to the Scrum Master
options.C: Request from the product owner to approve the new task
options.D: Add the task to the product backlog

explanation:
The project team is responsible for how to do the work. Therefore, if a new task is identified within the user story it could be immediately added.
Option B: The situation doesn’t involve any issue. The team member can add, adjust, or remove tasks in order to deliver the user story according to its acceptance criteria.
Option C: The new task doesn’t require the product owner's approval since it’s a technical component of an agreed-upon user story.
Option D: If the task represents a new feature or doesn’t contribute to the validation of the user story, then it should be added to the product backlog. In the described scenario, however, the task is an integral part of the user story.

stem: At a trade show, a prospect stops at the stand of a company that specializes in selling and installing network security appliances. The prospect asks the representative if their company can provide and set up 10 firewall hardware devices in 5 weeks, recommending an incremental approach to deliver 2 firewalls per week. The prospect adds that an external security expert will be conducting a penetration test, and that final acceptance will be granted only after all performed cyber attacks are detected and prevented. What is the prospect defining in the above scenario? (Select two)

options.A: Definition of Done
options.B: Quality Assurance
options.C: Technical Requirements
options.D: Quality Control

explanation:
A Definition of Done (DoD) is a checklist of the required criteria for considering a product ready for delivery (PMBOK 7th edition, page 81). The prospect also describes the quality control process that will focus on defect identification.
Option B: Quality assurance focuses on defect prevention.
Option C: Technical requirements cover the product requirements, such as WiFi support, storage, number of LANs, etc.

stem: To guide the development team on what they intend to achieve, a product owner of an HR solution shares the following table depicting the key deliverables of each quarter of the 9-month project. What agile artifact does this table represent?

options.A: Product vision statement
options.B: Product wireframe
options.C: Product roadmap
options.D: Product backlog

explanation:
The product roadmap is built by the product owner to demonstrate the anticipated sequence of deliverables over the project duration (Agile Practice Guide, page 52). As an Agile artifact, the product roadmap sets the product’s strategic view, indicating where the product is headed in both the short and long terms. In agile organizations, the product roadmap serves as a guide rather than a project plan.
Option A: A product vision statement outlines what a product would look like to ultimately achieve its vision and give purpose to its existence. A vision statement should be short, simple, and specific.
Option B: The Product wireframe is a mockup or a sketch of the user interface, high-level functionality, page layout, etc.
Option D: The product roadmap is different from the product backlog in that the product roadmap provides the big picture while the product backlog tackles the practical and feasible steps required to tangibly create the product.

stem: An experienced scrum master is often asked “How long should a sprint be?” to which the scrum master always responds by saying “It depends, you should initially find a balance that works for the team, but typically an agile scrum sprint is ____________ long.”

options.A: 3-5 days
options.B: 1 week
options.C: 2-4 weeks
options.D: 5-8 weeks

explanation: A Sprint has to be long enough for the team to finish all included stories. As per a Scrum rule, a Sprint should never exceed one month. The duration of a sprint depends on the project size and complexity as well as the team’s capacities. It takes 2 to 4 weeks on average to complete a sprint with a team of 3-9 members working on a single project.

stem: The project team holds a monthly status review meeting with the product owner to review post-iteration deliverables. What’s the best communication type to use in a status review meeting?

options.A: Push
options.B: Pull
options.C: Interactive
options.D: Formal

explanation: When an immediate response is required and the information you’re communicating is sensitive and could be misinterpreted, you should use interactive communication. It involves one or more people sharing thoughts and ideas, with participants responding in real time. Interactive communication can take place through teleconferences or face-to-face contact. When using communication media such as emails, the project manager can’t pick up on stakeholders’ facial expressions and body language.

stem: During the standup meeting, a team member raises an impediment. In order to address this impediment, the project manager suggests that two other members sit with the team members facing the issue and collaborate to find the appropriate solution. What technique is the project manager suggesting? (Select two)

options.A: Pairing
options.B: Swarming
options.C: Mobbing
options.D: Brainstorming

explanation:
Swarming and mobbing imply that multiple team members or the entire team focus collectively on resolving a specific impediment.
Option A: Although pairing, swarming, and mobbing all represent collaboration techniques used by the Agile team (Agile Practice Guide, page 39), the situation doesn’t describe pairing since this technique requires only two team members to work together to resolve an issue.
Option D: Brainstorming is used to generate ideas, rather than to resolve issues.

stem: Halfway through the current iteration, the progress report reveals that the agile project is off track. The project manager didn’t expect that since he carefully sequenced and assigned all project work to meet the iteration goal. What should the project manager have done differently to avoid this issue?

options.A: Train the team on how to implement the agile approach
options.B: Encourage the team to record their progress using the reporting system
options.C: Set up a contingency reserve
options.D: Encourage the team to self-organize to ensure their buy-in

explanation: Since he’s leading an agile project, the project manager should have empowered his team to be self-organized through handling iteration tasks selection and prioritization, rather than solely taking care of work sequencing and assignment. This ensures a high level of buy-in from the team. Encouraging the team to self-organize typically results in a highly motivated staff since it allows them to gain the autonomy to choose the most efficient way to accomplish their work (PMBOK 7th edition, page 249).

stem: A product owner sends a document including all the product backlog items to the project manager. The project manager informs the product owner that these product backlog items should be prioritized throughout the project. What should the project manager recommend?

options.A: The business analyst and project manager collaborate to define the priorities of the product backlog items.
options.B: The team prioritized the product backlog items based on their size; smaller items at the top and larger items at the bottom.
options.C: The product owner places the most valuable items at the top.
options.D: The sponsor decides the priority of product backlog items based on the need.

explanation: Ordering Product Backlog items is one of the Product Owner’s responsibilities although they may delegate the responsibility to others. Regardless, the Product Owner remains accountable. The most valuable product backlog items should be placed at the top.

stem: A project manager is leading a software development team to build a new e-commerce platform for a client. While selecting the suitable development approach for this project, the project manager wants to ensure that he’s choosing an approach that offers unique benefits tailored to the specific project requirements and objectives. Match each development approach with its corresponding description.
explanation: Correct Answer ● Behavior-Driven Development (BDD): Employing scenarios and specifications to drive the creation of automated tests. ● Test-Driven Development (TDD): Writing tests before writing code and then refactoring the code for improvement. ● Feature-Driven Development (FDD): Defining the interactions the client wishes to perform and breaking them down into smaller work pieces for development. ● Continuous Integration: Frequently incorporating work into the whole and then retesting to determine if everything still works as intended.

stem: A project manager is assigned to an Agile software development project. The project is almost completed when the client requests an additional feature that was not initially among the project requirements. The project is already nearing its budget limit, and accommodating the new requirement would require new funds. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Immediately incorporate the new requirement since agile prioritizes customer satisfaction and flexibility.
options.B: Negotiate with the client to prioritize the new requirement against other features and functionalities.
options.C: Decline the client's request for the new requirement due to budget constraints.
options.D: Escalate the request to the CCB for a decision on whether to prioritize the client's request.

explanation:
The project manager should negotiate with the client to prioritize the new requirement against other features and functionalities in the product backlog. Agile advocates for responding to change and satisfying the client, but this should be balanced with the project's budget constraints, considering that the budget is fixed in Agile projects.
Option A: The project manager should not immediately incorporate the new requirement, taking into consideration the impact and implementation requirements of the new feature.
Option C: The project manager should not decline the client's request for the new requirement due to budget constraints as it will lead to client dissatisfaction, which goes against agile principles of satisfying the customer and welcoming changing requirements, even late in development (Agile Practice Guide, page 98).
Option D: Escalating the request to the CCB is inaccurate since the scenario involves an agile project and not a predictive one.

stem: A project manager was assigned to lead a new project. Wondering about the project completion date, the product owner asks the project manager: “How many story points do you expect to complete per sprint?”. In order to provide the product owner with an accurate response, the project manager should:

options.A: Estimate the sprint velocity based on the team members’ input.
options.B: Complete multiple sprints in order to be able to answer the product owner’s question.
options.C: Rely on their own judgment as an experienced project manager to estimate the team's velocity.
options.D: Engage the team in estimating their velocity based on their previous agile projects.

explanation:
Typically, the project manager should rely on the available historical data of their team's velocity in order to set a reasonable and achievable number of story points per sprint, depending entirely on your team’s capacities and how much they can accomplish.
Options A & C: When a new team has no historical data, the sprint forecast can be done based on your experience with similar projects along with collaborative estimations from the entire team, to determine how many story points they can potentially deliver in the first sprint.

stem: Throughout his long career, a project manager has always followed a servant leadership style, particularly with agile teams. What does servant leadership imply?

options.A: One individual in charge of directing and guiding the team
options.B: Carrying out work through iterations, with one prominent leader
options.C: Naming a team leader, while team members serve as followers
options.D: Understanding and addressing the needs of team members

explanation: According to the Agile Practice Guide, servant leadership implies leading your team by focusing on understanding and addressing their needs to yield the best performance possible (PMBOK 7th edition, page 17).

stem: A project manager adopts an agile approach to develop credit card fraud detection software. The project team consistently struggles to complete all the user stories allocated for each sprint. Despite their efforts, they frequently fall short of achieving the sprint goals, leading to frustration and concerns about project progress. What is the most probable reason for the project team's inability to complete all sprint backlog items?

options.A: Insufficient collaboration and communication within the team, leading to misunderstandings and inefficiencies in task execution.
options.B: Inadequate sprint planning, resulting in unrealistic or overly ambitious sprint goals that are challenging to achieve within the allocated time frame.
options.C: Lack of the needed expertise or skills among team members, leading to delays in implementing user stories and meeting sprint objectives.
options.D: External disruptions, such as changes in requirements, impacting the team's ability to deliver on time.

explanation:
Inadequate sprint planning is the most probable reason for the team’s failure to complete all sprint story points. Unrealistic or overly ambitious sprint goals can lead to underestimation of effort and result in incomplete work by the end of the sprint.
Option A: Collaboration and communication are indeed essential, but they may not be the primary reason for the team's inability to complete sprint story points. Even with effective collaboration, poor sprint planning can still lead to challenges in meeting sprint objectives.
Option C: While a lack of technical expertise or skills could potentially contribute to delays, it is less likely to be the primary reason for consistently missing the sprint goal. Agile teams are typically cross-functional, meaning they involve all skills and expertise needed to achieve project deliverables with no external dependency.
Option D: Changing requirements during the sprint can impact the team's ability to complete the sprint backlog items. However, according to the scenario, there are no changes, and the team has consistently struggled to complete the user stories of each sprint.

stem: A project manager is leading the implementation of a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system for a large e-commerce company. A detailed product roadmap is created, outlining the different features to be developed over the next year. As the team prepares to start working on implementing advanced customer segmentation algorithms, they are not sure what this feature's functionality is. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Perform value stream mapping.
options.B: Perform story mapping with the team.
options.C: Perform sprint planning with the team.
options.D: Create a use case for the feature.

explanation:
A story map is a visual model of all the features and functionality desired for a given product, created to give the project team a holistic view of what they are building and why (PMBOK 7th Edition, page 190). Story mapping directly addresses the team's uncertainty about the upcoming feature and facilitates the creation of achievable user stories. Therefore, it's the most suitable option for guiding the team in understanding and breaking down the feature.
Option A: Value stream mapping involves analyzing the end-to-end process of delivering value to the customer. While valuable for understanding the overall flow of value creation, it does not directly address the immediate need to understand the functionality of the upcoming feature and define user stories. Value stream mapping is more focused on process improvement rather than user story definition.
Option C: Sprint planning involves selecting and prioritizing user stories from the product backlog for implementation in the upcoming sprint. Therefore, it can’t be performed before clarifying the functionality of the upcoming feature and defining its user stories.
Option D: Creating a use case shows the scenario of interactions between the feature and the user. Use cases typically describe a normal flow as well as exception flows, where the scenario diverges from the normal flow. This technique does not address the team's described need.

stem: When reviewing the velocity chart, the project manager noticed that the team's velocity was inconsistent. While searching for the root cause, the project manager notices that one team member has a very slow performance compared to the other members, which is negatively impacting the whole team’s performance. How should the project manager address this issue?

options.A: Plan training sessionsfor the concerned team member
options.B: Acquire a more competent resource
options.C: Mentor the concerned team member
options.D: Reassign the concerned team member to another project

explanation:
When a team member’s performance is negatively impacting the overall progress of the project, the project manager should immediately interfere. Mentoring can help the team member enhance their performance. It’s among the project manager’s responsibilities to serve as a guide in identifying and assisting the team members with their learning needs to ensure better productivity and performance (PMBOK 7th edition, page 18). By offering enough support and attention, the team member will respond positively by working harder, which will naturally result in better performance. A mentor should however continue to observe the team member’s performance and provide feedback to help them refine and improve their work.
Option A: Since training the team member would take time, mentoring them would be a more suitable option for this urgent issue.

stem: An agile team is working on the project of an e-commerce website. After a slow start and a lot of disputes, team members are starting to get along and support each other’s needs. In which area of the Tuckman ladder does this team currently exist?

options.A: Area A
options.B: Area B
options.C: Area C
options.D: Area D

explanation: Getting over the storming stage (area B) means that the team has managed to resolve their conflicts and that a sense of unity is starting to shape. During the norming phase (area C), a sense of cohesion and unity emerges, a common consensus is developed, and personal differences start to diminish. Team performance is improved at this point as members get more goal-oriented (PMBOK 7th edition, page 166). However, if disagreements resurface, the team can slide back into the storming phase. Please note that on the real PMP exam, you may be asked to answer this type of question by clicking on the correct area in the image.

stem: A project manager has implemented a practice where team members take turns facilitating daily stand-up meetings to promote collaboration and ownership. Each team member is assigned a rotating role to facilitate the stand-up meeting for a designated period, typically one week. However, one team member consistently fails to properly facilitate stand-up meetings, acting flustered, failing to engage other team members, and doing most of the talking. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Assign the responsibility of facilitating stand-up meetings to another more reliable team member.
options.B: Provide immediate feedback at the end of each stand-up meeting so all team members can learn from their colleague’s mistakes.
options.C: Organize coaching sessions with the team member to discuss the importance of their role in facilitating stand-up meetings and provide guidance on how to improve.
options.D: Remove the team member from the project team as their failure to facilitate meetings is hindering progress.

explanation:
Organizing coaching sessions with the team member is the most appropriate course of action. Coaching allows the project manager to provide support, guidance, and feedback to help the team member overcome any hardships they’re having playing the role of a facilitator. Servant leaders should support the team through mentoring, encouragement, and support. Sometimes team members may not have knowledge or experience in roles or functions. Servant leaders who may have more exposure or training in techniques can support the team by providing training (Agile Practice Guide, page 37). The coaching session should focus on identifying any obstacles or challenges the team member is facing and collaboratively developing strategies to overcome them.
Option A: Assigning the responsibility of facilitating stand-up meetings to another team member does not address the root cause of the problem. It could also lead to resentment among team members and disrupt team dynamics.
Option B: Providing immediate feedback at the end of each stand-up meeting so all team members can learn from their colleague’s mistakes can create tension and negatively impact the team member’s morale.
Option D: Removing the team member from the project team is extreme for the described issue and could disrupt project continuity and negatively impact the team.

stem: During the sprint planning meeting, the product owner and the cross-functional team members agreed on which backlog items would be executed in the next sprint. Who commits to delivering a potentially shippable increment by the end of the sprint?

options.A: The cross-functional team
options.B: The scrum master
options.C: The product owner
options.D: The entire Scrum team

explanation:
When the sprint planning is complete, the cross-functional team members acknowledge their commitment to the business value that will be delivered by the end of the sprint. The sprint goal and the sprint backlog embody this commitment (Essential Scrum by Rubin, Kenneth S, page 346).
Option B: The scrum master helps in maintaining the scrum processes and intervenes neither in the selection nor the execution of the sprint backlog items.
Option C: The product owner doesn’t deliver business value by the end of the sprint but rather owns the product backlog; the product owner manages, maintains, and prioritizes the product backlog items. Keep in mind that the Product backlog represents work that needs to be done to create the entire product, while the Sprint backlog is a subset that represents the work that needs to be executed in the current sprint.

stem: A project manager has been assigned to an agile project that is already mid-execution. Which of the following should the project manager check to examine the high-level description of the project scope?

options.A: Project charter
options.B: User stories
options.C: Epics
options.D: Work breakdown structure

explanation:
The project manager should refer to the project charter to find the ‘high-level description‘ of the project. The project charter is a formal document that describes the project in its entirety, including its objectives, work processes, and stakeholders. This project planning document can be used throughout the whole project lifecycle (PMBOK 7th edition, page 184).
Options B & C: User stories and epics only represent the detailed requirements, not the entire high-level description of the project scope.
Option D: The Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) also outlines the detailed requirements of projects that follow a predictive approach.

stem: A project manager works in an organization that uses Agile practices. In order to evaluate the project performance, the project manager uses (Select two):

options.A: Cost performance index
options.B: Value-based measurements
options.C: Empirical measurements
options.D: Schedule performance index

explanation:
Agile favors empirical and value-based measurements instead of predictive measurements (Agile Practice Guide, page 61). Agile teams focus on measuring value and implementing an empirical process in which progress is based on observations of reality, facts, experiences, and evidence.
Options A & D: The Agile approach consists of a fixed cost and schedule, hence the project manager can’t use the Cost Performance Index (CPI) & the Schedule Performance Index (SPI) couldn’t be used.

stem: A project manager kicks off a software development project aimed at creating an e-commerce platform for a gluten-free snacks brand. During the third sprint of the project, the project team encountered unexpected technical complexities related to integrating third-party payment gateways and ensuring seamless user authentication processes. Despite their initial estimation efforts, the team realizes that they are unlikely to complete all the user stories within the sprint time frame. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Cancel the sprint to allow the team to regroup, address the challenges, and plan more effectively for future sprints.
options.B: Engage in additional product backlog refinement activities to ensure that the team focuses on delivering achievable work within the remaining sprint time.
options.C: Examine with the product owner the possibility of adjusting the sprint goal based on the team's current progress and capacity.
options.D: Collaborate with the product owner to re-negotiate the remaining items of the sprint backlog.

explanation:
During the sprint, the sprint backlog can be clarified and re-negotiated with the product owner as more is learned. This helps adjust sprint backlog items based on the team's capacity and constraints and ensures that the Sprint goals remain achievable while maximizing value delivery.
Option A: The only one who has the authority to cancel the sprint is the Product Owner. Even then, canceling the sprint is a drastic measure for the described situation.
Option B: The product backlog refinement helps optimize the backlog for future sprints. This doesn’t have any relation with the problem on hand; completing the planned work within the current sprint.
Option C: Changing the sprint goal mid-sprint can introduce confusion and disrupt the team's focus. Agile recommends maintaining a stable Sprint goal to provide clarity and direction to the team.

stem: After reviewing the sprint performance, the project manager is dissatisfied with the current progress and sees the need for adjustments. During a meeting with the team to discuss the matter, the project manager learned that some user stories were not accurately estimated due to missing key information during the sprint planning. How should the project manager address this problem?

options.A: Re-estimate all of the sprint's user stories
options.B: Re-estimate the velocity of the sprint
options.C: Do nothing and raise the problem in the sprint retrospective
options.D: Collaborate with the team to review the remaining user stories in the sprint backlog

explanation:
A team should ideally prepare all of the sprint user stories before it starts. However, this is not always the case for a number of reasons. Inaccurate estimations of user stories can result in unsatisfying progress and unfinished tasks in the Sprint Backlog. In this case, the project manager should collaborate with the team to review and complete the remaining Sprint issues. The project manager should first help the team identify the uncompleted user stories, document them, and determine the needed effort for completing them. In the second step, the project manager should involve the product owner in redefining priorities.
Option A: No need to re-estimate all the sprint's user stories. Since the sprint is in progress, the focus should be on the remaining user stories.
Option B: The velocity is calculated by the end of the sprint by summing the story points of the completed user stories. Therefore, it couldn’t be estimated during the sprint. Needless to say, the velocity won’t help in resolving the issue at hand.
Option C: When a problem happens it should be addressed instantly. In the sprint retrospective, the team should reflect on what happened to avoid this problem in the future.

stem: A project manager is leading a project that has recently been incorporated into a broader program aimed at enhancing the organization's digital infrastructure. The program manager is conducting a comprehensive review of the project's progress to ensure alignment with program objectives and timelines. During the review meeting, the program manager seeks updates on what has been completed in design, development, testing, and deployment. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Showcase the team’s Kanban board.
options.B: Showcase the team's burndown chart.
options.C: Showcase the team's cumulative flow diagram.
options.D: Showcase the team's velocity chart.

explanation:
The Cumulative Flow Diagram (CFD) indicates features completed over time, features in development, and those in the backlog. It may also include features at intermediate states, such as features designed but not yet constructed, those in quality assurance, or those in testing (PMBOK 7th Edition, page 188).
Option A: Showing the sprint Kanban board offers visibility into the current state of tasks within the sprint, including those in progress, completed, and pending. However, it may not provide a comprehensive overview of progress or state across multiple development phases.
Option B: Presenting the team's burndown chart provides a visual representation of the progress made towards completing the sprint goal over time. It depicts the remaining work against the projected timeline. Therefore, it may not fully address the program manager's specific inquiry about the completion status of work in various development stages.
Option D: The same goes for the velocity chart, which tracks the rate at which the deliverables are produced, validated, and accepted within a predefined interval and thus is not appropriate for addressing the program manager's request.

stem: For their new project, a project manager decided to create a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), define and sequence all activities, and then execute tasks in month-long cycles. The sponsor can change 30% of the subsequent cycle’s scope of work with no need for a change request. Which of the following approaches is being adopted?

options.A: Adaptive
options.B: Hybrid
options.C: Predictive
options.D: Iterative

explanation: A hybrid approach incorporates different components from various approaches (PMBOK 7th edition, page 36). In the described scenario, the project manager is combining the characteristics and practices of predictive (planning everything at the beginning of the project), iterative (executing work in cycles), and adaptive approaches (by allowing a 30% change without going through a formal process).

stem: Among the challenges that an organization faces when shifting to Agile, is the need to build teams made of “T-shaped” members. A “T” shaped team member is:

options.A: A generalist who is able to tackle any task within the backlog, regardless of the required skills.
options.B: A person who has freshly started their career and needs coaching by the scrum master.
options.C: An individual who specializes in a single field and rarely contributes to another field.
options.D: An individual who supplements their competence in one area with less-developed skills in associated areas and has an aptitude for collaboration.

explanation:
A “T” shaped team member typically has encompassing expertise in one field with supporting but less-developed skills in related areas. T-shaped people also have an aptitude for collaboration.
Option C: “I” shaped people have a profound specialization in one domain and only seldom participate in work outside of that domain (Agile Practice Guide, Page 42).

stem: A medium-sized IT company that has been using the predictive approach assigns an agile consultant to assist in their transition to the Agile approach. Which of the following aspects should the Agile consultant take into consideration when assisting in this transition?

options.A: The organization’s familiarity with the predictive approach
options.B: The organization’s culture
options.C: The existence of a Scrum master
options.D: The organization’s size

explanation:
An organization’s culture influences the type of project management approaches adopted by project teams.
Options A & D: The familiarity with the existing approaches, the size of the organization, and the competency of the team are all factors that contribute to the culture.

stem: A project manager works for a company that is undergoing a reorganization. During a staff meeting, the project manager learns that management has decided to shift technology to use the cloud. The project manager uses an Agile approach to lead the project and recognizes that this shift will directly impact the project. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Assess the impact of the shift with the sponsor before moving forward with the change management procedure.
options.B: Assess the impact of this shift with the team and refine the backlog.
options.C: Close the project and start over to properly adapt to the new technological transition.
options.D: Send a formal request to the sponsor asking for an exception from using the cloud.

explanation: Agile practices provide the ability to quickly adapt to new conditions. In this case, shifting to a new technology imposes assessing and refining the backlog with the team’s assistance.

stem: A project manager is assigned to a new agile project in the finance sector. The project team has identified several risks that could potentially impact project delivery. The product owner advises the team to utilize a risk-adjusted backlog to manage these risks effectively. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Ensure that at least one or two risk responses are added to each sprint.
options.B: Dedicate a sprint to deal with all identified risks.
options.C: Ensure that the risk register is always up-to-date.
options.D: Dedicate the sprint retrospective meetings to review the status of risks.

explanation:
A risk-adjusted backlog is a backlog that includes work and actions to address threats and opportunities (PMBOK 7th Edition, page 185). By incorporating at least one risk response into each sprint, the project team can actively address identified risks and work towards resolving them iteratively throughout the project lifecycle, allowing the project to adapt and respond effectively to changing circumstances.
Option B: The project team should not dedicate a whole sprint to deal with all identified risks, since in Agile, a sprint should demonstrate progress in the form of a product increment that potentially releases to production at the end of the sprint. Plus, dedicating a sprint to managing risks would be neither practical nor proactive.
Option C: Ensuring that the risk register is always up-to-date is not applicable in this scenario since it involves an agile project and not a predictive one. In Agile, risk management is done by adding related items to the product backlog. These work items are periodically refined, then prioritized and added to the sprint backlog.
Option D: The goal of the sprint retrospective is to identify and reflect on what went well and what didn’t during the sprint, and what could be improved. This can naturally result in identifying certain risks but that does not mean that this meeting should be dedicated to reviewing the status of the project risks.

stem: A project manager is using the Agile approach to manage a software development project. During a meeting with the team, the project manager presents the _____________ to showcase how much work still needs to be done during the current iteration.

options.A: Schedule
options.B: Burnup chart
options.C: Milestone chart
options.D: Burndown chart

explanation: Unlike the burnup chart which shows the completed work, a burndown chart is a graphical depiction of the work that still needs to be completed (PMBOK 7th edition, pages 108).

stem: Which of the below statements represents the most accurate definition of backlog refinement? (Select three)

options.A: The process of creating the initial list of product requirements, formerly known as backlog grooming.
options.B: When the product owner or team members review the backlog to make sure it has the proper items.
options.C: The continuous elaboration of project requirements to satisfy the stakeholders’ needs.
options.D: The continuous activity of writing, updating, and prioritizing requirements.

explanation:
Backlog refinement occurs when the product owner along with some, or all of the team members checks the backlog to make sure it contains the proper items, that these items are prioritized, and that the ones at the top are ready to be delivered (PMBOK 7th edition, page 235). This activity is carried out regularly and can be either an officially scheduled meeting or an ongoing activity.
Option A: The process of developing the initial list of product requirements represents backlog elaboration or creation.

stem: A project manager is leading an internal accounting software development project. During a sprint planning meeting, the project manager tackles a task that involves setting an automatic email as a reminder when an unpaid invoice misses its due date. The Agile team agrees to assign the task a total of 8 Story Points, based on the developers' estimate of 5 story points and the testers' estimate of 3 points. Which of the following statements is correct regarding this situation?

options.A: The project manager should be the one estimating the task, not the team.
options.B: The task should be estimated as a whole and not per segment.
options.C: Story points should never be estimated, they should be calculated.
options.D: The team should involve relevant stakeholders in the task estimate.

explanation: Story points are assigned to each user story to estimate the total effort needed to bring a feature or functionality to life. Thus, they shouldn’t be assigned partially. The team has to carefully consider how much work and effort each story requires in order to ensure that they can deliver the work they've committed to.

stem: A project manager is managing a two-year project that involves a high level of uncertainty and unforeseen complexity. The team expects adjustments as the scope of work gradually becomes more clear over time. To manage stakeholder expectations, what should the project manager clear up concerning their choice of using an iterative approach to manage the project?

options.A: That work will be subject to short feedback loops with the backlog being reprioritized in each iteration
options.B: That work will be developed progressively based on monthly feedback loops
options.C: That all tasks will be prioritized up front, and that work will be gradually decomposed
options.D: That the team will start executing the backlog work from the bottom up

explanation: Short feedback loops and backlog reprioritization are common in projects that use an iterative approach. Frequent delivery and feedback allow the team to prioritize work and respond to changes more efficiently. Option B: The duration of the iteration should be determined according to the project’s characteristics. For example, a monthly feedback loop could not be appropriate for a two-month-long project. Weekly or fortnightly feedback would be more convenient in this case.

stem: A project manager needs to choose the suitable project management approach for the project they’re leading. There are a variety of approaches to choose from, each ideally suited for a specific project type. Agile and Scrum are two of the most common and often conflated terms. Given their similarities, they can get confusing sometimes, but they are, in fact, two distinct concepts. What is the primary distinction between Scrum and Agile?

options.A: Agile is a set of values and principles, while Scrum only presents a set of values.
options.B: Agile is a set of values, principles, and practices, while Scrum only involves a set of values and principles.
options.C: Agile is a set of values and principles, while Scrum represents a set of values, principles, and practices.
options.D: Agile is a framework, while Scrum is a philosophy.

explanation: On the surface, Agile and Scrum look similar as they both rely on an iterative process, frequent client interaction, and collaborative decision-making. The primary distinction between Agile and Scrum is that Agile is a project management philosophy that utilizes a core set of values or principles, while Scrum is a specific Agile practice used to facilitate a project. Although Scrum is an approach within Agile, Agile does not necessarily imply Scrum since Agile encompasses a wide range of approaches. Scrum is based on a small set of core values, principles, and practices (collectively forming the Scrum framework). References: Agile Alliance & Essential Scrum by Rubin, Kenneth S (Preface).

stem: The traditional format of a daily stand-up meeting consists of gathering in a circle near a task board where each member takes their turn to answer a number of questions. Which of the following statements best describes the daily stand-up in agile?

options.A: It is a meeting during which the upcoming work schedule is discussed.
options.B: It is a meeting where the team discusses what they completed yesterday, their plans for today, and any challenges faced during task execution.
options.C: It is a daily brainstorming session.
options.D: It is a daily lessons-learned session.

explanation: The daily standup is a meeting held by members of the project team. This meeting brings the team together for a status update, to ensure that everyone is on the same page and has insight into what is going on, whether it’s good or bad. Such a meeting usually takes up to 15 minutes during which every team member is asked three questions: What did you do yesterday that helped your team meet the Sprint goal? What will you do today to help your team meet the Sprint goal? And, Did you face any impediments that prevented you or your team from meeting the Sprint goal? (PMBOK 7th edition, page 179)

stem: Agile is not fit for all projects, despite all the advantages it can bring forth. Therefore, it's important to understand the drawbacks of this approach. Which of the options below represent the disadvantages of the Agile approach? (Select three)

options.A: Poor resource planning
options.B: Limited documentation
options.C: Self-organized teams
options.D: Fragmented output

explanation:
Poor resource planning, limited documentation, and fragmented output are three key downsides of the agile approach. Since Agile is built on the fact that teams don't know what their final result will look like earlier in the project, it's difficult to anticipate project costs, time, and resources at the start, and this difficulty becomes more pronounced as projects become larger and more complex. Moreover, in Agile, documentation occurs during the project, and it is often done “just in time”, rather than at the beginning of the project. As a consequence, documentation becomes less informative. Additionally, while incremental delivery can help launch products faster, it's often regarded as one of the Agile approach’s major disadvantages: when teams work on each component at different time periods, the end result often becomes fragmented instead of being one coherent deliverable.
Option C: Agile teams are self-organizing which is proven to contribute to a higher velocity, increased quality, and less need for team management.

stem: The Sprint goals were not met by the Scrum team. A key team member took two days off at the start of the four-week Sprint due to a family emergency. What is the most likely reason for the team's failure to achieve the Sprint goals?

options.A: The project manager didn’t assign a replacement for the OOTO (Out Of The Office) member
options.B: The team is inexperienced
options.C: The team did not plan the sprint effectively
options.D: The team is overworked

explanation: When a team struggles to achieve the sprint goals, it’s mainly due to poor sprint planning. A team that fails to reach its sprint target is a team that can't properly plan its work, does not have a clear understanding of its own capabilities, or does not have a good sense of how to forecast stories and/or tasks. A team member’s two days off should not be an excuse for missing the sprint goals.

stem: An associate project manager is working for a digital design agency specializing in branding and packaging. In their current project, the project manager uses an approach that implies sharing partially completed work with the client in order to obtain early feedback and modify the product accordingly. The project manager is using a(n)____________ approach.

options.A: Incremental
options.B: Predictive
options.C: Agile
options.D: Iterative

explanation:
The iterative development approach focuses on developing the product through a series of repeated cycles that successively improve or add functionalities to the product by incorporating stakeholders’ feedback.
Option A: The iterative approach differs from the incremental approach in that change is expected. In fact, change is a necessary part of the iterative approach. (Source: Effective Project Management Traditional, Agile, Extreme, Hybrid by Robert K. Wysocki, page 49).
Option C: An adaptive or agile approach is also change-driven like the iterative approach. Yet, it requires ongoing stakeholder/client engagement and the use of backlogs (including product requirements and user stories) to reﬂect their current needs.

stem: A project manager depends on time-boxing to help team members avoid wasting time on shallow work and stay focused on the main deliverables. Which of the following statements best describes time-boxing?

options.A: Duration of intense activity within a specific release
options.B: A time frame for executing specific activities
options.C: Tight planning to reduce the time required for an activity completion
options.D: Setting a deadline for product delivery

explanation: A timebox is a fixed period of time in which work has to be completed. The timebox duration could be a few hours, days, or weeks depending on the work complexity or size (PMBOK 7th edition, page 181).

stem: A few days after introducing a new release to the market, the Product Owner received a complaint from a user, claiming that the product had an annoying defect. What should the Product Owner do next?

options.A: Create a task to fix the defect, add it to the product backlog, then prioritize it
options.B: Ask the development team to fix the defect immediately since the product is already released
options.C: Estimate the effort required to fix the defect, then decide what to do accordingly
options.D: Ask the development team to roll back the last release in order to work more on exploring undetected defects

explanation:
In Agile, any change request, whether to implement a new requirement or fix a defect, should be inserted in the Product Backlog and then prioritized by the Product Owner.
Option B: If the defect is critical, the Product Owner can prioritize it to be tackled in the upcoming sprint. The fact that the product is already on the market doesn't mean that discovered defects should be immediately fixed.
Option D: Additionally, going to an older version (i.e., rollback) is not a wise decision taking into consideration that only one defect was detected.
Option C: Finally, the product owner is not the one responsible for estimating efforts; it’s the responsibility of the development team.

stem: During the execution of a hybrid project, the team has completed several sprints, and the project manager needs to analyze the project's progress and forecast its future performance. The project manager uses different metrics and measurements to assess project and team performance. Match the following EVM metrics and Agile measurements with their corresponding formula or chart: Cost Performance Index (CPI) - Burndown Chart - Earned Value (EV) - Cumulative Flow Diagram (CFD)
explanation: Correct Answer A. Cumulative Flow Diagram (CFD) is an Agile measurement tool that visualizes work in progress (WIP). B. Burndown Chart visually represents the remaining work (in story points) over time. C. Earned Value (EV) is calculated by multiplying the percentage complete by the Budget at Completion (BAC): Actual % Complete x BAC D. Cost Performance Index (CPI) is calculated by dividing the earned value by the actual value: EV / AC

stem: A project manager gets assigned to carry out an internal project to create a new website for the organization. Months into the project, the project team faces multiple challenges; the completion date is unclear because the scope is changing frequently as new knowledge is gained. The team has completed some deliverables, however, when new stakeholders join the project, they express their dissatisfaction with the outcomes, claiming that they do not align with business goals. What can the project manager do to prevent similar issues in the future?

options.A: Develop a prioritized backlog and establish iteration review sessions with stakeholders to ensure alignment with business goals.
options.B: Create a detailed Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) and a milestone schedule that are approved by all stakeholders.
options.C: Implement daily meetings to review team performance and address impediments promptly.
options.D: Organize kick-off meetings for each project phase to share the project management plan with new stakeholders.

explanation:
Creating a prioritized backlog and holding iteration review sessions with stakeholders, i.e. adopting an agile project development approach, allows for continuous alignment with business goals. This enables the project team to adapt to evolving requirements and expectations, fostering stakeholder satisfaction and project success.
Option B: Developing a detailed Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) and milestone schedule suggests using a predictive approach, which is not adequate to address the challenge of evolving requirements.
Option C: While scheduling daily meetings can facilitate regular communication and issue resolution, it can’t resolve the described issues.
Option D: Organizing kick-off meetings for each project phase to share project management plans does not address these issues either.

stem: During an iteration review meeting, the product owner rejected one of the features demonstrated by the development team. What will happen next to the rejected user story?

options.A: It will be automatically moved to the next sprint backlog
options.B: It will be deleted from the product backlog and from the project
options.C: It will be updated to address the reasons why it was rejected
options.D: It will be moved back to the product backlog for reprioritization

explanation: The right step consists of understanding why the feature was not accepted in the first place, and then moving on to make the required updates. After that, the feature can be moved back to the backlog for reprioritization. Deleting the user story is not a rational choice since the feature has already been developed, which implies that it brings added value to the product.

stem: A project manager is assigned to manage a software development project. When they came across one of the project’s key stakeholders in the company’s hallway, the project manager seized the opportunity to get their feedback. The key stakeholder was impressed with the project’s progress and requested the project manager to urgently add a new user story to improve the product’s User Interface (UI). How should the project manager respond to this request?

options.A: Welcome the stakeholder’s request and add the user story to the sprint backlog.
options.B: Add the user story to the product backlog and schedule it for the next sprint to protect the team from disruptions.
options.C: Add the user story to the product backlog and let the product owner decide its priority.
options.D: Refuse to create the user story since it’s the product owner’s responsibility to maintain and refine the product backlog.

explanation:
The project manager should add the user story to the product backlog and let the product owner decide its priority.
Options A & B: When a new requirement is received, it should be added to the product backlog (not the sprint backlog) and then prioritized by the product owner in order to be implemented.
Option D: It is the responsibility of the product owner to maintain and refine the product backlog. This being said, a request can be made by any stakeholder and a user story can be created by anyone involved in the project and not just the product owner.

stem: A Scrum Master attends or facilitates the different Scrum events including the Sprint, Sprint planning, Daily standup, Sprint review, and Sprint retrospective. Which of the following options describes the sprint retrospective meeting?

options.A: A meeting for refining product backlog items
options.B: A meeting for discussing the negative and positive aspects of a sprint as well as any possible improvements
options.C: A meeting for defining and evaluating the work of the next sprint
options.D: A meeting held at the end of the project’s last sprint

explanation:
During the sprint retrospective meeting, all the good and bad aspects of the sprint are discussed. The retrospective meeting is considered a meeting for improvements, as it is mainly held to find the proper ways and means of identifying potential pitfalls and past errors, and to seek out new ways to avoid those mistakes. This meeting isn't held at the end of the project’s last sprint; it recurrently takes place after the Sprint Review and before the following Sprint Planning.
Option A: A backlog refinement meeting is used to refine product backlog items.
Option C: The sprint planning meeting is used to define and evaluate the work of the next sprint.

stem: A project manager is leading a project using an adaptive development approach. How should the project manager plan the project activities?

options.A: Plan all of the iterations work before the start of the project
options.B: Progressively elaborate the scope based on continuous feedback
options.C: Develop a high-level plan as the project progresses
options.D: Execute the project activities described in the Statement Of Work (SOW)

explanation:
Planning activities in an adaptive approach entails progressively elaborating the work scope based on the stakeholders’ continuous feedback. The project is split into iterations, and at the end of each iteration, the customer reviews the accomplished work on the product. Then, the customer’s feedback is used to define the detailed scope of the next iteration.
Option A: Defining all iterations’ work before the start of the project depicts an iterative development approach Option D: Implementing activities described in the statement of work depicts a predictive development approach.

stem: After discussing the matter with stakeholders, the project manager decided to go with a hybrid approach for the new project in order to take full advantage of both predictive and adaptive approaches. When the project manager documented and estimated all activities, one of the stakeholders complained that the project seemed to follow the predictive approach instead. What should the project manager do next to demonstrate that a hybrid approach is being followed?

options.A: Sequence activities
options.B: Develop schedule
options.C: Plan iterations
options.D: Estimate costs

explanation:
The project manager can demonstrate that they are following the hybrid approach by adopting iterative practices along with predictive methods.
Options A, B, D: These options represent processes within the predictive approach, therefore they will not demonstrate to the stakeholder that the project manager is following a hybrid approach.

stem: An organization selected a pilot project to experiment with the Agile approach. During the fourth sprint retrospective, the project team complained that many organizational processes were hindering their work progress, resulting in project delays and rework. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Start dedicating part of daily standup meetings to resolving impediments.
options.B: Conduct a root cause analysis in the following sprint retrospective.
options.C: Identify the organizational processes that are causing issues and work on removing, changing, or alleviating them.
options.D: Encourage the project team to be self-organizing by dealing with any problem that gets in their way.

explanation:
Transitioning to Agile does not mean that the approach with all its components will work for the organization, project, or team. Therefore, when issues with the new processes arise, the best practice would be customizing, tailoring, and adapting them to the team’s needs for optimum efficiency. This involves removing any processes that don’t seem to bring any value to the way the team is conducting work, changing to other more suitable processes, or altering the existing processes to fix any issues and make them more compatible with requirements.
Option A: Daily standups are meant for learning the current progress of each team member’s work as well as detecting impediments rather than dedicating part of the meeting to resolving them, which is neither convenient nor practical since the meeting duration is time-boxed to 15 minutes.
Option D: Besides, the impediments were already detected by the development team, which means that the project manager should work on removing them as their role entails, beyond the standup meetings.

stem: At the time of joining the organization, the scrum master was leading a team of 6 members. But, the number has doubled since then, making collaboration complicated. Plus, team members expressed their discontent with standups lately, as they tend to repetitively exceed their allotted time. What could the scrum master do to deal with this situation?

options.A: Be more vigilant to standups’ duration so they do not exceed 15 minutes.
options.B: Increase the standup meeting timebox to 20 minutes.
options.C: Split the team into two Scrum teams and apply the Scrum of Scrums technique to facilitate coordination between them.
options.D: Switch to a predictive approach since scrum is not suitable for teams counting more than 9 members.

explanation:
Scrum of Scrums (SoS), aka meta Scrum, is used to coordinate the work of two or more Scrum teams (Agile Practice Guide, page 111). The main aim of implementing the Scrum of Scrums approach is to create smaller, more coordinated independent teams. Since your team exceeds the maximum number of 9 team members per Scrum team, the logical alternative is to split the team in order to benefit from the efficiency of Scrum processes.
Option D: The consequences of increasing resources should not be tackled by switching to a predictive approach. Instead, Scrum can evolve to “Scrum of Scrums” or even “Scrum of Scrum of Scrums” in such a case.
Option A: Monitoring the standup duration will not fix the problem since a very large team naturally results in longer standup meetings.
Option B: Deciding to increase the meeting duration is not right either since it goes against Scrum principles.

stem: Drag the following terms to the right position in the Agile triangle of constraints below: Cost, Scope, Flexible, Fixed
correct: Unlike predictive approaches, projects that follow adaptive approaches have a fixed cost and
explanation: schedule, and flexible scope. A. Fixed, B. Flexible, C. Cost, and D. Scope.

stem: An organization is making a progressive transition from the predictive to the adaptive approach. What can the project manager do to prepare the team for the transition? (Select two)

options.A: Provide training for the team on agile values and practices.
options.B: Apply the “learning-by-doing” philosophy by immediately switching to agile approaches.
options.C: Plan a gradual transition by introducing a few iterative or incremental techniques to their current project.
options.D: Suggest a full transition since agile practices cannot be combined with predictive ones.

explanation:
The project manager should provide their team with relevant training in order to enable them to adopt the new agile practices with more confidence. They should also gradually introduce certain iterative or incremental techniques to make the transition smoother. This will improve the team learning process and accelerate delivering value to sponsors.
Options B & D: Many teams can’t make a full immediate switch to the agile approach. It is preferable and even recommended to make a gradual transition by combining adaptive and predictive practices, which is known as a hybrid approach (Agile Practice Guide, page 30).

stem: An organization intends to launch a project where team members are going to employ a pull system while aiming to limit work in progress.
