The pull system functions as follows: when a work item is done, it triggers a pull to bring in the next item on the to-do list. Which Agile framework does this describe?

options.A: Scrum
options.B: Kanban
options.C: Pull
options.D: Lean

explanation:
Kanban is a workflow project management approach that uses a board to display and manage work items in columns, e.g., To do, In progress, Testing, and Done. Kanban is built around four key principles: Visualizing workflow, Limiting work in progress (WIP), Focusing on flow, and Continuous improvement.
Option A: Scrum doesn’t rely on a pull work system, it relies on sprints to execute a selection of predetermined work items.
Option D: Lean is not an Agile Framework, it’s rather a philosophy that promotes removing waste within work processes.
Option C: Pull is a made-up term. Question 67 A project manager was assigned to a large project that had unclear requirements and deliverables. To deal with the situation, the project manager opted for an agile approach. What should the project manager do next? A. Acquire an agile coach to clarify the project scope. B. Facilitate the identification and prioritization of current work items, then ensure their execution in an iterative and incremental way. C. Set up a cross-functional team to help define all the needed iterations for completing the project. D. Have a meeting with the product owner or sponsor to discuss project baselines.

stem: A project manager was assigned to a large project that had unclear requirements and deliverables. To deal with the situation, the project manager opted for an agile approach. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Acquire an agile coach to clarify the project scope.
options.B: Facilitate the identification and prioritization of current work items, then ensure their execution in an iterative and incremental way.
options.C: Set up a cross-functional team to help define all the needed iterations for completing the project.
options.D: Have a meeting with the product owner or sponsor to discuss project baselines.

stem: Drag four of the following concepts and approaches to their right positions: Agile, Predictive, Hybrid, Scrum, Lean, Kanban.
correct: A. Lean: a set of concepts that includes eliminating waste, amplifying learning, and delivering as fast
explanation: as possible. B. Kanban: a subset of lean which also refers to a framework within agile. C. Agile: a subset of lean and an umbrella for several frameworks. D. Scrum: one of the agile frameworks.

stem: In a meeting with the product owner, the agile project manager has been informed that many other functionalities should be added to the product, without the possibility of extending the project’s deadline. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Use the smoothing technique and allude that delays are possible in such cases.
options.B: Inform the product owner that lower-priority work items will have to be dropped from the project.
options.C: Create a separate backlog for the new functionalities and work on it when time allows.
options.D: Inform the product owner that the new functionalities should be first authorized through an official change request.

explanation:
The agile project manager should inform the product owner that, consequently, they have to drop lower-priority work items from the project. Unlike the predictive approach, agile projects do not require formal change requests to change the scope. However, when new functionalities with higher priority are added, lower-priority functionalities might have to be dropped in case the project timeframe can’t be extended.
Option A: The project manager should not have a pretext for delays. Plus, they should discuss what’s in their mind directly with the product owner without any implicit hints.
Options C & D: It’s not appropriate to have two backlogs. The new requirements should be prioritized within the existing backlog. The new functionalities’ priority is high, thus they should not be tackled “when time allows”.

stem: An organization assigned a Product Owner to a new agile project and asked them to work on creating value and generating Return on Investment (ROI) as early as possible. How can the product owner achieve the organization’s demands?

options.A: Share these priorities with the project team
options.B: Support and serve the project team
options.C: Prioritize product backlog items
options.D: Improve work processes

explanation:
In order to get the most value as early as possible, the product owner should focus on prioritizing product backlog items.
Option A: Sharing the organization’s priorities with the project team is important to help them understand the product owner’s choices.
Option B: Still, the product owner is the one responsible for the product, not the project team.
Option D: Improving work processes and supporting and serving the project team is the main focus of the scrum master rather than the product owner.

stem: A product owner started the day with a sprint planning meeting to discuss and define the goal and backlog of the new sprint. Which of the following options is correct regarding the sprint planning meeting?

options.A: A discussion between the product owner, the scrum master, and the cross-functional team
options.B: A discussion between the cross-functional team members only
options.C: A discussion between the product owner and the scrum master
options.D: A discussion between the scrum master and the cross-functional team members

explanation: In the Scrum framework, the sprint planning meeting should include the scrum master, product owner, and the cross-functional team. When needed, other stakeholders can be invited to attend this meeting. During the sprint planning meeting, the product owner identifies the features with the highest priority. The team asks questions to get the necessary understanding to be able to turn high-level user stories into more detailed tasks.

stem: A project manager is leading an iterative project. The product owner calls for a meeting with the project team and other prominent stakeholders to review a demonstration of the produced deliverable. When should the project manager organize this meeting?

options.A: At the beginning of every iteration
options.B: At the end of every iteration
options.C: At the end of the project
options.D: At the start of the project

explanation: Iteration review meetings take place at the end of each iteration to allow the project team to obtain feedback from the product owner and concerned stakeholders on a regular basis.

stem: A project manager has been leading an Agile project for the last 9 months. When should the project manager stop tailoring the process?

options.A: When the Product Owner decides
options.B: When the Project Manager decides
options.C: When the cross-functional team members decide
options.D: The tailoring process should never be stopped

explanation: A project manager who truly understands Agile knows that tailoring its processes is a continuous task. Projects are undertaken to create a unique service, product, or result which means that every project is unique. This is where process tailoring steps in. Process tailoring addresses the fact that project management processes are not “one size fits all”. Every project has its own process needs and based on that, the project team needs to conduct the needed adjustments to their processes. This can include adding, removing, or revising processes.

stem: A project manager is assigned to an industrial project. The project team encounters a technical issue with a critical component of the system. Despite troubleshooting efforts, the root cause remains elusive, and the team risks missing the iteration goal. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Escalate the issue to senior management for immediate intervention.
options.B: Allocate additional resources to the problem area to expedite its resolution.
options.C: Implement a spike to conduct focused research and experimentation to identify the root cause.
options.D: Continue working on the iteration after adjusting its goal to accommodate the delay.

explanation:
A spike is a time-boxed activity used in Agile projects to investigate and address technical uncertainties or challenges. In this scenario, implementing a spike would allow the team to allocate dedicated time and resources to conduct focused research and experimentation to identify the root cause of the technical issue. This approach allows a systematic and structured problem-solving process, helping to mitigate risks and ensure timely resolution without compromising the iteration.
Option A: Escalating the issue to senior management should be warranted for severe issues that require the intervention of a higher authority or if the project manager has exhausted all available solutions, which is not the case. In the context of a technical issue, the immediate senior management intervention is neither necessary nor productive.
Option B: While allocating additional resources may seem like a proactive approach to accelerate problem resolution, it may not address the underlying issue effectively; Adding more resources without a clear understanding of the problem's root cause could lead to inefficiency or misallocation of resources. It may also result in increased costs without guaranteeing a faster resolution.
Option D: Adjusting the iteration goal does not address the root cause of the problem. Continuing work on the iteration without resolving the technical issue may lead to further complications or quality issues down the line.

stem: An Agile project manager is leading a software project using the Scrum framework. While the team implements user stories during the sprint, what should the product owner do?

options.A: Add more tasks for the team so they can deliver more value.
options.B: Let the team do their work and respond to any questions they might have.
options.C: Protect the team from interruptions and facilitate discussions.
options.D: Monitor the sprint progress and extend its duration if the team cannot complete the assigned work on time.

explanation:
The product owner should let the team do their work and answer any questions they might have during the sprint.
Option A: The product owner should not add more tasks.
Option C: Facilitating and protecting the team from interruptions are among the scrum master’s responsibilities.
Option D: The sprint duration is determined at the beginning of the project and typically does not change. Furthermore, any work items that cannot be completed by the team during the sprint should be put back in the backlog and rescheduled for the upcoming sprints.

stem: A project manager is in charge of a software development project. Their organization primarily uses agile methods. An intern who joined the project team once asked the project manager: “What is a User Story?” How should the project manager reply?

options.A: A story that refers to the ideal user for your project
options.B: A day in the end-user life
options.C: A small, granular unit of work that brings added value to the customer
options.D: A collection of all the requirements that the customer wants in a project

explanation: A user story is a brief description of deliverable value for a specific user (PMBOK 7th edition, page 192). A user story is not a narrative story about users; it is a small, granular work unit.

stem: A project manager is assigned to an internal project to develop Human Resource management software. During sprint planning, one of the team members insists that a user story concerning the implementation of a rewards policy should not be brought into the next sprint because it doesn’t include enough details on how to set rewards according to the different positions and roles of the organization employees. What is the most likely reason for the team member to push out this user story?

options.A: The user story doesn’t meet the Definition of Ready
options.B: The user story doesn’t meet the Definition of Done
options.C: The user story involves an unachievable stakeholder requirement
options.D: The user story might result in a waste of time and effort

explanation: The team member tried to push out the user story because it doesn’t meet the Definition of Ready (DoR); the user story is not ready for implementation as it does not describe how to define rewards according to each employee’s role or position within the organization. The Definition of Ready (DoR) represents a checklist of all the criteria that must be met before a user story can be considered ready to be included in the sprint for execution (Agile Practice Guide, page 151).

stem: A project manager is leading a project using an iterative development approach. During which meeting is a potentially shippable product increment presented to the concerned stakeholders?

options.A: Iteration kickoff meeting
options.B: Iteration planning meeting
options.C: Iteration review meeting
options.D: Iteration retrospective meeting

explanation: The project team is expected to deliver shippable product features by the end of each iteration. During the Iteration Review meeting, the project team demonstrates their work to the product owner and concerned stakeholders, in order to get feedback and approval (PMBOK 7th edition, page 179).

stem: During a meeting with stakeholders, the project manager is asked about the amount of work completed by the agile team during the last sprint. What information should the project manager share with stakeholders?

options.A: The sprint velocity
options.B: The sprint backlog items
options.C: The average velocity
options.D: The forecasting velocity

explanation:
Velocity is the measurement of how much work is completed in each sprint. It is calculated by adding up the sizes of the completed items by the end of the sprint (Essential Scrum by Rubin, Kenneth S, page 119).
Option B: The sprint backlog is a list of product backlog items pulled into a sprint, which may not be completed by the end of the sprint.
Option C: Average velocity represents the average velocity of all the previous sprints.
Option D: The forecasting velocity is used when the team is new to the Agile approach and has no historical data.

stem: An agile team is demonstrating a recently developed product increment. Among the deliverables is the product’s logo. After explaining the meaning behind their choice for the different elements of the logo, the senior graphic designer solicited feedback. The product owner appreciated the logo, while the majority of the cross-functional team noted that the logo icon would look better if it was 20% bigger. However, the Scrum Master thinks that a 10% size increase would be enough to make the logo look better. Which of the following decisions should be ultimately considered?

options.A: The icon size should be increased by 20% as per the recommendation of the majority of the cross-functional team.
options.B: The icon size should be increased by 10% as per the recommendation of the Scrum master.
options.C: The icon size should not be increased since the product owner was pleased with the result.
options.D: The icon size should not be increased since the senior graphic designer is the one qualified to make decisions when it comes to design.

explanation:
The product owner is the one responsible for accepting or rejecting the demonstrated product increment during the iteration review meeting. This means that the icon size should not be increased.
Options A & B: The icon size should not be increased since the product owner didn’t ask for any modifications.
Option D: The cross-functional team, including the senior graphic designer, as well as the scrum master, does not have the authority to decide whether a product increment or feature is complete or requires further development.

stem: After sizing the selected product backlog items for the next release, the product owner estimated that 5 sprints are needed to complete the release. However, after two sprints, the project manager finds out that the velocity of the team has declined for various reasons, which means that the release deadline won’t be met. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Re-prioritize the backlog
options.B: Add more members to the team
options.C: Decompose user stories to increase the velocity of the team
options.D: Discuss the issue with the product owner to find the appropriate solution

explanation:
The project manager should inform the product owner and discuss with them the different options and measures. If the release date cannot be changed then the product owner could re-prioritize the release backlog.
Option A: The agile project manager should not reprioritize the backlog. It’s the product owner's responsibility.
Option B: Adding more members or developers to the team may increase the velocity, but it will increase costs as well. Plus, this option should be approved by the product owner, and could only be adopted when meeting the release deadline and finishing its scope are more important than costs.
Option C: Decomposing user stories cannot result in more productivity nor increase the team’s velocity since the amount of work will still be the same.

stem: A project manager is assigned to a new agile project for developing a mobile app for finding parking spaces. The project team is working on implementing the outlined requirements. However, the project sponsor frequently intervenes with new demands and changes. The sponsor's requests often come directly to individual team members, continuously disrupting the team's workflow. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Talk to the project sponsor and request that all project requirements be communicated in writing to protect the team from disruptions.
options.B: Encourage team members to focus solely on the outlined requirements to maintain productivity and minimize distractions.
options.C: Ask the product owner to collaborate with the project sponsor to prioritize and incorporate his new requirements into the project.
options.D: Assign the responsibility of managing the sponsor's demands to a dedicated team member to avoid distracting the whole team.

explanation:
Asking the product owner to collaborate with the project sponsor to prioritize and incorporate their new requirements into the project ensures alignment with the project objectives and minimizes disruptions to the team's workflow. This way the sponsor's requests are properly prioritized and incorporated in a structured manner, ensuring that any new requirements align with the project's objectives and overall vision.
Option A: Directly confronting the sponsor may create tension and strain the relationship between the project manager and sponsor. Additionally, this may lead to resistance or pushback from the sponsor and is unlikely to resolve the issue effectively.
Option B: Encouraging team members to focus solely on the outlined requirements suggests ignoring the sponsor's requests, which is wrong taking into consideration that the agile approach promotes welcoming change. Additionally, disregarding the sponsor's input may result in missed opportunities or valuable insights that could benefit the project.
Option D: Assigning the responsibility of managing the sponsor's demands to a dedicated project coordinator is not the appropriate course of action since this is the core responsibility and role of the product owner.

stem: During a meeting with the sponsor, the project manager is asked how much work is left and whether the team will be able to finish the project on time. Which of the following point-in-time measurements can the project manager use to answer the sponsor’s inquiries? (Select two)

options.A: Product backlog
options.B: Feature burnup chart
options.C: Sprint burndown chart
options.D: Lead time

explanation:
Feature burnup and burndown charts, lead time, and cycle time provide in-the-moment measurements, giving insight into the team’s capacity and the schedule’s predictability. Lead time is the duration between task creation and task completion. Cycle time, however, is the duration between the moment the team starts working on a user story and the moment it gets delivered to the end user.
Option A: The product backlog is not a measurement, it’s rather a list of the work that needs to be done to develop the final product.
Option C: The Sprint burndown chart shows progress on the sprint level, not the project level.

stem: When the sprint is almost over, one of the team members informs the project manager that they don't have enough time to properly prepare the demonstration for the sprint review since they’re trying to complete the sprint backlog items. What could the project manager suggest in order to avoid such an issue in future sprints?

options.A: Creating a task for conducting the demonstration
options.B: Handling the demonstration instead of the team member
options.C: Delivering the demonstration without any preparation
options.D: Delaying the demonstration for a few days to allow the team to get properly prepared

explanation: The creation of a task for the product demonstration and making it part of the sprint allows the team to dedicate the needed time to properly prepare for the demonstration. However, you should keep in mind that the sprint demo shouldn’t take up too much of the team’s time. Time shouldn’t be spent putting long slide decks together, for instance. Team members should focus on their work and only include stories that meet the team’s Definition of Done in the demonstration. Typically, a day or two before the end of the sprint, the project manager should hold a short demo run-through to give their notes on the things the team needs to set up in order to properly perform the demonstration.

stem: A project manager opts for planning poker to estimate user stories. After going through the details of the first user story, the project manager asks team members to choose a card to represent their estimation of the ideal number of days required to complete the user story and then to reveal their cards. The estimates were vastly disparate, so the project manager instantly asked team members to re-estimate the user story in an attempt to converge their estimations. What did the project manager do wrong?

options.A: The team used ideal days to estimate the user story
options.B: The team re-estimated the user story immediately after revealing their cards
options.C: Cards shouldn’t be revealed
options.D: The project manager shouldn’t waste time with multiple rounds of estimates

explanation: Team members missed out on the benefit of discussing the reasoning behind their estimations when they immediately moved on to re-estimation. Often, estimates vary in the first round of planning poker. The team should discuss the story and each one's estimates. After the discussion, each team member should re-estimate the story again by selecting a card. The process should be repeated until reaching a consensus. The number of estimation rounds may vary from one user story to another.

stem: A PMO is in the process of transitioning to an Agile work approach. The team has shown high resistance to the changes since they are unaccustomed to adaptive approaches. What can the PMO leaders do to encourage adoption?

options.A: Forge ahead and provide point-in-time training on the new methods
options.B: Train project managers on the adaptive approaches to help convince the team
options.C: Stick to the predictive approach to avoid any conflicts
options.D: Use a hybrid method that combines both adaptive and predictive practices

explanation: Transitioning a team to Agile could be difficult and confusing when they are not accustomed to or familiar with this approach. One of the most effective transition methods is the adoption of a hybrid approach that combines both predictive and adaptive methods as a means of introducing Agile to the team.

stem: During a sprint planning meeting for a two-week sprint, the product owner shared a list of prioritized user stories. The development team estimated each story, and the total came to 45 story points. The project manager was surprised because the team's average velocity was only 30 story points. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Request from the team to decompose the user stories into tasks, then re-estimate the user stories.
options.B: Add all user stories to the sprint and request the team to complete as many user stories as they can.
options.C: Request from the product owner to postpone the execution of some user stories to future sprints.
options.D: Suggest changing the duration of the sprint to three weeks.

explanation:
Agile emphasizes sustainable pace and realistic planning. Given that the team's capacity is typically around 30 points, it’s important to limit the scope of work to something achievable within the sprint. By postponing some stories, the team can work at a sustainable pace while maintaining the focus on completing valuable work.
Option A: Decomposing and re-estimating might not change the fact that the overall scope is too large for the team’s velocity.
Option B: Trying to add more work than the team can handle (even with a request to "complete as much as they can") will lead to incomplete work and decreased team morale.
Option D: Changing the sprint duration goes against Agile principles, as sprint lengths should be consistent to maintain a steady cadence of work and avoid disrupting the team's rhythm.

stem: A project manager is leading a project using an adaptive approach. The product owner and the project team are currently preparing and updating user stories for the next iterations. What activity does this depict?

options.A: Backlog refinement
options.B: Schedule management
options.C: Project management
options.D: Sprint Review

explanation: Backlog refinement involves preparing the next iteration’s stories. In order to make sure the backlog contains the right items for the next iteration, the product owner, along with the team, should review and prioritize backlog items, ensuring that top items are ready to be delivered (PMBOK 7th edition, page 235). This activity can take place as a formal planned meeting or as a regular ongoing task.

stem: A project manager is using an Agile approach to manage a web application project. During the daily standup, two team members start discussing which JavaScript framework to use: Angular, React, or Vue. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Let the discussion continue since it’s very important
options.B: Time-box the conversation and suggest that team members carry on with this subject after the standup meeting
options.C: Facilitate the conversation and invite the rest of the team to weigh in
options.D: Contribute to the discussion and share his own opinion on the matter

explanation: The daily scrum is not an event for problem-solving activities. However, the team can address any problem after the standup meeting with a small group of interested members (Essential Scrum by Rubin, Kenneth S, page 24). For the daily standup to be effective, the Scrum Master or the project manager must keep the attendees' attention on the core agenda and time-box any side conversations that can always be carried out later, after the daily standup.

stem: A product owner asks a team member to help create a report that will be shared with the project sponsor. The report is not related to the product and is not part of the product backlog. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Request from the product owner to add the report work to the sprint backlog so the team member can work on it.
options.B: Protect the team by informing them that the report work shouldn’t be added to the current sprint, instead, it should be prioritized for future sprints.
options.C: Inform the product owner that only product-related work should be included in the product backlog.
options.D: Do not intervene and allow the team member to collaborate directly with the product owner on the report.

explanation:
Since the report is not related to the product, it should not be part of the product backlog or the sprint backlog. The project manager should protect the team from disruptions and ensure that they stay focused on delivering the potentially shippable increment at the end of the sprint.
Option A: Adding non-product work to the sprint backlog would reduce the team's capacity to complete their planned product-related tasks. It can also lead to a loss of focus on the sprint goal, which could hurt the overall progress of the product.
Option B: Adding the report to the product backlog is a misuse of the backlog, as the work is unrelated to the product.
Option D: Not intervening means allowing non-product work to creep into the sprint, which will negatively impact the team's progress on the sprint.

stem: A project team has developed the initial schedule using a network diagramming method and has arrived at the overall project duration. Upon examining the schedule, the project manager finds that the duration of several activities requires adjustment to address potential resource constraints. Match the following common resource issues with their explanations:
explanation: Correct Answer ● Dropped Baton: An activity is not ready to start and the preceding activity finishes early, resulting in lost time between activities. ● Student Syndrome: Procrastination in starting activities can use up valuable slack built into the activity duration. ● Self-protection: Workers are reluctant to finish tasks early so as not to communicate their efficiency and set precedents for future tasks. ● Parkinson’s Law: Workers use all the time allocated for an activity regardless of how long it actually takes to complete the task. ● Sandbagging: Workers intentionally underestimate or lower expectations to produce relatively greater-than-anticipated results.

stem: In an interior design project for a library, the client asks the project team to increase the number of bookshelves beyond what was agreed on. Since the project is on schedule and adding additional shelves will not cause any delay, the project manager consents to the client’s request. This is an example of:

options.A: Gold Plating
options.B: Customer Obsession
options.C: Scope Creep
options.D: Successful Project

explanation:
Scope creep (also known as “feature creep” or “requirement creep”) refers to the uncontrolled expansion of the project’s scope (PMBOK 7th edition, page 249). The project manager should assess the change request from all perspectives, not only from a schedule perspective, and follow the change control process to implement the change.
Option A: The tackled situation is not considered gold plating since the client is the one who brought up the change request; it was neither the project manager nor team members who added changes without the client’s approval, as gold plating implies.
Option B: Customer obsession consists of an excessive focus on providing a better customer experience by meeting and even exceeding your client’s needs. However, customer obsession shouldn’t mean delivering beyond scope since the latter can increase the project schedule and cost, thus decreasing the success rate of the project.

stem: A project manager is managing a software development project which was planned to last three months. Throughout the entire project, progress aligned with the planned schedule. However, one day before the delivery deadline, a team member discovered a bug that could cause a one-week delay. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Inform the stakeholders that there is a bug that requires 2 to 3 days to fix and put more pressure on the team to fix it within that time frame.
options.B: Inform the stakeholders about the situation and that it may take a week to resolve the bug.
options.C: Update the lessons learned and add them to the organizational process assets.
options.D: Close the project since the project end date is reached.

explanation:
As soon as it becomes obvious that the project will be delayed, the project manager should notify the client and present them with new alternatives. The project manager should be honest and transparent about delays. Under the RESPONSIBILITY section of the PMI's Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct, page 3: When the project manager discovers errors or omissions caused by others, they should communicate them to the appropriate body as soon as they are discovered. Under the HONESTY section, page 6: the project manager should provide accurate information in a timely manner.
Option D: The situation describes a predictive project since we have a planned schedule. Therefore, the project should fulfill its entire scope before closing it.

stem: Shortly after starting the second phase of the project, the project manager meets with the sponsor to check if any potential players were left out in the first phase and to discuss these new stakeholders’ influence. What activity is the project manager doing with the sponsor?

options.A: Planning stakeholder engagement
options.B: Identifying stakeholders
options.C: Planning resource management
options.D: Identifying risks

explanation: The project manager is identifying stakeholders and analyzing their level of influence. Although the project has been active for two months, it is recommended to perform this activity on a regular basis, especially when the project gets into a new phase.

stem: A project manager is leading a project to implement a new Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system for a local customer. The project manager guides the team to define the project requirements in detail before moving to execution. The project will be delivered after 4 months, but the customer will pay the organization in monthly installments. Which of the following project development approaches is the project manager adopting?

options.A: Predictive
options.B: Adaptive
options.C: Iterative
options.D: Incremental

explanation:
Since requirements are fixed and deliverables will only be shipped at the end of the project, then the project manager is using a predictive approach.
Options B & D: Adaptive and incremental approaches involve frequent small deliveries. In the described scenario, payment installments are not linked to deliverables or iterations; it’s just a payment option that has no influence or connection to the project development approach.
Option C: The iterative approach is characterized by a single delivery (Agile Practice Guide, page 18), but it has dynamic requirements.

stem: A project manager is assigned to a 12-month project that has a $100,000 budget. Six months have passed and $60,000 has been spent. On closer inspection, the project manager finds out that so far, only 40% of the work has been completed. The value of the completed 40% work is referred to as:

options.A: Planned value
options.B: Earned value
options.C: Actual cost
options.D: Cost variance

explanation:
Earned Value refers to the value of the work accomplished to date (PMBOK 7th edition, page 239). If the project gets terminated at this point, Earned Value will show you the value that the project has produced. In this case, the project’s Earned Value (EV) is $40,000 = 40% of the value of total work.
Option A: The planned value is $50,000 (50% of the budget).
Option C: The amount of $60,000 represents the Actual Cost (AC).
Option D: The cost variance is -$20,000 (EV - AC).

stem: A project manager is carrying out the initial planning activities for a gas pipeline construction project. When estimating the activity of installing 1000 meters of pipes, one team member states that they ran the same length of pipes in 14 hours on a previous similar project. Another team member claims that, according to the current project conditions, it’s possible to run 100 meters of gas pipes per hour. Using the analogous estimating technique, how many hours will it take the team to run the gas pipeline?

options.A: 10 hours
options.B: 11 hours
options.C: 12 hours
options.D: 14 hours

explanation: Unlike parametric estimating, the analogous estimating technique uses expert judgment by comparing a particular activity to a similarly completed one on a previous project in order to determine its duration or cost. This means that the project manager should rely on expert feedback, i.e., completing a similar task in 14 hours.

stem: During project execution, a team member reaches out to the project manager to inquire about the work needed to be accomplished in this phase of the project. Which of these documents comprises thorough descriptions of work packages?

options.A: WBS
options.B: WBS Dictionary
options.C: Activity List
options.D: Scope management plan

explanation: The planned work is included in the lowest level of the WBS components, known as work packages. Detailed information on work packages, such as descriptions, owners, prerequisites, successors, due dates, etc. is included in the Work Breakdown Structure Dictionary (PMBOK 7th edition, page 253).

stem: An activity has an Early Start (ES) of day 5, a Late Start (LS) of day 12, an Early Finish (EF) of day 10, and a Late Finish (LF) of day 17. Which of the following statements are correct regarding this activity? (Select two)

options.A: The activity is on the critical path
options.B: The activity is not on the critical path
options.C: The activity has a float
options.D: The activity has a lag

explanation:
Since it has a 7-day float, this activity is not on the critical path. The float of this activity can be calculated by subtracting the Early Start (day 5) from the Late Start (day 12) or by subtracting the Early Finish (day 10) from the Late Finish (day 17). Since the float of the activity is greater than zero, then it’s not on the critical path. Remember that critical path activities have zero float.
Option D: Lag time is the amount of time whereby a successor activity is required to be delayed with respect to a predecessor activity. However, since the described scenario doesn’t have any information about the successor activity, it does not consist of a lag.

stem: A project manager is leading a construction project. Throughout its execution, the project was influenced by both Enterprise Environmental Factors (EEFs) and Organizational Process Assets (OPAs). Match the following statements with the corresponding influence category:
correct: A. Construction work requires a building permit from the City council: EEF
explanation: B. Workers who don’t obey safety rules will be penalized: OPA C. Only authorized personnel are allowed on site: OPA D. Workers have expertise in infrastructure construction: EEF

stem: A project manager is assigned to a new construction project to build a new office complex. During the planning phase, the project manager identifies a significant risk related to adverse weather conditions during construction. The project timeline is tight, and any delays due to weather could impact the overall project schedule and budget. To effectively manage this risk, the project manager must select the most appropriate risk response strategy. Match the risk response with the corresponding risk response strategy for the identified risk:
explanation: Accept: Acknowledge the risk of adverse weather conditions without opting for any proactive action. ● Mitigate: Revise the construction schedule to include buffers for potential weather-related delays. ● Escalate: Seek the approval of senior management for additional budget allocation or resources to implement contingency measures. ● Avoid: Implement alternative construction methods or materials that are less susceptible to weather impacts. ● Transfer: Purchase weather insurance coverage to protect against potential financial losses resulting from weather-related delays.

stem: In a process improvement project for a manufacturing company, a team member is assigned to create the project status report. However, the team member does not submit the project status report on time. When approached, the team member expressed his frustration, feeling that the report doesn't accurately reflect the project's reality, is excessively lengthy, and won't be thoroughly reviewed by stakeholders anyway. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Review the requirements of the report with the team member to redefine its purpose.
options.B: Instruct the team member to submit the report as requested and document this delay in the performance review.
options.C: Reassign the report to another team member to prepare and submit it as requested.
options.D: Notify the team member's functional manager that the report was not submitted as requested, seeking their intervention to address the issue.

explanation:
Reviewing the requirements of the report with the team member to redefine its purpose addresses the root cause of the team member's frustration; by collaborating with the team member to reassess the purpose and requirements of the report the project manager ensures it aligns with the project's needs and stakeholders' expectations and that it will better meet project needs.
Option B: Focusing on compliance and documentation of the team member's delay in their performance review does not address the underlying issue of dissatisfaction with the report's requirements. While documentation might be important for accountability, the focus should be on improving processes and addressing concerns.
Option C: Shifting the responsibility to another team member does not resolve the underlying issue and could lead to resentment and disengagement within the team if not handled sensitively.
Option D: Escalating the issue to the team member's functional manager may be an option in cases of repeated non-compliance. However, it should be considered as a last resort. Collaboration and problem-solving should be prioritized to address the root cause of the issue.

stem: For a construction project, concrete is poured after the completion of rebar and formwork. Now, workers must wait 14 days before removing the formwork, as the concrete must be strong enough for this operation. The 14-day period is an example of:

options.A: Lead
options.B: Lag
options.C: Free float
options.D: Cycle time

explanation:
Lag Time is when a delay is purposely made between activities.
Option A: Lead time is the time saved by starting an activity before its predecessor is completed.
Option C: Free Float is the amount of time that an activity can be delayed without delaying the Early Start date of its successor activity.
Option D: Cycle time is how long it takes the team to complete a task.

stem: A project task is 90% complete. It cannot, however, be finished until another task is completed. What type of dependency is this? (Select two)

options.A: Finish-to-start (FS)
options.B: Finish-to-finish (FF)
options.C: Mandatory dependency
options.D: Discretionary dependency

explanation:
This is an example of finish-to-finish mandatory dependency. Two tasks may in fact run concurrently in the case of a finish-to-finish dependency. However, the second task can be entirely completed only after the first task is 100% done.
Option C: Mandatory dependencies are those that are legally or contractually required or inherent in the nature of the work (PMBOK 7th edition, page 60).

stem: A project manager is leading a construction project of a shopping center. During the execution phase, the project manager received an approved change request from the client to modify the partition of the center. After checking the change request, the project manager realized that the budget allocated for its implementation might not be sufficient. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Discuss the budget for the change with the client
options.B: Implement the change since it’s already approved
options.C: Reject the change request due to its inadequate budget
options.D: Disregard the change request since the project follows a predictive approach

explanation:
The project manager must discuss the impact of the change request on the project cost with the client.
Option B: The project manager should not process the change request unless the client understands and accepts its impact. Usually, the project manager is part of the Change Control Board (CCB), which ensures the project manager’s review and awareness of the change request. However, in the described scenario, the project manager doesn’t seem to be part of the CCB since they were not aware of the change request until it was approved. Therefore, the project manager should analyze and validate the consequences of the change before implementing it.
Option C: The CCB, represented by the client in the described scenario, could amend the change request in the light of the Project Manager’s input.
Option D: Change in all projects is inevitable, including predictive projects. The project manager doesn’t have the authority to reject a change request; it’s up to the CCB to approve or reject change requests.

stem: A project manager is assigned to an industrial equipment manufacturing project for a major client. The project team successfully completes the assembly and installation of a complex machinery system. However, upon delivery, the client raised concerns, noting that the accompanying maintenance manual was not provided. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Review the contract terms and conditions to ascertain the agreed-upon obligations related to deliverables.
options.B: Initiate a formal change request process to include the missing maintenance manual as an essential deliverable in the project scope, addressing the client's concerns promptly.
options.C: Evaluate the effectiveness of the stakeholder engagement plan to determine if any gaps contributed to this misunderstanding.
options.D: Ask the team to immediately add the required maintenance manual and update the project issue log to monitor the resolution of this issue.

explanation:
Reviewing the contract terms and conditions to ascertain the scope and obligations related to deliverables should be the project manager’s first step. It’s important that the project manager refers to the contract to check the agreed-upon contractual obligations and requirements in order to address the client's concerns effectively. By reviewing the contract terms, the project manager can determine if the maintenance manual was indeed included in the scope of work and the appropriate course of action.
Option B: Initiating a formal change request process to include the maintenance manual as a deliverable should only be done after reviewing the contract and verifying that the maintenance manual is included in the scope of work.
Option C: Evaluating the effectiveness of the stakeholder engagement plan to determine if any gaps contributed to this misunderstanding is not the best course of action in this scenario as it does not address the immediate concern of the missing maintenance manual.
Option D: Asking the team to immediately add the required maintenance manual and update the project issue log does not address the client's concerns or ensure that the missing maintenance manual is included as an essential deliverable in the project scope.

stem: Team members have been allocated to a project with 50% availability. Two months into execution, the project manager discovered that the team had been spending less than 50% of their time working on the project. The project schedule is about to become heavily delayed, putting deadlines in jeopardy. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Discuss getting additional resources with the project sponsor
options.B: Negotiate clear and written assignments with reliable scheduling priorities with functional managers
options.C: Adjust the schedule and negotiate new deadlines due to unexpectedly slow work progress
options.D: Crash the project in order to complete it on time

explanation:
Since the project manager didn’t assign the team members himself, then the organization must be functional. In this case, it is best to talk with functional managers and negotiate clear and written assignments with reliable scheduling priorities.
Option A: It is the responsibility of functional managers, not the project sponsor, to manage staff assignments. The project manager, on the other hand, should provide a resource calendar to make sure that functional managers are aware of when and what resources he needs for his project.
Options C & D: Adjusting or crashing the schedule without tackling the source of the problem is not the right course of action. Besides, crashing the project requires adding more resources, which is beyond the project manager’s authority in a functional organization.

stem: A project manager wrapped up an intensive session with the project team, meticulously breaking down the project scope to ensure alignment with the customer's requirements. The project manager wants to maintain control over the project scope to ensure that any changes undergo the proper process. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Create a scope baseline and document it in the configuration management plan.
options.B: Create a change management plan to outline how changes will be managed.
options.C: Create a scope management plan incorporating strategies to minimize scope changes.
options.D: Create a resource assignment matrix to specify the roles authorized to approve scope changes.

explanation:
A baseline is the approved version of a work product or plan, where actual performance is compared to the baseline to identify variances. Baselined items are noted in the configuration management plan (PMBOK 7th Edition, page 188). The configuration management plan describes how the information about the items of the project (and which items) will be recorded and updated so that the product, service, or result of the project remains consistent and/or operative (PMBOK 6th Edition, page 116). It defines configurable items, items that require formal change control, and the process for controlling changes to such items.
Option B: While developing a change management plan is essential, it's not the immediate next step after breaking down the project scope. Instead, establishing a baseline for the project scope takes precedence to provide a stable foundation for managing scope changes effectively.
Option C: A scope management plan is created to provide guidance on how the scope will be defined, developed, monitored, controlled, and validated, and not to set strategies for minimizing scope changes. Strategies are defined to manage changes and not to limit them.
Option D: A Resource Assignment Matrix (RAM) shows the project resources assigned to each work package. It is used to illustrate the connections between work packages or activities, and project team members. It does not indicate individuals authorized to approve scope changes. Scope change requests are submitted to the Change Control Board (CCB) which is a formally chartered group responsible for reviewing, evaluating, approving, deferring, or rejecting changes to the project.

stem: A project manager is reviewing a change request that involves integrating a third-party system, which the project team has not previously worked with. However, team members stated that if the third-party system layout follows the international standard, its implementation will take no more than two months. What should the project manager do after the change request gets approved?

options.A: Check the impact of the change request on the project’s critical path.
options.B: Use parametric estimating to check the team’s estimate accuracy.
options.C: Hold a meeting with the project team to evaluate the adopted estimation approach.
options.D: Update the assumption log noting the basis of the two-month estimation.

explanation:
An assumption is a factor that is considered to be true, real, or certain, without proof or demonstration. An assumption log records all assumptions and constraints throughout the project (PMBOK 7th Edition, page 185). The appropriate next step for the project manager is to document the team’s assumption that the third-party system layout follows the international standard.
Option A: The analysis of the change request’s impact on the project schedule should have been done before submitting the change request.
Option B: Parametric estimating uses an algorithm to calculate cost or duration based on historical data which can’t be applied in this scenario since the team has not previously worked with this type of system, hence the lack of historical data.
Option C: Holding a meeting with the project team to evaluate the adopted estimation approach refers to conducting a retrospective meeting to go through what went well and what didn’t, which should not be the project manager’s first action after the change request approval.

stem: A project manager is in the phase of planning the redesign of a commercial building. The project team includes one carpenter who is only available to work part-time. Since the carpenter’s work is on the critical path, the project manager has to push back the project’s planned completion date to accommodate the carpenter’s availability. What technique did the project manager use?

options.A: Load Balancing
options.B: Resource Loading
options.C: Resource Leveling
options.D: Resource Smoothing

explanation:
Resource leveling is used to optimize resource allocation by adjusting the activities’ start and finish dates. This often results in changing the original critical path, as was the case in the described scenario; the carpenter is a scarce resource for the project and her availability is constrained, which led to extending the project schedule to manage this limitation.
Option A: Load balancing is common in computing and it refers to the process of distributing a set of tasks over a number of resources with the aim of speeding up the overall data processing.
Option B: Resource loading is the total assigned hours of work divided by the number of hours you have to do the work.
Option D: Resource smoothing is performed to achieve a more consistent resource utilization over a period of time.

stem: The following diagram represents the decomposition of the project deliverables into smaller tasks. What is this diagram called?

options.A: Affinity diagram
options.B: Product breakdown
options.C: Product roadmap
options.D: Work breakdown structure

explanation:
The WBS is a hierarchical decomposition of the total scope of work to create the required deliverables (PMBOK 7th edition, page 81). The planned work is included in the lowest level of the WBS components, which are called work packages.
Option B: Product breakdown is a product analysis technique (PMBOK 6th edition, page 153).
Option C: The product roadmap demonstrates the anticipated sequence of deliverables throughout the project duration.
Option A: Afﬁnity diagrams classify a large number of ideas into groups for analysis and review.

stem: A project manager is assigned to lead a project to construct a building extension within the organization. The project team has meticulously planned the project scope, schedule, and cost. The project is funded and about to start when an executive from another department asks the project manager to formally assist him in delivering a website as part of their rebranding project. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Explain to the executive that the website work is out of the project’s scope.
options.B: Review the impact of the new task on the project schedule and cost.
options.C: Ask the executive to submit a change request for the added scope.
options.D: Assign a team member to help the executive create the website.

explanation:
The construction of a building extension and the creation of a website are two different projects, therefore the project manager should explain to the executive that the website work is out of the construction project’s scope.
Options B, C, D: For the same reason, with or without a change request, the project manager should not incorporate the website into the current project's scope.

stem: A project manager has developed the project schedule using the network diagramming method and has calculated the overall project duration. However, the project manager was surprised to find three critical paths. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Approve the network diagram and closely monitor all three critical paths
options.B: Approve the network diagram and closely monitor the longest path among the three
options.C: Re-examine the network diagram since it’s supposed to only have one critical path
options.D: Re-examine the network diagram since it’s not supposed to have more than two critical paths

explanation:
The project manager should approve the network diagram and closely monitor all three critical paths.
Options C & D: Theoretically, there is no limit on how many critical paths a network diagram could have.
Option B: If a project has more than one critical path, then all critical paths must have exactly the same length.

stem: After completing the creation of the scope statement, a project manager wanted to make sure that all of the project deliverables were identified and could be managed effectively. So, the project manager opted for the ____________________ method to develop the WBS in order to capture all of the project’s details.

options.A: Scope decomposition
options.B: Bottom-up estimating
options.C: Rolling wave planning
options.D: Checklist analysis

explanation: Scope decomposition is a planning method used to decompose and subdivide the project and scope deliverables into more manageable, small work units. The decomposition level depends on the complexity and size of the project (PMBOK 7th edition, page 84).

stem: During the project execution phase, the Change Control Board (CCB) approved a change request that no one on the project team knew how to implement. What should the project manager do to deal with this issue? (Select two)

options.A: Document the issue in the issue log
options.B: Hire a subject matter expert
options.C: Formally request the CCB to revoke their decision
options.D: Ask the team to do more research on how to implement the approved change request

explanation:
Hiring a subject matter expert and conducting more research will help your team implement the change request. This is considered a problem-solving approach since it entails ﬁnding solutions to the encountered issues or challenges. Uncertainty can be reduced by collecting more information through conducting research, engaging experts, or performing a market analysis (PMBOK 7th edition, page 229).
Options A & C: Neither documenting the issue in the issue log nor asking the CCB to revoke their decision could help resolve the issue.

stem: A newly assigned interim project manager got a call from one of the project vendors claiming that they had already completed 50% of the agreed-upon work and asked for payment. What should the project manager consult to determine if payment is required for the vendor and how much to pay?

options.A: Request for Proposal (RFP)
options.B: Contract
options.C: Response to bid
options.D: Procurement management plan

explanation:
The contract is the document the project manager should refer to in order to verify the payment procedure. A contract is a mutually binding agreement that obligates the seller to provide the required services and the buyer to pay a predetermined amount on an agreed-upon date or schedule (PMBOK 7th edition, page 191).
Option C: The response to the bid might be different from the final agreement, ie., the contract, since it might have been followed up with negotiations.
Option D: The procurement management plan is a generic planning document; it defines the process and steps on how to conduct procurement.

stem: During a construction project, the construction team finds out that the designed model for the swimming pool requires some raw material that is no longer available in the local market. However, there is an alternative with the same price and probably a better quality. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Update the resource management plan to replace the old material with the new one.
options.B: Submit a change request in order to get formal approval for using the new material.
options.C: Order a sample of the new material and check its compliance with the quality management plan.
options.D: Use the new material right away since it has the same price and probably a better quality.

explanation:
The project manager should submit a change request to the Change Control Board (CCB) according to the procedures described in the change management plan.
Option A: In the case of using a new material, the resource management plan should be updated.
Option C: The CCB may decide to further investigate the new material, import the old material from another country, or even change the swimming pool design. If the CCB decides to further investigate the new material, then the project manager may need to order a sample.
Option D: The project manager should not use the new material unless the CCB approves the change request.

stem: After multiple negotiation sessions, all terms and details were agreed upon and the seller finally got the 18-month building project contract for $715,500. What type of contract is used in this scenario?

options.A: Time and Material
options.B: Fixed Price
options.C: Cost Reimbursable
options.D: Cost Plus Incentive

explanation:
Fixed price contracts are used for projects with clear requirements where a price is fixed in return for the seller’s services and/or products.
Option A: Time and Material (T&M) contracts set a quote for an hourly rate plus the cost of materials instead of quoting a fixed price for the entire project.
Option C: Cost-reimbursable contracts reimburse the contractor for the actual costs they incur to provide their services and/or product, plus an additional fee.
Option D: A Cost Plus Incentive contract, for instance, is a cost-reimbursable contract that incentivizes the contractor to bring their best performance by completing the project under budget or before deadlines.

stem: During the execution of a construction project, the supplier informed the project manager that delivering the new order of steel bars may have a 3-day delay. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Negotiate the delay with the vendor to get it reduced
options.B: Look for another vendor
options.C: Evaluate the impact of the delay
options.D: Update the project schedule

explanation:
The project manager should evaluate the impact of the delay before making any decision.
Options A, B, D: A delayed activity doesn’t necessarily result in the whole project delay. For instance, if the activity is not on the critical path and it has a lag of more than three days, then the delay won’t probably have any impact on the project. Therefore, there is no need to negotiate the delay or look for a new vendor to get the order delivered on time.

stem: After baselining the scope and during project execution, a key stakeholder, who is a member of the Change Control Board (CCB), requested a new requirement. The project manager is convinced that this new requirement can add value to the project. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Implement the change request since the key stakeholder is a member of the CCB.
options.B: Implement the change request since it will add value to the project.
options.C: Submit a change request according to the change control system.
options.D: Record the change request in the change log.

explanation:
Regardless of the fact that the change was requested by a member of the CCB, the project manager should submit a change request according to the procedures defined in the change control system. This system describes how modifications to project deliverables should be undertaken (PMBOK 7th edition, page 332).
Options A & B: The project manager should not implement the change without getting the CCB’s formal approval. Being convinced of the change’s value or having the consent of one member of the CCB is not sufficient to move forward with the implementation.
Option D: The change request has not been submitted yet to the CCB, so it should not be recorded in the change log. After submitting it, the change log should be updated to track the status of the change.

stem: A solar-powered car project is almost finished when the project manager receives an approved change request to replace a defective component of the car batteries. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Record the problem in the issue log
options.B: Meet with the change control board to discuss the matter
options.C: Repair the defective component
options.D: Replace the defective component

explanation:
Since the project manager has received an approved change request, they should ensure its appropriate implementation.
Option C: Since the change request specifically entails the replacement of the defective component, the project manager shouldn’t repair it instead.

stem: A project manager is wrapping up a one-year project. Which of the following activities should be prioritized?

options.A: Updating the change log
options.B: Releasing the project resources
options.C: Completing the knowledge transfer activities
options.D: Celebrating the project’s completion

explanation:
Because projects are temporary endeavors, most of the acquired knowledge is lost once the project is completed. The project manager should be attentive to knowledge documentation and transfer to allow the organization to gain and retain the knowledge and experience obtained through running projects (PMBOK 7th edition, page 78).
Option A: The change log should be updated to monitor the change requests’ status.
Options B & D: Once the knowledge transfer activity is completed, a celebration could take place and resources can be released.

stem: A project manager closed all contracts related to their construction project, except one that concerns setting up security cameras. The only thing left for this contract is to go through a quick inspection by an expert in order to check out wireless connection, night vision, cloud storage, etc. Knowing that the security cameras are working fine and that the project needs to be closed as soon as possible, what should the project manager do?

options.A: Close the contract and the project with no inspection
options.B: Close the contract, but keep the project open
options.C: Close the project, but keep the contract open
options.D: Keep the contract and the project open

explanation:
The project manager should keep both the contract and the project open until the seller performs the inspection.
Option C: Closing a project entails conducting several processes and steps including closing out all contracts.
Options A & B: Closing a contract requires verifying that the seller has delivered their work as predetermined in the contract.

stem: A project manager is leading a project using the predictive approach within a functional organization. During the project execution, the project manager encountered an issue that was not identified in the planning phase. To resolve this issue, additional work should be added to the project scope, which will result in an increase in the project cost. To whom should the project manager escalate the need for additional funds to complete this work?

options.A: Program manager
options.B: Product owner
options.C: Project sponsor
options.D: Functional manager

explanation:
In a functional organization, the project manager doesn't manage the budget. Thus, they should escalate the need for additional funds to the functional manager. If the functional manager validates their assessment, they will need to escalate their request to the project sponsor to approve allocating additional financial resources. If the project manager was working in a projectized or strong matrix organization, they wouldn't need to raise their request for more funds to the functional manager.
Option A: A program manager, as the name suggests, only handles programs, which is not the case in this scenario.
Options B & C: The product owner’s role is limited to the scrum framework, which is an adaptive approach. If that were the case, the project manager would need to report similar issues to the product owner, who will escalate the matter to the project sponsor.

stem: Adopting a predictive approach to plan an agriculture project, a project manager chooses the ___________ method to estimate the cost by the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS).

options.A: Analogous
options.B: Parametric
options.C: Top-down
options.D: Bottom-up

explanation: The bottom-up method can be used as an estimation technique for the project's overall cost by estimating the approximate value of smaller components and using the total sum of these values to find the overall cost. This type of estimation is used to create the project schedule or budget. The project work is typically subdivided into smaller parts and each component is given a duration and cost estimate. The individual duration estimates are aggregated to determine the schedule, while the individual cost estimates are aggregated to determine the budget.

stem: A project manager is assigned to an industrial project that follows a predictive approach. During the risk planning phase, the project manager decided to create a contingency reserve for:

options.A: Passive risk acceptance
options.B: Active risk acceptance
options.C: Workaround
options.D: Unidentified risks

explanation:
Risk acceptance acknowledges the existence of a threat, but no proactive action is taken (PMBOK 7th edition, page 248). The most common active acceptance strategy is to establish a contingency reserve, including time, money, or resources to handle the threat if it occurs.
Option A: Passive acceptance involves no proactive action apart from a periodic review of the threat to ensure that it does not change signiﬁcantly (PMBOK 6th edition, page 443).
Options C & D: A workaround is an unplanned response to deal with unidentified risks and risks that are passively accepted.

stem: A project manager is leading a construction project. Work on light spots is pending since ceiling tiles are still being installed, which may cause some delays within the project. What should the project manager refer to in order to check the electricity team’s availability in the next two weeks to resolve this dependency?

options.A: Resource Calendars
options.B: Responsibility Assignment Matrix (RAM)
options.C: RACIMatrix
options.D: Organigram

explanation:
A resource calendar is a calendar for planning, managing, and monitoring resources, including both employees and equipment. It gives project managers an overview of how resources are being utilized, which resources are available, and when.
Option B: The Responsibility Assignment Matrix (RAM) describes the involvement of different parties and their roles in completing tasks or deliverables in a project. It's used to clarify roles and responsibilities within a team, project, or process.
Option C: RACI is an acronym for Responsible Accountable Consult and Inform and it’s used to assign roles and responsibilities for each task in a given process.
Option D: An organigram, also called an organizational chart, organogram, or organizational breakdown structure (OBS), is a diagram that depicts the organization’s structure and the relationships and ranks of its different positions.

stem: A project manager created the following high-level hierarchical list of human and physical resources of a project that consists in creating a bulk SMS platform for marketing campaigns. What does this visual illustration represent?

options.A: Resource calendar
options.B: Organization breakdown structure
options.C: Resource breakdown structure
options.D: RACI chart

explanation:
A resource breakdown structure is a hierarchical list of team and physical resources related by category and resource type that is used for project planning, management, and control (PMBOK 7th edition, page 187). Each descending level corresponds to a more detailed description of the resource.
Option A: A resource calendar is a calendar for planning, managing, and monitoring resources.
Option B: Organizational Breakdown Structure (OBS), also known as Organization Chart, is used for representing the project organization.
Option D: RACI is an acronym for Responsible Accountable Consult and Inform and it’s used to assign the roles and responsibilities of the individuals involved in a project or a process.

stem: A project manager is leading a project that has a fixed fee of $5,000 and an estimated cost of $50,000. Knowing that the actual cost of the project reached $60,000, what is the total cost of the Cost Plus Fixed Fee contract?
explanation: The total cost of the Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) contract is the sum of the Actual cost and the Fixed fee; $60,000 + $5,000 = $65,000.

stem: A project manager is assigned to lead a construction project for the first time. Three months into the project, the project manager notices higher-than-expected running costs and decides to assess the project's financial status by calculating the difference between Earned Value (EV) and Actual Cost (AC). What is the project manager calculating?

options.A: Cost Performance Index
options.B: Cost Variance
options.C: Planned Value
options.D: To-Complete Performance Index

explanation: The amount of budget deficit or surplus at a given point in time expressed as the difference between the Earned Value (EV) and the Actual Cost (AC), is known as Cost Variance (PMBOK 7th edition, page 238).

stem: A construction organization launches a new project for building a wastewater treatment center. With the project’s start, the project manager receives updated building codes and regulations from the local authorities. In order to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, what should the project manager do next?

options.A: Update the project schedule to reflect revised timelines for obtaining permits and approvals from local authorities.
options.B: Modify the quality management plan to include updated quality standards and specifications mandated by the revised building codes and regulations.
options.C: Modify the procurement management plan to account for changes in materials or equipment specifications necessitated by the updated building codes and regulations.
options.D: Update the communication management plan to provide stakeholders with regular updates on any changes resulting from updated building codes and regulations.

explanation:
Modifying the quality management plan to include updated quality standards and specifications should be the project manager’s next step after receiving the updated building codes and regulations. This ensures that deliverables are aligned with the updated requirements and that the project remains compliant with regulatory standards.
Option A: While updating the project schedule is important for accommodating changes in timelines due to regulatory updates, it does not directly address the need to ensure compliance with building codes and regulations. This only focuses on schedule adjustments and does not address the broader scope changes necessitated by regulatory requirements.
Option C: While updating the procurement management plan may be necessary to accommodate changes in materials or equipment specifications, it does not directly address the need to ensure compliance with the building codes and regulations. Option D: While adjusting the communications management plan is important for ensuring stakeholders are informed about project progress and changes, it does not directly address the need to ensure compliance with the building codes and regulations.

stem: A project manager is in charge of an ergonomic chair design project. Upon the identification of some technical risks, the project manager decides it’s best to create a prototype. This is an example of risk:

options.A: Acceptance
options.B: Avoidance
options.C: Transfer
options.D: Mitigation

explanation: Risk mitigation can imply prototype development in order to prevent the risk from scaling up. Creating a prototype will support the testing and through testing, you can generate the necessary data to probably even close the risk. To keep costs low, you can opt for partial prototypes for the specific portions of the process that involve the risk.

stem: Project deliverables have recently undergone thorough quality checks by a specialist testing team and have received overall excellent feedback. Excited to move to project closure, the project manager presents the deliverables to the project sponsor for final approval. However, the sponsor accepts all deliverables except three; one is identified as a defect, and the other two as missed requirements. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Immediately make the necessary changes to address the non-accepted deliverables and prevent any further delays in project closure.
options.B: Note the non-accepted deliverables in the risk register, as this might cause the project delay.
options.C: Proceed with project closure since the testing team did not identify any issues.
options.D: Submit a change request for the non-accepted deliverables, providing detailed explanations for the reasons behind the sponsor’s non-acceptance.

explanation:
A change request should be submitted along with the reasons for non-acceptance of completed deliverables to ensure that the identified issues and the sponsor’s concerns are formally addressed and that any deviation from the project requirements is properly documented, evaluated, and fixed.
Option A: No changes should be immediately made without following proper change management procedures. It's crucial to document any changes through formal channels to ensure proper tracking and alignment with project objectives.
Option B: The risk register is primarily used to identify, assess, and develop mitigation plans for potential future events that could negatively or positively impact the project. While the sponsor's rejection does pose a challenge, it's not necessarily an unforeseen event. It's more of a current issue requiring a solution, not a future risk to be monitored.
Option C: You can’t proceed with project closure without getting the sponsor’s formal acceptance of the project deliverables.

stem: A project manager has recently joined a project that has been in development for the past two years. The project manager is familiarizing himself with the project's documentation when he notices that it has undergone various project steps that deviate from the typical phases of design, build, and test. This project’s phases include concept development, feasibility study, commissioning, milestone review, and more. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Reduce and update the project phases to avoid administrative overhead and promote faster delivery.
options.B: Alter the project to adhere to the usual project Design, Build, and Test phases.
options.C: Adhere to the established phases and familiarize himself with the organization's unique process and methodologies.
options.D: Proceed with a waterfall delivery approach, consolidating all project phases into one major release.

explanation:
Each project and organization can be different, with different approaches, phases, politics, ways of working, governance, and approvals.
