If not, they should be persuaded of the importance of continuous improvement as a crucial part of the Agile approach.

stem: A project manager is leading an iteration-based project that uses story points for effort estimation. While checking the burndown chart of the current iteration, the project manager finds that the trend line is above the projected line. What does that mean?

options.A: The iteration is behind schedule
options.B: The iteration is on schedule
options.C: The iteration is ahead of schedule
options.D: None of the above. The schedule should not be controlled in Agile

explanation: In the burndown chart, the trend line shows how much work is pending. When the actual progress line is above the projected line, it indicates that there is more work pending than initially planned. Agile self-organized teams use empirical and value-based measurements, such as the burndown chart, to monitor the iteration status. Controlling the schedule when following an agile approach is different than when using the predictive approach; the team is responsible for completing iterations on time. Besides, if the iteration ends without completing all the work, no change requests can be issued since the schedule is fixed and the scope is variable in Agile.

stem: After acquiring resources for a new hybrid project, the project manager decided to develop a training plan to improve their competencies. Which of the following tools can the project manager use to assess the team members’ skills? (Select two)

options.A: Brainstorming
options.B: Ability tests
options.C: Focus groups
options.D: Team-building

explanation:
Individual and team assessment tools include attitudinal surveys, speciﬁc assessments, structured interviews, ability tests, and focus groups.
Option A: Brainstorming is mostly used for collecting project requirements.
Option D: Team-building is used for team development.

stem: To collect more funding, a project manager sends their project’s business case to an investor who happens to be quite demanding, as they might reject a project because its goal is not SMART. What does “S” stand for?

options.A: Specific
options.B: Simple
options.C: Smart
options.D: Safe

explanation: SMART is an acronym that stands for Specific, Meaningful, Achievable, Relevant, and Timely (PMBOK 7th edition, page 97). Each letter in SMART can have other alternatives, except the “S” which commonly refers to “Specific” or “Strategic and Specific”.

stem: The cross-functional team is complaining that their work is moving slowly because the project sponsor is constantly inquiring about the implementation details and technical choices. What should the scrum master do?

options.A: Assign one team member to answer all of the sponsor’s questions.
options.B: Inform the sponsor that any future questions should be brought to them being the scrum master.
options.C: Ask the product owner to help the team deal with the sponsor’s questions.
options.D: Inform the team that they should ask for permission before discussing any details with the sponsor.

explanation: Apart from being responsible for guiding the team, the Scrum Master is also responsible for protecting the development team from any interruptions or distractions. This situation requires the Scrum Master’s intervention on behalf of the team to ask the sponsor subtly to stop interrupting the team’s work.

stem: To obtain the human resource requirements of their new project, the project manager published a job offer on a well-known recruitment platform. Days later, over 300 applications were submitted. Going through all of them will take a lot of time and effort. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Use a weighting system to select the best applicants
options.B: Add a section for minimum qualifications in the job description
options.C: Create a screening system to reduce the number of applications to treat
options.D: Randomly select a few candidates and pick the best of them

explanation:
A screening system could be used to short-list applicants based on predefined criteria, such as technical capabilities, years of experience, location, etc. Since the number of applications is high, it would be better to resort to screening. By defining go/no-go criteria, the project manager will be able to reduce the number of applications to treat.
Option A: Using a weighting system requires a thorough examination of each application since a score will be attributed according to a set of predefined criteria. Hence, this option would be time-consuming. It could, however, be used after applying the screening system.
Option B: Altering the job description is not the right action since the job offer had already been published, and applications had been received. Thus, the question addresses the resource selection phase.
Option D: Random selection is not a suitable option because it does not ensure the selection of eligible resources.

stem: A project manager noticed that team members are dedicating too much time to refining the product backlog, which is impacting their commitment to the sprint work. How should the project manager approach this problem?

options.A: Ask the product owner to assume the responsibility of refining the product backlog so that the development team can concentrate on their sprint work.
options.B: Do nothing since refining the product backlog is quite important.
options.C: Constrain the team to their sprint work by canceling product backlog refinement meetings.
options.D: Coach the team to better manage their time through refining the product backlog for the next sprint while remaining committed to their current sprint.

explanation: In agile projects, the scrum team opts for a gradual method of work elaboration, in which they only refine the product backlog items that they intend to implement in the next sprint or in the near future. However, it’s important for the team to strike the right balance between product backlog refinement tasks and their sprint work.

stem: For an innovative project using an iterative approach, the project manager schedules a demonstration session with a group of end-users to showcase progress and gather feedback. Despite the fact that this is the fifth demonstration meeting, users still asked for other changes. The project team will be now implementing the requested alterations and another demonstration session will be scheduled. Which of the following statements best describes this situation?

options.A: Better change control and requirements management practices should be implemented.
options.B: The project team is not well acquainted with the project requirements.
options.C: The project team is developing the product effectively.
options.D: The end users are indecisive about what they want.

explanation:
In an iterative approach, it is expected that feedback will be gathered from end-users at regular intervals (such as during demonstration sessions), and the product will be refined based on this feedback. The fact that users are requesting changes after multiple demonstrations is a natural part of the iterative process. It shows that the team is responding to evolving user needs and making continuous improvements.
Option A: Change control and requirements management practices would be more appropriate for a predictive approach, where changes after scope definition might indicate issues. In iterative methods, changes are normal and expected.
Option B: The ongoing changes reflect adjustments based on real-time input rather than a lack of understanding of the requirements.
Option D: In an iterative approach, user feedback evolves naturally as they see and interact with product increments.

stem: A project manager is managing two agile teams. The organization set a $5,000 bonus for the best-performing team and asked the project manager to determine the reward criteria. The project manager decided to use velocity as a performance metric and announced that the team with the highest velocity would get the bonus. Is velocity a suitable criterion in this case?

options.A: No, velocity should not be used as a performance metric for rewards and recognition
options.B: No, velocity is only used for planning purposes
options.C: No, velocity is only used as a team diagnostic metric
options.D: Yes, velocity indicates which team gets more work done on each sprint

explanation:
Velocity should not be used as a performance metric for assessing the team’s productivity. When misused in such a scenario, velocity can result in imprudent and misleading behavior; team members might start to manipulate the system to show higher velocity numbers. They may also undermine quality to get more work “done” which will lead to increasing levels of technical debt (Essential Scrum by Rubin, Kenneth S, page 137).
Option B: Velocity is used as a planning tool; for example, if your team’s velocity is 20 story points and you intend to achieve user stories of 100 story points, you’ll need 5 sprints to get all the work done.
Option C: Velocity is also used as a team diagnostic metric since a consistent velocity is the hallmark of a healthy agile team.

stem: A project manager is assigned to lead an external software development project under a T&M contract. After coming up with a way to automate the testing activities, the project manager finds out that this will lead to finishing the project ahead of schedule and under budget. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Inform the customer of the potential cost and time changes.
options.B: Hold this information since all cost savings are considered as an additional profit.
options.C: Do nothing since the customer will have access to all of these details at the end of the project and savings will be split according to the contract terms.
options.D: Use the saved time and money to add more features.

explanation:
Since a Time and Material contract consists of quoting the spent and used labor and materials instead of determining a fixed price for the provided service and/or product, the customer should be informed of the schedule and budget changes in order to issue a correct invoice.
Options B & C: Withholding similar information is considered unethical.
Option D: Adding more features requires the approval of the customer. Otherwise, this behavior will be considered Gold Plating. In T&M contracts, there are no incentive fees, unlike the Cost Plus Incentive Fee contract where savings are split between the two parties according to a pre-negotiated formula.

stem: An organization assigned an agile coach to assist the project manager and the project team with the transition to Agile project management. During a training session, the agile coach explained the nature of the relationship between the development team and the customer along with both parties’ responsibilities in Scrum, stating that:

options.A: The development team is responsible for determining which features should be addressed first.
options.B: The customer is responsible for determining how to carry on the project work.
options.C: The customer is responsible for defining value and assessing the user experience.
options.D: The development team is responsible for prioritizing features.

explanation:
The Scrum framework explicitly defines the role and responsibilities of the development team, the product owner, the customer, and other stakeholders. The customer or the product owner are the ones responsible for defining the product scope and features, prioritizing the derived user stories according to their values, and deciding which will be generated first.
Options A, B, D: The development team is responsible for determining how to carry out the work (the approaches and the techniques that will be implemented and followed for the development process). Upon completing and delivering the development work, it is up to the customer to review and assess the user experience in order to confirm whether the delivered product meets their needs and expectations.

stem: A team member was assigned to add an “upload” button to a website’s support page so that users can attach files when reporting any issues. During the iteration review, the team member proudly demonstrated that they did not only add the button, but also included the possibility of uploading files through “drag and drop”. How do you describe the team member’s behavior?

options.A: This is “delivering value”, which should be encouraged
options.B: This is “customer obsession”, which should be encouraged
options.C: This is “scope creep”, which should be avoided
options.D: This is “gold plating”, which should be avoided

explanation:
Gold plating entails adding more features that are not included or agreed upon in the scope or product backlog, in order to please the customer.
Option C: This does not involve scope creep because the customer didn’t request the change. Option B: Customer obsession consists of hyperfocus on customers’ requirements through consistently collecting their feedback to improve their user experience. The product owner should foreground what customers want by prioritizing their requirements in the product backlog.
Option A: The iterative and incremental aspects of the agile approach ensure the continuous delivery of value to the customer.

stem: One of the cross-functional team members took an urgent unplanned leave, putting the rest of the team under a lot of pressure in order to meet the sprint goal. How should the agile project manager address this issue?

options.A: Ask team members to take their time finishing tasks with no need to rush.
options.B: Ask the functional manager to assign a replacement for the leaving team member.
options.C: Ask team members to work extra hours.
options.D: Ask the product owner to extend the sprint duration in order to give the team more time to finish the sprint backlog.

explanation:
Emergency leaves are a common risk that can occur anytime in any type of project. Taking into consideration that agile promotes a work-life balance, team members should be encouraged to work according to their available capacity to keep everyone motivated and avoid draining their energy.
Option C: Therefore, working extra hours is not an option.
Option B: Asking for a replacement won’t be practical for a short period of time since it’ll take them more time to learn about the project.
Option D: Sprint duration is time-boxed and should not be extended.

stem: In predictive projects, the scope baseline, which is usually used as a basis for future comparisons, can only be modified through formal change control procedures. What are the components of the scope baseline?

options.A: Scope statement, WBS, and WBS dictionary
options.B: Scope management plan and WBS
options.C: WBS and WBS dictionary
options.D: Project charter and Scope management plan

explanation: Scope Baseline is the approved version of a scope statement, work breakdown structure (WBS), and its associated WBS dictionary (PMBOK 7th edition, page 188).

stem: When working on the WBS, a project manager disagrees with the project team about whether to use numbers or letters when indicating the highest level of the Work Breakdown Structure. The project manager believes that with a lot of levels in the WBS, A.1.2.2 will be clearer and easier to read than 1.1.2.2. What is this disagreement mainly about?

options.A: Code of accounts
options.B: Control accounts
options.C: Work packages
options.D: Scheduling software

explanation:
Code of accounts is the identifier of the WBS components.
Options B & C: Control accounts, planning packages, and work packages are components of the WBS rather than identifiers. Control accounts present the highest level of the WBS, while work packages are the lowest level.

stem: A project manager had already assembled a team for a new project when they got promoted to a portfolio manager position. The project manager informed their successor that the majority of the team needed training. In order to be able to provide the team members with the suitable type of training, the succeeding project manager should refer to:

options.A: Resource Management Plan
options.B: Responsibility Assignment Matrix
options.C: Work performance reports
options.D: Work Breakdown Structure

explanation:
The Resource Management Plan covers staffing acquisition, timetable, training needs, recognition and rewards, release criteria, compliance, and safety.
Option B: The Responsibility Assignment Matrix (RAM) is a useful tool for ensuring a clear division of roles and expectations.
Option D: The Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) is a hierarchical decomposition of the total scope of work to be carried out by the project team to accomplish the project objectives and create the required deliverables.

stem: A team has 100 story points in the product backlog and a velocity of 30 points per iteration. Taking into consideration that the iteration is two weeks long, how many weeks does the team need to complete the backlog?

options.A: 4 weeks
options.B: 6 weeks
options.C: 8 weeks
options.D: 10 weeks

explanation: It will take the project team 3.3 iterations to complete the backlog work items (100 story points / 30 story points = 3.3 iterations). It would take 4 iterations to complete the work because the timebox of the iteration shouldn’t be changed. Since the question specifically asks how many weeks are needed to complete work, then 8 weeks is the right answer.

stem: Leading an internal software development project within a large technology company, the project manager encounters a resistant stakeholder who is the head of the company’s IT department. The stakeholder expresses strong opposition to the project, citing concerns about potential disruption to existing operations and the need for retraining the staff to adopt new technologies. Despite the project manager’s attempts to engage the stakeholder in project discussions, he remains actively resistant to the project implementation efforts. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Call for a stakeholder workshop involving all key project stakeholders to facilitate open dialogue and collaboration.
options.B: Proceed with the project according to the original plan without making any accommodations.
options.C: Develop a stakeholder engagement plan tailored specifically to address the concerns and preferences of the resistant stakeholder.
options.D: Negotiate with the resistant stakeholder and make changes to project objectives or deliverables to appease his objections.

explanation:
Developing a stakeholder engagement plan tailored specifically to address the concerns and preferences of the resistant stakeholder is the right approach to this situation. Developing a tailored stakeholder engagement plan demonstrates a proactive and systematic approach to managing the resistant stakeholder. By customizing communication channels, engagement activities, and feedback mechanisms to meet the stakeholder's preferences, the project manager can foster meaningful dialogue and ensure that the stakeholder's concerns are addressed effectively.
Option A: Calling for a stakeholder workshop involving all key project stakeholders is unnecessary since the project manager is facing challenges with one particular stakeholder.
Option B: Ignoring the resistant stakeholder's objections and proceeding with the project without addressing their concerns disregards the importance of stakeholder engagement and may lead to increased resistance.
Option D: Attempting to negotiate with the resistant stakeholder by compromising on project objectives undermines the integrity of the project and may lead to poor outcomes.

stem: The team of a newly initiated project comprises individuals from various departments within the organization, each with their own agenda. This led to numerous conflicts hindering the team’s productivity and project progress. The program manager asks the project manager to leverage his positional authority to address these conflicts and ease the team's transition to a more cohesive state. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Step back from the conflicts to allow the self-organized team to independently reach a consensus.
options.B: Use his legitimate power to force a resolution for the conflicts.
options.C: Act as a mediator to appease the conflict.
options.D: Collaborate with the team to resolve the conflicts.

explanation:
Using legitimate or positional power when it comes to conflict resolution entails pushing one’s viewpoint at the expense of others; offering only win-lose solutions to resolve an emergency (Process Groups: A Practice Guide (2022), page 259). While positional power should be exercised judiciously, there are instances where decisive actions are required to maintain project momentum.
Option A: In situations where conflicts persist and hinder productivity, active intervention may be necessary. Therefore, withdrawing or stepping back from the conflicts to allow team members to resolve them independently is not an option in this scenario.
Option C: Acting as a mediator to appease the conflict means smoothing or accommodating the conflict, which does not address the underlying issues causing these conflicts nor does it put an end to them.
Option D: Collaborating with the team to resolve the conflicts is the healthier option when addressing conflicts, except when dealing with persisting conflicts that hinder progress; this requires a more assertive approach to facilitate resolution.

stem: An organization intends to form a change control board for assessing and managing change requests. What is the most appropriate selection of members to form the change control board?

options.A: Project sponsor and product owner
options.B: Project manager and project team members
options.C: Project sponsor, project manager, and project team members
options.D: Product owner and scrum master

explanation:
The change control board is established within an organization to review all change requests and decide whether to approve or reject them. The appropriate board structure should involve the project manager, project team members, and the sponsor. Along with these members, the change control board (CCB) could also include key stakeholders such as subject matter experts and consultants.
Option D: The product owner and Scrum master are roles under the Scrum framework, which doesn’t include a change control board.

stem: A project manager is leading a construction project that consists of adding a number of bungalows to a seaside hotel. Since they need to procure the required construction materials, the project manager is responsible for issuing all of the following documents, except:

options.A: Proposals
options.B: Source selection criteria
options.C: Request for quotes
options.D: Purchase order

explanation:
As the buyer, the project manager is responsible for issuing the source selection criteria, Request For Quotes (RFQ), and Purchase Order (PO) as procurement documents. Proposals, which involve all information required in the request for quotes, are created by the seller.
Option B: Source selection criteria are set by the buyer and used to choose the most convenient provider.
Option C: A request for quote (RFQ) is used to solicit selected suppliers to submit quotes and bids for certain tasks or products.
Option D: A purchase order (PO) is issued by the buyer for the seller in order to indicate the ordered products or services’ quantity, type, and prices.

stem: A project manager works in an IT company that strictly complies with the Agile Software Development Manifesto. All of the following are values of the Agile Manifesto, with the exception of:

options.A: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools
options.B: Working software over comprehensive documentation
options.C: Customer collaboration over contract negotiation
options.D: Following an iteration over following a plan

explanation: The correct value is “Responding to Change over Following a Plan”. All of the other alternatives are the right values of the Agile Manifesto (Agile Practice Guide, page 8).

stem: After shortlisting vendors, a project manager is in the process of preparing the contract. What type of contract should the project manager opt for if they want to terminate the project in case they’re not satisfied with the delivered incremental shippable product?

options.A: Fixed Price
options.B: Cost Reimbursable
options.C: Fixed Price with Incentive
options.D: Time & Materials (T&M)

explanation: The project manager should choose a Time and Materials (T&M) contract. This type of agreement allows them to only pay the contractor for the actual cost of the invested time (usually involves specific hourly rates), as well as the actual cost of the used materials and equipment.

stem: A project manager is leading a project with some remote team members. The project manager recently received a complaint from these members, claiming that they are being treated as second-class employees. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Review team charter
options.B: Conduct a performance survey to evaluate the efficiency of remote work
options.C: Invest more in collaboration tools
options.D: Perform a root cause analysis

explanation: Identifying the main cause of the issue by performing a root cause analysis is what the project manager should do in the first place, as there is no mention in this scenario of why remote team members feel like they are treated as second-class employees. For instance, they might be feeling isolated due to a lack of collaborative tools or they might be feeling discriminated against due to cultural differences. After finding out the root cause of the issue, the project manager can discuss the matter with the concerned members to come up with an appropriate solution.

stem: Which of the following is an example of an information radiator?

options.A: Prototype
options.B: Milestone
options.C: Kanban board
options.D: Brainstorming

explanation:
Information radiators, such as the Kanban board, are a visible display of up-to-date information concerning the team’s work status.
Option B: A milestone is a point or an event in the project that does not display status information.
Options D & A: Brainstorming is a data-gathering technique, whereas a prototype is a method of getting early feedback on requirements.

stem: During the sprint, the scrum master asked two senior members whether the remaining work in the sprint backlog could be completed to achieve the sprint goal. The team members replied by saying that they were not supposed to track such data. What should the scrum master do next?

options.A: Take disciplinary action against the two team members.
options.B: Take charge of tracking the sprint backlog progress.
options.C: Inform the two team members that tracking sprint backlog is the responsibility of the development team and guide them through the process.
options.D: Ask the two team members about the sprint backlog progress during the next standup instead.

explanation:
The scrum master needs to coach the two senior team members and bring to their attention that the scrum team is responsible for tracking the total work remaining in the sprint backlog as an indicator of whether or not they will achieve the sprint goal.
Option B: In order to get a clear idea about the sprint backlog progress, the scrum master can simply check the burndown chart, but it’s not their responsibility to continuously track the sprint backlog work progress.
Option D: The project manager can also attend the standup meeting in order to detect any bottlenecks and help tackle and remove them.

stem: A new project manager was excited to lead a project for the first time. However, their enthusiasm faded away as soon as they realized that, despite their position, they had limited control over the project. In which type of organization would the project manager have the most control as a project manager?

options.A: Projectized organization
options.B: Weak matrix organization
options.C: Balanced matrix organization
options.D: Strong matrix organization

explanation: A projectized organization allows project managers to have the most control over their projects. In this type of organization, the project manager is responsible for making practically all of the decisions as all organizational units report directly to the project manager. Furthermore, most of the organization’s resources are fully dedicated to project work.

stem: A project manager decides to plan and manage a new project using a waterfall approach. The project team starts estimating the required resources when the Project Management Office (PMO) issues a mandate stating that the organization will no longer use third parties or off-site workers and that all resources must be onsite. Upon reviewing the project’s activity list, the project manager realizes that a crucial part of project work requires off-site resources. What should the project manager do first?

options.A: Discuss the issue with the project sponsor to navigate other options.
options.B: Perform alternatives analysis to evaluate the impact of using onsite resources instead of off-site resources.
options.C: Update the resource calendar to adapt it to the PMO’s mandate.
options.D: Update the resource management plan to adapt it to the PMO’s mandate.

explanation:
The project manager should first perform alternatives analysis to evaluate the impact of using onsite resources instead of off-site resources. Alternatives analysis consists of identifying the variables to be considered in evaluating options, and the relative importance or weight of each variable (PMBOK 7th Edition, page 122). This will allow the project manager to find the best solution to perform the project activities, within the defined constraints.
Option A: If the analysis reveals a significant impact that can impede the project’s execution, the project manager can then discuss the issue with the sponsor. Escalating the matter in this case might be inevitable to navigate and find other options to proceed with the project within the PMO’s newly imposed restrictions. This should be considered as a last resolution if the project manager can’t find any solution or if the required solution passes his authority and requires the intervention of the sponsor.
Option C: Updating the resource calendar is premature since the project manager is still in the resource planning phase and hasn’t committed to any resource allocations yet.
Option D: After determining the impact of the PMO’s mandate on the project, and if the project is deemed achievable within the applied constraint, the project manager can update the resource management plan as a next step to reflect this change and adapt the plan to the PMO’s mandate.

stem: A project manager is overseeing a complex multi-million project to repair an interstate bridge. After developing a Request For Proposal (RFP) that includes source selection criteria and a detailed statement of work, the project team evaluated multiple vendor responses and selected the most suitable seller. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Seek upper management approval to finalize the contract award.
options.B: Update the stakeholder register to include the seller and hold a meeting to initiate the collaboration.
options.C: Create the contract and proceed with the project execution based on the agreed terms.
options.D: Update the procurement management plan by incorporating the approved RFP.

explanation:
Final approval of complex, high-value, high-risk procurements will generally require organizational senior management approval prior to award (Process Groups: A Practice Guide (2022), page 238).
Options B & D: Updating the stakeholder register or the procurement management plan is not the appropriate next step following the selection of the seller. The priority at this stage is finalizing the agreement with the chosen vendor.
Option C: Creating the contract and proceeding with the project execution is usually the typical next step in many procurement processes. However, in this scenario, upper management involvement is crucial for finalizing the contract.

stem: A project sponsor assigned a product owner to an agile project. After a few iterations, the sponsor announced that since the product owner seemed to be oblivious to their role and responsibilities, they would be replaced by someone else. What did the first product owner probably do wrong?

options.A: Tell the agile team what work they should do
options.B: Tell the agile team how they should do their work
options.C: Tell the agile team when the work needs to be done
options.D: Tell the agile team why the work is needed

explanation: It’s not among the product owner’s responsibilities to tell a self-organizing agile team how to do their work. However, it’s among their responsibilities to let them know what they should do through defining requirements and user stories, when they should do it by defining priorities, and why they do it by defining a vision.

stem: An organization decides to develop an innovative system to control the quality of its products. The project manager assigned to the project opted for an Agile approach. Why did the project manager make this choice?

options.A: To avoid change requests as much as possible
options.B: To avoid scope creep as much as possible
options.C: To get feedback as early as possible
options.D: To complete the project as early as possible

explanation: Since it’s based on short development iterations, Agile approaches allow for early and frequent feedback by delivering a working piece of the product at the end of each iteration to the customer. Since traditional projects can only obtain customer feedback at the end, it is often too late to incorporate the feedback or fix any issues at that stage, unlike Agile projects where new changes are welcomed and integrated into the product development process.

stem: Agile team members are estimating a complex user story. Which of the following items the agile team should not include in their estimations?

options.A: Research time
options.B: Troubleshooting time
options.C: Testing time
options.D: Waste time

explanation: Waste time involves the time lost due to interruptions, unproductive meetings, low internet speed, server connection latency, etc. User story estimates should not include waste time; they should only include all known activities needed to complete the user story such as research, execution, troubleshooting, testing, etc.

stem: A scrum master is leading a project with two-week sprints. The cross-functional team, which is composed of five members, had a disagreement about the maximum duration of a standup meeting. While some believe it should be 15 minutes, others think that 10 minutes are sufficient. The scrum master interfered to inform them that the maximum duration of the daily standup is:

options.A: 10 minutes, since each team member needs 2 minutes for their status update
options.B: 10 minutes, since it’s a 2-week sprint and they should dedicate 5 minutes for each week
options.C: 15 minutes, since 3 minutes should be allocated for each team member
options.D: 15 minutes, regardless of the team size and iteration length

explanation: The duration of a daily Scrum meeting is time-boxed as 15 minutes; it does not change depending on the length of a Sprint or the size of the team (Agile Practice Guide, page 53).

stem: During a training session, and in order to clearly explain what a project can be, a project management coach gave their trainees the following example:

options.A: Saving an endangered species of rhinos from extinction
options.B: A weekly clean-up of the local park
options.C: A shoe factory that produces 1000 pairs monthly
options.D: Preparing pasta for your family every Monday

explanation:
Saving an endangered species of rhinos from extinction is the only correct example of a project since it has a unique outcome and a limited time frame. Governments and NGOs usually lead this kind of project which can take years. However, activities occurring after the project is complete, such as routinely keeping track of the endangered species population, could be considered operations.
Options B, C, D: Periodically cleaning the local park, cyclically producing shoes, or routinely preparing dinner are all examples of operations rather than projects.

stem: A project manager is pitching an innovative project idea in an entrepreneurial event to get the needed investment. To ensure that they engage both the audience and the jury during the pitch, the project manager should:

options.A: Point her finger
options.B: Make eye contact
options.C: Wave her hands
options.D: Stand up straight

explanation: In order to establish a proper connection with the audience and jury, the project manager should make eye contact. It is critical to maintain eye contact with the receiving part of the communication process. The project manager should confidently look at the audience, without focusing on one person. Instead, they should make a sweeping glance at the audience from the left to the right and from the front to the back of the room to try and hold the attention of each member of the audience.

stem: A scrum master suggested facilitating the first backlog refinement session since the product owner and some of the development team are new to the agile method. After a quick intro, what should the scrum master ask the participants to do?

options.A: Only add more details to the product backlog items
options.B: Only add initial estimates and more details to the product backlog items
options.C: Only add more details to the product backlog items and define their priorities
options.D: Add initial estimates and more details to the product backlog items and define their priorities

explanation: During backlog refinement, the team helps the product owner create or review emergent product backlog items as well as progressively refine larger ones. The team also estimates the size of product backlog items and helps the product owner prioritize them. As a general rule, the development team should allocate up to 10% of its time in each sprint to assisting the product owner with refinement activities (Essential Scrum by Rubin, Kenneth S, page 106).

stem: While reviewing an important Epic, members of the self-organizing team had different interpretations of how it should be broken down, which revealed a lack of common understanding of the project’s purpose. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Ask the team to check the release plan
options.B: Ask the team to check the acceptance criteria of the Epic
options.C: Remind the team of the sprint goal
options.D: Remind the team of the project vision

explanation:
The project manager should remind the team of the project’s vision since the team seems to lack a common understanding of the project’s purpose.
Option A: Referring to the release plan can only help the team understand the goal of that specific release.
Option B: Epic’s acceptance criteria are the conditions that have to be met to be approved by the product owner. Even though these conditions can help the team understand the Epic and how to break it down, they can’t help them get a clear understanding of the project’s purpose.
Option C: The sprint goal only states and clarifies the vision of the iteration, not the overall project vision.

stem: A product owner is assigned to a new agile project at a software development company. The company’s main measure of its projects’ success is the number of features delivered into production. The product owner’s team has been delivering a record number of features since the project started. However, despite the high volume of features being rolled out, customers have started to voice their frustration about encountering numerous issues and bugs in the software. What should the product owner do?

options.A: Encourage the team to keep the same pace of delivering more features and issues will be fixed later on.
options.B: Add an item to the sprint backlog, to deal with the technical debt.
options.C: Include customer satisfaction and quality KPIs as product success metrics.
options.D: Discuss customer feedback during the demonstration of the finished product.

explanation:
The scenario depicts the Hawthorne effect which states that the very act of measuring something influences behavior. Therefore, only measuring a project team's output of deliverables can encourage the project team to focus on creating a large volume of deliverables rather than focusing on deliverables that would provide higher customer satisfaction (PMBOK 7th Edition, page 112). Including customer satisfaction and quality KPIs as product success metrics would balance the team’s behavior and make them focus on delivering and satisfying customers' requirements.
Option A: Encouraging the team to keep the same pace of delivering more features without proactively fixing the encountered issues means overlooking the underlying issue of product quality and customer dissatisfaction. Even if it means meeting the company’s performance metrics, this behavior will eventually lead to project failure.
Option B: Adding an item to the sprint backlog to deal with the technical debt doesn’t address the root cause of the issue. Additionally, handling technical debt should be a continuous endeavor throughout the project; it requires more than just adding a single item in the current sprint.
Option D: Discussing customer feedback during the demonstration of the finished product is counterproductive since the customers have already shared their feedback i.e. expressing their frustration about encountering numerous issues and bugs in the software, therefore the product owner should address this urgently rather than waiting until the demonstration of the finished product.

stem: A project manager is leading a hybrid project to replace the organization's outdated system that has recently undergone a feature upgrade release. During the daily stand-up meeting, the senior developer mentions that, following the upgrade, certain parts of the system are not connecting to various areas within the organization. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Assign the senior developer as a risk owner and ask him to collaborate with the rest of the team to come up with a suitable risk response.
options.B: Review the project plan to ensure connectivity to all areas.
options.C: Note the developer’s concern in the issue log and work on finding a solution.
options.D: Note the developer’s concern in the risk register and work on developing potential risk responses.

explanation:
An issue log is used to record and monitor information on active issues. Issues are assigned to a responsible party for follow-up and resolution (PMBOK 7th Edition, page 185).
Option A: The scenario depicts an issue; a risk that has already occurred, therefore noting the developer’s concern in the issue log and assigning him as a risk owner are not the appropriate steps in this situation.
Option B: Altering the project plan does not address the need to find a solution for the encountered issue.
Option D: The risk register is used to document potential issues that could occur whereas the developer is raising a concern about an issue that already occurred i.e. parts of the system are not connecting to various areas within the organization following the upgrade.

stem: A project manager performs a cost-benefit analysis before embarking on a new project to assess its potential costs and revenues. The analysis results will determine whether the project will be profitable or whether the organization should choose another project instead. The project manager finds out that the project's Benefit-Cost Ratio is 1.3. What does this mean?

options.A: The project’s revenue is 1.3 times its profit
options.B: The project’s cost is 1.3 times its profit
options.C: The project’s profit is 1.3 times its cost
options.D: The project’s revenue is 1.3 times its cost

explanation: A benefit-cost ratio (BCR) is a monetary or qualitative metric that shows the relationship between potential project costs and benefits. If the BCR is greater than 1.0, its revenue will potentially outweigh its cost and if it’s less than 1.0, the costs outweigh the gains (PMBOK 7th edition, page 102). The benefit-cost ratio (BCR) formula is as follows: the sum of the project's benefits divided by the sum of its costs. In this situation, 1.3 means that revenue is 1.3 times the cost. The term “benefit”, in the Benefit-Cost Ratio, refers to all the cash flow or income generated from the project, unlike “profit” which represents the net income after deducting all expenses and operating costs.

stem: In a weak matrix organization, employees work across multiple projects and with various departments within the company to increase employee interaction and promote teamwork spirit. If additional employees are needed, who is in charge of the hiring process under this matrix?

options.A: The project manager
options.B: The sponsor
options.C: The project team
options.D: The functional manager

explanation: The functional manager is the one in charge of managing resources under a weak matrix. This matrix form has a huge resemblance to a traditional workplace hierarchy. A functional manager is a project’s main decision-maker as they supervise all of its aspects. Although the project manager also serves as a point of authority, they primarily report back to the functional manager.

stem: A project manager is assigned to lead a digital marketing project. Some stakeholders don’t support the project, and others want the entire project to be planned out before it starts. The sponsor, on the other hand, is looking for a quick win to get the support of the majority of stakeholders and ensure the project’s continuation. What approach should the project manager adopt in such circumstances?

options.A: An agile approach, as it would please the majority of stakeholders.
options.B: An agile approach, as it would produce functioning deliverables quickly.
options.C: A predictive approach, as it would give more clarity to the project.
options.D: A predictive approach, since agile is only used for software development projects.

explanation:
Since the sponsor is looking for a quick win, then the project manager should adopt an agile approach. The agile approach introduces working functionalities early in the project, which could help the project manager/sponsor win the stakeholders’ support and avoid project discontinuation.
Option C: Certain stakeholders wanted the entire project to be planned out before it started, so they would be pleased with using a predictive approach for the project implementation. This approach gives more clarity to the work scope. However, the risk of losing stakeholders’ support along the way is very high since the project manager won’t be able to introduce tangible results until the end of the project (PMBOK 7th edition, page 46).
Option D: Finally, agile is applicable to various fields, not just in the software industry (Agile Practice Guide, page 1).

stem: A project manager was assigned to develop a mobile app with a team of five members. Which of the following project life cycles can be adopted by the project manager?

options.A: Initiation, planning, executing, monitoring and controlling, and closing
options.B: Wireframing, prototyping, designing, developing, testing, and deploying
options.C: Development, introduction, growth, maturity, and decline
options.D: Forming, storming, norming, performing, and adjourning

explanation:
The project life cycle that can be adopted for developing a mobile app project is: Wireframing, prototyping, designing, developing, testing, and deploying. A project life cycle comprises the different development phases that a project goes through from its start to its completion. Depending on different factors, a project lifecycle often includes Feasibility, Design, Build, Test, Deploy, and Close phases (PMBOK 7, pages 33 - 42).
Option A: Initiation, planning, executing, monitoring and controlling, and closing are process groups rather than project lifecycle phases.
Option C: Development, introduction, growth, maturity, and decline are the phases of product life cycle.
Option D: Forming, storming, norming, performing, and adjourning are team development phases according to Tuckman’s theory.

stem: An organization went through a transformation to adopt the Kanban approach for managing its new projects. The Kanban board includes four columns: To Do, Doing, Testing, and Done. How should the project manager deal with the items on these different lists?

options.A: Limit the items in the To-do list
options.B: Limit the items in the Testing list
options.C: Increase the number of items in the Testing list
options.D: Increase the number of items in the Doing list

explanation:
In Kanban, the project manager should limit Work In Progress (WIP), meaning work under the “Doing” and “Testing” columns. This helps boost performance, which automatically leads to increasing items in the “Done” list.
Option A: Items on the “To do” list should be increased so the team won’t be blocked waiting for the next items to work on.

stem: A project manager works for a mobile app development company. One of his latest projects involves the creation of an exercise app that syncs with another nutrition app to combine and analyze the data. As a result of a recent regulatory change, the project team is working on refining the backlog. The process of backlog refinement involves:

options.A: The identification of the work items to be accomplished during the next sprint.
options.B: A board to keep track of the product and sprint backlogs.
options.C: A prioritized list of product requirements which is maintained by the project team.
options.D: The gradual development of product specifications to meet the needs of the product owner.

explanation:
Backlog refinement refers to the progressive elaboration of project requirements where the Agile team collaboratively integrates reviews and updates with the sole purpose of satisfying the customer and product owner’s needs (PMBOK 7th edition, page 235).
Option A: The identification of the work items to be accomplished during the next sprint is carried out during the sprint planning.
Option C: The backlog is a prioritized list of product requirements that is maintained by the team.
Option B: An information radiator or a Kanban board helps to keep track of the product and sprint backlogs.

stem: Halfway through a sprint, the development team realized that they planned for more work than they could possibly complete. What should the project manager advise the development team to do next?

options.A: Ask the product owner to remove some work items from the sprint backlog.
options.B: Collaborate with the product owner to reprioritize the product backlog items.
options.C: Continue work and put off discussing this issue to the sprint retrospective.
options.D: Inform the product owner during the sprint review that some features could not be completed.

explanation:
First, the development team should collaborate with the product owner in order to remove some work items from the sprint backlog. The sprint backlog is a living artifact that should be updated whenever something new is learned or discovered.
Option C: Afterward, in the sprint retrospective, the team should discuss how they can improve their estimations.
Option D: The agile team should be proactive and should not wait for the sprint review in order to inform the product owner that they couldn’t complete the affected work.
Option B: Reprioritizing the product backlog items won’t help solve this problem. This activity is often undertaken during the refinement sessions with the purpose of making user stories ready for the following iterations.

stem: A project manager is leading a software project. The project team finished all of the tasks in the iteration backlog early and decided to work on code clean-up for the rest of the iteration. Despite their intention to decrease technical debt, which will save the customer maintenance fees in the future, neither the customer nor the project manager seems to be happy. What could be the reason behind the customer’s dissatisfaction?

options.A: The customer wanted to avoid scope creep
options.B: The customer wanted to avoid gold plating
options.C: The customer wanted to prioritize the scope
options.D: The customer wanted to minimize costs by ending the iteration earlier

explanation:
The probable reason for customer dissatisfaction is there are more prioritized items in the product backlog that the team could have worked on instead of the code clean-up activity. Stakeholders are the ones responsible for defining and prioritizing the scope and requirements for the project team (PMBOK 7th edition, page 14).
Option A: Since the customer didn’t ask for the code clean-up work, then it could not be considered scope creep. What the team did is “gold plating”, which implies doing additional activities that were neither agreed upon nor included in the iteration backlog, with the intention to please the customer.
Option B: By definition, gold plating entails providing extra value to the customer. However, the customer can get more value by prioritizing the product backlog. In such a scenario, the customer expects to get notified when the project team completes all of the iteration backlog items.
Option D: In an adaptive approach, the scope is variable while the project cost and schedule are fixed. Consequently, the customer would not be interested in ending a pre-approved iteration earlier.

stem: A contracted project manager is leading a project using a predictive approach. The project sponsor is disappointed with the progress so far, claiming that a critical deliverable has been overlooked. Although the sponsor approved all project stages to date, they asked the project manager to put the project on hold until they reassess the situation. To reach an agreement, the project manager decided to use arbitration and mediation as: (Select two)

options.A: Dispute resolution techniques
options.B: Coaching techniques
options.C: Assisted negotiation techniques
options.D: Direct negotiation techniques

explanation:
Arbitration and mediation imply reaching an agreement through the intervention of an arbitrator or a mediator.
Option D: When direct negotiation fails to produce a satisfactory result, indirect or assisted negotiation methods like mediation or arbitration should be considered. An arbitrator examines the legal aspect of a dispute while a mediator attempts in good faith to narrow discrepancies. Litigation is another dispute resolution technique that involves going to court as a last resort when every other resolution method fails.
Option B: Arbitration and mediation are not coaching techniques; they’re rather used to help others be more effective and productive at work by setting an example, giving praise, providing constructive criticism, etc.

stem: Shortly after joining a new organization, a project manager noticed a lack of collaboration within the team. What should the project manager do to create a cooperative work environment?

options.A: Conduct soft skills development training
options.B: Opt for a pull-based system for work assignments
options.C: Organize team-building activities
options.D: Adopt an agile work approach

explanation:
Team-building activities foster a cooperative working environment when continuously implemented throughout the project lifecycle and especially in its early stages when barely any relationships among team members are developed.
Option A: Carrying out soft-skills training could improve your team’s ability to better communicate and collaborate, but it’s less effective compared to team-building activities.
Option B: Opting for a pull-based system for work assignments, i.e., a lean or a Kanban method, has the main purpose of improving productivity and decreasing delivery times rather than promoting collaboration.
Option D: Following an agile approach should not be done just to increase collaboration among team members, as the project may not be suitable for such an approach in the first place.

stem: A project manager strives to build a work environment that promotes creativity, innovation, and ideas sharing. They set up regular meetings with the team to discuss project risks and issues. What type of leadership is the project manager applying?

options.A: Transactional
options.B: Interactional
options.C: Transformational
options.D: Laissez-faire

explanation:
Transformational leadership is when the project manager empowers the team by encouraging their ideas and creating an atmosphere that promotes innovation and creativity.
Option A: A transactional leader is in favor of rules and procedures as they rely on the reward and punishment powers to run the team.
Option B: Interactional leadership is a hybrid of transformational and transactional leadership.
Option D: Laissez-faire leaders adopt a hands-off approach by fully trusting and relying on the team to set their own rules and make decisions on their own.

stem: A project manager works for a kitchen equipment manufacturer. Their superiors decided to adopt Lean practices, informing the project manager to start preparing for this transition. What type of power is being used by the project manager’s superiors?

options.A: Legitimate
options.B: Referent
options.C: Expert
options.D: Situational

explanation:
Legitimate power (aka formal, authoritative, or positional) is derived from someone’s position or formal title. The project manager's superiors’ decision stems from their position as there are no indications that they used other forms of power in the described situation.
Option B: Referent power implies a leader’s ability to influence their followers through admiration, respect, or identification with the leader.
Option C: Expert power, however, is based on employees' perception that the leader has a high level of knowledge or a specialized set of skills making him/her an expert.
Option D: Situational power implies being appreciated and respected for stepping up and saving the project or the team in a certain situation.

stem: Match the following techniques with the corresponding description in the table below: Brainstorming - Benchmarking - Focus group - Nominal group

During a retrospective meeting, a development team expressed their desire to get training in Python programming. The project manager was checking some well-known training providers when they found a new provider that offers the same training for really interesting prices. The project manager was hesitant about getting the training from this new provider since he wasn’t sure about the quality. Link the risk response on the left to the correct strategy on the right:

A project has been hampered by many quality issues, putting the project at risk. Which meeting should the project manager conduct with the team to figure out how to avoid or deal with such problems in the future?

options.A: Kick-off
options.B: Lessons learned
options.C: Risk review
options.D: Team building

explanation:
Lessons learned meetings are collaborative retrospective sessions for discussing, documenting, and soliciting feedback about the project's successes and missteps. These meetings are a must for the project team to learn from previous mistakes and improve future processes and projects. Lessons learned meetings should be held whenever needed, to review the way a project has been progressing, note important learnings, and set new ways for amelioration.
Option A: Kick-off meetings are meant for communicating the objectives of the project and ensuring the stakeholders’ commitment to the project.
Option C: Risk review meetings are used to verify the status of existing risks and identify new ones (PMBOK 7th edition, page 180). However, capturing lessons learned from current or closed risks commonly happens in the lessons learned meetings.
Option D: Team building activities aim to increase collaboration among team members.

stem: A project experienced a significant team conflict during the final sprint. Nonetheless, the agile team succeeded in delivering a product that was accepted by the customer. What should the project manager do at the end of the sprint?

options.A: Conduct a retrospective meeting with the team to discuss what happened.
options.B: Meet individually with the involved team members to express concerns regarding their behavior.
options.C: Disregard the conflict since the project is coming to an end.
options.D: Disregard the conflict since the team succeeded in achieving the project goals.

explanation: Even though the project is going to be closed soon, the project manager should hold a retrospective meeting to openly discuss what happened during the last sprint. This allows the agile team to understand what went well and what actions to take in the future to improve work processes and collaboration. Lessons learned is an important process not only for the ongoing project but also for the organization. Thus, the project manager should openly discuss the conflict, rather than disregard it.

stem: During a retrospective meeting, some agile team members stated that it sometimes gets confusing to check who is working on each work item and at what stage they are. What can the project manager do to solve this problem?

options.A: Coach the team on how to be more attentive during the daily standup meeting.
options.B: Guide the team on how to use the Kanban board and update it regularly.
options.C: Send a daily status report to all team members to remove the impediment.
options.D: The project manager shouldn’t do anything since agile teams are self-organizing.

explanation:
In the case of unclear work assignments or work progress, the project manager should help their team by using a Kanban board to display the flow of work (Agile Practice Guide, page 58). A kanban board could be already used, but team members might not be updating it properly; they’re not self-assigning tasks or they’re not moving work items to the right column. The project manager should ensure that all team members know how to properly handle the kanban board.
Option A: It’s also not sufficient to coach the team to pay more attention during standups, as it’s difficult to keep in mind the status of all items throughout the day, thus an up-to-date information radiator is needed.
Option C: Even though the problem raised by the team is considered an impediment, it’s not practical for the project manager to solve it by sending a daily status report to everyone.
Option D: Self-organizing teams work autonomously by assuming responsibility for achieving the product increment. However, they still need the project manager's help to adjust work processes and support them so that they can focus on achieving deliverables without interruptions or hindrances.

stem: The project team has been suffering from low morale since the departure of a key project stakeholder, who was a big support and motivation source for them. What should the project manager do first?

options.A: Understand the team’s needs and what motivates them
options.B: Perform team-building activities to strengthen team bonds
options.C: Try to prevent the departure of the key stakeholder
options.D: Set objectives and encourage the team to attain them

explanation:
The project manager should first identify the incentives of their team members. Knowing what each team member needs will help the project manager provide them with the necessary conditions to reach their potential, create a productive work environment, and keep them encouraged in the long run.
Option C: In most cases, the project manager cannot prevent the departure of a stakeholder if they decide to. Instead, the project manager should set a long-term motivation policy to avoid having their team’s morale depend on the presence of certain members or factors.
Options B & D: Setting objectives or performing team-building activities won’t probably solve this team’s issue since they might be missing other motivational factors that the key stakeholder was providing, such as recognition for instance.

stem: In order to ensure that the agile team is cross-functional, a project manager hires a new team member who is more inclined towards testing tasks. After a few days, the new member informs the project manager that he is unable to do his work properly because he doesn’t have the necessary permission to access part of the code. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Ask the team member to raise the issue during the retrospective meeting.
options.B: Tell the team member to adjust the acceptance criteria of the pending tasks and then inform the product owner.
options.C: Explain to the team member that he cannot access the whole code due to security restrictions.
options.D: Reach out to the appropriate stakeholder to either confirm or update the team member’s privilege.

explanation:
Being a servant leader, the project manager should reach out to the appropriate stakeholder in order to verify why the new member doesn’t have access to that portion of the code.
Option A: Retrospective meetings are set up to improve processes rather than remove impediments.
Option B: If the new member’s permission can’t be changed, the project manager should explain this to them and to the product owner in order to update the tasks’ acceptance criteria.
Option C: The access denial could be for security reasons, or because the concerned stakeholder is unaware of the nature of the new member’s duties. In an Agile work environment, a project manager should listen to their team members and act to solve the impediments they’re facing.

stem: Mid-sprint, an agile team encountered too many impediments to the point it became impossible to produce any working increments by the end of the sprint. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Cancel the sprint.
options.B: Proceed with resource-leveling or smoothing.
options.C: Ask the development team to work on the less difficult work items first.
options.D: Continue supporting the development team even though the sprint goal will not be achieved.

explanation:
In agile, the project manager should be a servant leader. Therefore, the right course of action in the described scenario is to support the development team by helping them remove existing and new impediments, regardless of whether they can achieve the sprint goal or not.
Option A: The project manager cannot cancel the sprint either, since it’s up to the product owner to make such a decision.
Option B: Resource leveling or smoothing are two schedule compression techniques used in a predictive work environment.
Option C: The project manager should not dictate what the agile team should work on during the sprint.

stem: A product owner initiates some preliminary work before the actual start of the project. All of the following items can be defined during this stage, except:

options.A: Baselined product backlog
options.B: Product roadmap
options.C: Product vision statement
options.D: Release plan

explanation:
There are no baselines in agile since the scope is variable by nature. Baselining is used in the predictive approach to refer to a finalized plan (cost, schedule, scope, etc.) that would be followed during project execution and used for evaluating the actual performance.
Options B, C, D: Before the actual start of the project, the product owner can work on the product vision statement, product roadmap, product backlog, and release plan.

stem: When an agile team was discussing the technical choices of their new project, a senior team member recalled a similar past project that went through some big challenges and ended up being over budget and behind schedule. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Look for the performance details of the mentioned past project in the Organizational Process Assets (OPAs).
options.B: Look for the performance details of the mentioned past project in the Enterprise Environmental Factors (EEF).
options.C: Look for the performance details of the mentioned past project in the issue log.
options.D: Since the mentioned past project followed a predictive approach, its performance details are irrelevant.

explanation:
Organizational Process Assets (OPAs) include organizational processes and procedures, and corporate knowledge base. To know more about the past project’s performance, the project manager could check the concerned project files such as its scope, schedule, cost, and quality baselines, in addition to its administrative documentation, stakeholder register, issue log, and any other relevant documents. Option B: You cannot find the details of the past project’s performance in the Enterprise Environmental Factors (EEF) since the latter represent the conditions that have an influence on the project but are beyond the team’s control.
Option C: OPAs form the corporate knowledge base, and only checking the issue log might not be sufficient to figure out why the previous project went through a lot of difficulties.
Option D: Even though the new project is agile and the previous one is predictive, it’s recommended to take advantage of its documented lessons learned. Eventually, the challenges that the previous project went through might not be even linked to its adopted approach.

stem: In the project initiation phase, the sponsor asked the project manager to provide an approximate cost estimate for the project by the end of the day. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Create the product backlog items, estimate how many iterations are required to complete the items, and then sum up the cost estimate of each iteration.
options.B: Create the WBS and sum up the cost estimate of each work package.
options.C: Create the cost management plan.
options.D: Provide an estimate based on similar past projects.

explanation:
Since the sponsor requested the cost estimate on short notice, in an early stage of the project with little to no information available to conduct cost estimations, the most practical method for the project manager to respond to the sponsor’s query is to rely on similar past projects’ data to estimate their current project cost. This entails using analogous estimating to calculate the project costs based on the known costs of a similarly completed project. Along with historical data, this technique relies on the project manager’s expert judgment.
Option A: The only person responsible for creating the product backlog items is the product owner, so the first option can’t be realized by the project manager.
Option B: Developing the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) is not an option too, since it requires the project team’s involvement in the process and it’s improbable for it to be done in one day.

stem: In one of the project’s initial meetings, a stakeholder informed the project manager that the video editing software they plan to develop should include a free subscription plan. They explained that this plan should only allow users to edit videos of less than 5 minutes and that all of their exported videos should be watermarked. Where should this information be captured? (Select two)

options.A: Project charter
options.B: Product backlog
options.C: Project scope statement
options.D: Scope management plan

explanation:
Since the described scenario does not include any indication as to which approach is being used for the project implementation, both possibilities should be considered: If it’s an adaptive approach, then the stakeholder requirements should be incorporated into the product backlog. All product features, changes, bug fixes, and all other types of activities that the team should work on to deliver the final outcome should all be added to the product backlog. However, if the project is following a predictive approach, then the communicated requirements should be included in the project scope statement. This document should comprise all project scope elements such as requirements, assumptions, acceptance criteria, etc.
Option A: The project charter is the document that officially authorizes the existence of the project, and it only includes a high-level description of the project rather than detailed requirements or features.
Option D: The scope management plan describes how the scope will be defined, developed, monitored, controlled, and validated, rather than what’s in the scope.

stem: At the end of a sprint retrospective, a team member stated that the meeting output was almost the same as the previous ones and suggested canceling it or at least reducing its frequency. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Extend the sprint timebox in order to allow for more improvements to be discussed in the retrospective.
options.B: Reduce the frequency of retrospectives to once every two sprints.
options.C: Go with voting, and if all team members agree, then skip retrospectives.
options.D: Keep the same frequency of retrospectives and reflect on how to make them more relevant and actionable.

explanation:
The sprint retrospective is one of the main scrum events, which aims to help the team adjust and improve their work processes over time. The project manager has to better facilitate the meeting, engage team members, solicit and collect more feedback, check various metrics, and use different investigation techniques such as the why-why method to help them take future actionable measures accordingly.
Option A: Extending the sprint timebox denotes smoothing the problem rather than trying to solve it.
Options B & C: The project manager should not cancel the retrospective meeting nor reduce its frequency. Instead, the project manager should reflect on why the retrospective meeting is not driving the intended value to the team.

stem: A project manager selected a seller to provide certain services. Both parties agree to use a Fixed Price Incentive Fee contract (FPIF). What should be defined next? (Select two)

options.A: The extra financial incentive the seller will get and when they will get it.
options.B: How much the seller will get for their predetermined services.
options.C: What hourly, daily, or weekly rate the seller will charge.
options.D: What legitimate costs will be reimbursed by the buyer.

explanation:
The Fixed Price Incentive Fee contract (FPIF) implies that the buyer pays the seller a predetermined fixed fee, plus a bonus if the seller meets a defined set of performance criteria (PMBOK 7th edition, page 335).
Option C: In Time & Materials contracts (T&M), the two parties discuss and set the seller’s hourly, daily, or weekly rate.
Option D: In Cost-Reimbursable contracts (CR), the two parties determine which legitimate costs are to be reimbursed by the buyer.

stem: A scrum master is facilitating a retrospective meeting when a team member suggested changing the sprint timebox from three weeks to two weeks. What should the scrum master do?

options.A: Investigate the cause behind the team member’s suggestion to tailor the process.
options.B: Accept the implementation of any suggestion provided by self-organizing team members.
options.C: Decline the team member’s suggestion since it can reduce the team’s velocity.
options.D: Decline the team member’s suggestion since the sprint timebox is set at the beginning of the project and should never be changed.

explanation:
The scrum master should investigate the cause behind the team member’s suggestion to tailor the process. This might reveal other problems that the team is facing that can be fixed by taking a different action rather than changing the sprint timebox.
Option B: The scrum master’s role is to create and maintain good working processes. Therefore, they should examine and challenge new ideas along with the team members before moving on with their implementation.
Option C: Often, the higher the risk and the unpredictability, the shorter the sprint should be. Consequently, rejecting or accepting such a decision should not be based on the team’s velocity.
Option D: Changing the sprint timebox is possible during the project, but it should not be frequently done. Such a decision should be made thoroughly and should involve the product owner too since the scrum events’ frequency will be changed too.

stem: During one of the meetings with their remote team, a project manager was not able to clearly hear a particular team member. At first, the project manager thought that it was an internet or equipment issue. But when asked, the team member turned off their cooling fan and the voice became more clear. What kind of knowledge is being used by the team member to fix the problem? (Select two)

options.A: Implicit knowledge
options.B: Explicit knowledge
options.C: Codified knowledge
options.D: Tacit knowledge

explanation:
Tacit knowledge, aka implicit knowledge, is the know-how embedded knowledge that the team member acquires through experience, insights, intuitions, etc.
Option B: Unlike explicit knowledge, this type of knowledge is difficult to extract and codify.

stem: A project manager is assigned to lead a huge construction project. When conducting procurements, the project manager wanted to ensure that all potential providers fully and clearly understand the project procurement requirements and specifications. How can the project manager achieve this?

options.A: Conduct face-to-face meetings with each seller
options.B: Conduct a negotiation meeting with each seller
options.C: Conduct a virtual meeting with each seller
options.D: Conduct a bidder conference

explanation:
The best way to clearly explain a project’s procurement needs and how the whole process is going to take place is through a bidder conference. This event allows all potential providers to get a better common understanding of the project as well as clarifications to any of their inquiries, allowing them to submit properly prepared proposals. Bidder conferences ensure that all sellers have an equal chance to win the contract.
Options A & C: Individual or virtual meetings contradict the conference's main goal, along with being less practical and efficient.
Option B: Negotiation meetings are conducted with the selected provider to discuss their contract terms.

stem: A stakeholder added a user story to the product backlog. The user story seemed clear to the scrum team. However, during execution, the assigned member gets confused about one of its implementation scenarios. What should the team member do in this case?

options.A: Ask the stakeholder for clarification.
options.B: Ask the product owner for clarification.
options.C: Convey the confusion to the scrum master, who will help get clarification from the product owner.
options.D: Wait for the next standup meeting to report the issue to the scrum master or product owner if they do attend the meeting.

explanation:
During sprint execution, the product owner should be available to respond to questions raised by the development team.
Option A: The product owner represents the customer and stakeholders, which means that the development team should refer only to the product owner if they have any inquiries.
Option C: Since the blocker concerns the clarification of a user story, the development team can reach out directly to the product owner without the intermediation of the scrum master. In agile, the development team is self-organizing, thus they’re responsible for ensuring the achievement of the sprint work.
Option D: Waiting till the next standup meeting to get clarifications is not proactive and can reflect a lack of ownership.
