stem: During the planning phase, the project manager speculated that there would be no changes in the composition of the project steering committee. But, since any change could be very critical to the project, the project manager assigned a team member to monitor for triggers. Where should the name of the person responsible for monitoring the steering committee be recorded?

options.A: Risk register
options.B: Issue log
options.C: Change log
options.D: Stakeholder register

explanation:
A risk register contains a list of all identified risks, their description, planned responses, probability, impact, risk owner, etc. (PMBOK 7th edition, page 185). In the described scenario, the change in the composition of the steering committee is considered a risk and the name of the person responsible for managing it should be noted in the risk register.
Option B: Once the risk occurs, it becomes an issue. Since the described situation doesn’t involve any issues yet, the issue log is not the Correct Answer.
Option C: The situation doesn’t involve any change requests either. Therefore, a change log is not the right option.
Option D: The stakeholder register includes information about the project stakeholders and their classification. Unlike the stakeholder engagement plan, the stakeholder register doesn’t contain action items for when, how, and who should monitor and engage stakeholders.

stem: A senior software engineer has recently been assigned to manage a project using the Agile approach. To ensure the successful delivery of the project, the project manager should first:

options.A: Identify all riskswith the team
options.B: Determine all of the sprints’ activities with the team
options.C: Define the project success criteria with the sponsor
options.D: Define quality metrics with the sponsor

explanation: To ensure the successful delivery of the project, the project manager should first define success criteria with the sponsor. Agreeing upon the project’s success criteria will reduce the possibilities of its failure and reinforce its success odds. When determining the project success criteria, you should avoid using unclear and general terms and focus on being precise and clear. It’s recommended to be specific by saying, for instance: “the product should be completed by November 30th” instead of saying “The product should be completed as soon as possible”.

stem: In order to ensure that the project is performed in accordance with the organization’s requirements, the project manager carries out a tailoring process. Under this context, Tailoring is:

options.A: The knowledge and practices which are applicable to most projects in most cases.
options.B: The application of a set of knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to the project activities in order to meet its requirements.
options.C: The selection of the appropriate processes, inputs, tools, techniques, and life cycle phases for managing a project.
options.D: The application of knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques needed for meeting a program's requirements.

explanation:
Tailoring involves the selection of the appropriate processes, related inputs and outputs, techniques, and life cycle phases in order to manage a project (PMBOK 7th edition, page 6).
Option B: Project management is the application of a set of knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to project activities to meet the project requirements.
Option D: Program management is the application of knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to meet the program requirements.

stem: A project member notices that certain members of the team confuse projects and operations and oftentimes consider operations to be ongoing projects. Therefore, the project manager explains that there's no such thing as an ongoing project, emphasizing the difference between a project and an operation by defining operations as:

options.A: An undertaken temporary endeavor to make a distinctive product, service, or result.
options.B: The application of a set of skills, knowledge, tools, and techniques in a project to meet its requirements.
options.C: A collection of programs that have been grouped to achieve strategic business goals.
options.D: Ongoing endeavors that generate repetitive outputs.

explanation: Operations are ongoing endeavors that produce repetitive outputs. Operations are the continuous execution of activities according to an organization’s procedures to produce the same result or a recurrent service. Operations are permanent in nature as they involve all of the common business functions: production, manufacturing, and accounting are examples of operations.

stem: An organization launches a construction project of a new commercial building in a bustling urban area. Due to certain circumstances, there were delays in the project activities. As a result, the completion date should be pushed back by ten days. While analyzing the impact of this delay, the project manager noticed that one of the identified project risks has slightly increased, but it remains within acceptable limits. What should the project manager do next? (Select two)

options.A: Submit a change request to update the project schedule.
options.B: Update the sprint backlog to reflect the delayed work.
options.C: Hold a meeting to review the impact of the identified risk
options.D: Capture the change in a project status report and communicate it to key stakeholders.

explanation:
The project manager should capture the change in a project status report to communicate it in the next status meeting to ensure that all stakeholders are aware of the delay and the impact it has on the project. It will also allow the project manager to discuss any necessary adjustments to the project plan and risk response strategies with the team. A status meeting is a regularly scheduled event to exchange and analyze information about the current progress of the project and its performance (PMBOK 7th Edition, page 180). Addressing risk at weekly status meetings ensures that risk management remains relevant. These meetings can be used to identify new risks as well as identify changes to existing risks (PMBOK 7th Edition, page 127).
Option A: While submitting a change request to update the project schedule may be necessary, it is not the immediate next step in this scenario.
Option B: Updating the sprint backlog is not relevant in this context as it is a term used in Agile methodology, which may not be applicable to this construction project.
Option C: Reviewing the risk has been already done.

stem: An Agile team wants to examine the visual overview of all of the product’s required features and functionality. What should the project manager suggest the team review?

options.A: Themes
options.B: Epics
options.C: Product backlog
options.D: Story map

explanation:
A story map is used by the agile team to get a visual overview of the product development “Big Picture” including an outline of its features and functionalities (PMBOK 7th edition, page 285).
Options A & B: Themes and epics only represent high-level requirements with no specification of the exact features that will be developed.
Option C: The Product Backlog lists all of the product’s required features and functionalities, but they’re not displayed visually.

stem: A project manager takes over a project that's fallen behind schedule. The project manager holds a meeting to consult with the team and decide on the appropriate course of action to bring the project back on track. Team members seek the project manager’s guidance on what tasks they should focus on next. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Refer to the WBS Dictionary as it describes work packages and acceptance criteria.
options.B: Review the project schedule, Responsibility Assignment Matrix (RAM), and the resource calendar.
options.C: Break down the project scope into smaller work packages.
options.D: Prioritize the product backlog to provide direction to the team on what they should be working on next.

explanation:
Along with the project schedule, the project manager should check the Responsibility Assignment Matrix (RAM) and the resource calendar. RAM is used to show project resources their assignment to each work package (the “what”). The resource calendar, on the other hand, is used to show the availability of resources (PMBOK 7th Edition, page 189).
Option A: The WBS dictionary does not include any information about team members' assignments and what they should tackle next.
Option C: The project manager took over the project in its execution phase, meaning that the scope had already been broken down into smaller work packages.
Option D: The project is most probably following a predictive approach since the scenario mentions schedule issues, and even if it’s following an agile approach, it’s not up to the project manager to prioritize the product backlog since that falls under the product owner’s responsibilities.

stem: During the process of hiring an electrical engineer, a project manager only conducted one behavioral interview. Later on, the project manager discovered that the candidate’s technical skills did not meet the job requirements. Therefore, the project manager decided that going forward, the recruitment process would include a technical test and an additional technical interview. What risk response strategy did the project manager apply?

options.A: Mitigate
options.B: Accept
options.C: Transfer
options.D: Avoid

explanation:
In the described scenario, hiring an unqualified engineer is the risk. Since they were aware of this risk, the project manager took measures to mitigate it. Mitigation involves decreasing the probability of a risk occurrence, or lowering its impact when it does occur (PMBOK 7th edition, page 123).
Option D: Even with the addition of a technical test and an interview, there is still a chance that the candidate might not meet the job requirements (the test could be too easy or generic for instance), that’s why “Avoid” can’t be the right answer.

stem: A project manager was asked to lead a project of a flight booking website development. The airline requested that the website should be able to support one thousand visitors per hour. This condition is also known as a(n): (Select two)

options.A: Requirement
options.B: Scope
options.C: Acceptance criterion
options.D: Deliverable

explanation:
The condition of supporting one thousand visitors per hour is considered a requirement and an acceptance criterion for the project. A requirement is defined as “a condition or capability that is necessary to be present in a product, service, or result to satisfy a business need.” (PMBOK Guide 7th edition, page 82).
Option B: The project scope represents the overall amount of work required to achieve the project’s main objectives.
Option D: Acceptance criteria are conditions required to be met before deliverables are accepted. This condition cannot be considered a deliverable or scope on its own. Deliverables refer to quantifiable products or services that must be delivered by the end of the project, i.e., the flight booking website.

stem: In order to gather end-user feedback, a senior project manager of an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) project discusses several ideas with the project team and then they draw the following diagram. What tool are they using?

options.A: Mind map
options.B: Affinity diagram
options.C: Decision tree
options.D: Data representation

explanation:
The project manager and their team used the mind mapping technique. In a mind map, several options are discussed and then visually organized.
Option B: This diagram is not an affinity diagram as it does not classify a large number of ideas into groups.
Option C: The illustrated diagram is not a decision tree because it doesn’t display or help the team choose the best decision among the different alternatives for gathering end-user feedback.
Option D: Options A, B, and C are all data representation methods, which makes option D “Data representation” too generic to be considered the Correct Answer.

stem: During the project execution, a team member informs the project manager that the electronic equipment used in the project is no longer functioning due to the excessively hot weather. What should the project manager do to solve the problem? (Select three)

options.A: Identify the problem
options.B: Analyze the problem
options.C: Prevent the problem
options.D: Check the solution

explanation:
The project manager should use methodical steps to perform problem-solving. These steps include: ● Identifying or specifying the problem. ● Defining the problem and breaking it into smaller manageable problems. ● Investigating by collecting data. ● Analyzing to detect the root cause of the problem. ● Solving by choosing the suitable solution. ● Checking the implemented solution to determine whether the problem has been fixed or not.
Option C: Preventing the problem is not correct because the problem already took place in the described scenario.
Option E: After evaluating the solution, it can either be kept or replaced if found ineffective.

stem: A project manager is leading a high-risk project that has recently suffered from fluctuating performance and a high defect rate. During a meeting, the sponsor asks for an overview of work performance and where the project is currently standing. Which of the following documents should the project manager send to the sponsor?

options.A: Quality report
options.B: Status report
options.C: Risk report
options.D: Project management plan

explanation:
The status report is a work performance report that includes information on the project's progress and status (PMBOK 7th edition, page 190). A status report can include information about Earned Value (EV), trend lines and forecasts, reserve burndown charts, defect and risk summaries, etc.
Options A & C: Even though the project is at high risk and is encountering quality issues, the sponsor didn’t explicitly request a detailed risk or quality report. The sponsor asked for work performance information to help them gain insight into the project situation and make better decisions.
Option D: The project management plan is not a reporting document; it’s a planning document that is elaborated in the project planning phase.

stem: Astral Bank is well-known for offering excellent online services to its customers. As part of their new project, customers will be able to electronically submit a loan request. Three weeks into project execution, the project manager discovers that an important resource has been over-allocated. This project needs:

options.A: Resource leveling
options.B: Resource smoothing
options.C: Resource calendar
options.D: Resource loading

explanation:
Resource leveling is the process of balancing resource use in order to address resource over-allocation. Resource smoothing, on the other hand, is performed to achieve a more consistent resource utilization over a period of time.
Option B: Even though resource leveling and resource smoothing are both resource optimization techniques, they are used for different reasons. If the Astral Bank project should not exceed certain predeﬁned resource limits, then smoothing would be the right technique to use. A
Option C: Resource calendar showcases team members’ availability.
Option D: Resource loading is the total assigned hours of work divided by the number of hours required to complete it. In the described scenario, the key resource is over-allocated, so their load is over 100%. The project manager could use a resource calendar and resource loading as tools and techniques to help them achieve resource-leveling.

stem: An experienced project manager never initiates a project without conducting a kick-off meeting. What’s the purpose of conducting such a meeting?

options.A: Informing and engaging stakeholders to ensure their commitment
options.B: Obtaining approval to proceed with project execution
options.C: Ensuring the allocation of the required project resources
options.D: Reassuring the stakeholders that execution is on track

explanation:
A project kickoff meeting is an opportunity to get the project team, sponsor, and stakeholders all on the same page. Its purpose is to communicate the objectives of the project, ensure the team’s commitment to the project, and explain the roles and responsibilities of each stakeholder (PMBOK 7th edition, page 179). In a large project, the kick-off meeting is usually associated with the end of the planning phase and the start of project execution. However, for small projects, this meeting can take place shortly after initiation, in the Planning Process Group.
Option B: It’s an informational rather than a decisional meeting, which means that the project manager doesn’t seek approval to proceed with the execution during this meeting.

stem: A product owner selected a number of user stories with a total of 110 points for the next release. Knowing that the team’s velocity is 20 story points, what’s the estimated duration to complete the release?

options.A: 5 sprints
options.B: 5.5 sprints
options.C: 6 sprints
options.D: It’s not possible to calculate the estimated number of sprints to complete a release in Agile

explanation: A release of 110 story points takes 6 sprints to be completed by a team that has 20 story points’ velocity. Even though dividing 110 by 20 equals 5.5 sprints, the number of iterations should be an integer since the predetermined timebox of a sprint should not be changed. In Scrum, it’s possible to calculate the estimated number of sprints as long as the velocity of the team and the estimation of the workload are known. But, you need to keep in mind that this is an estimation rather than a commitment since changes could happen along the way.

stem: To see where each team member stands regarding a certain decision, a project manager uses the Fist of five voting technique. When the team starts voting, one member holds up five fingers. What does this mean?

options.A: The team member wants to intervene in order to further discuss the decision.
options.B: The team member is totally against the decision.
options.C: The team member totally supports the decision.
options.D: The team member wants to refrain from taking part in the voting.

explanation: The Fist of five or Fist to five is a voting technique that agile teams use to help them achieve consensus during decision-making meetings or sessions. This method is used as follows: The facilitator states the decision or action the team is going to vote on and then asks each one of the attendees to hold up a number of fingers that corresponds to their level of support for the stated decision. A closed fist signifies full objection whereas five fingers mean full support for the decision. Until everyone holds up three or more fingers, the voting goes through multiple rounds to achieve consensus.

stem: A product owner who’s new to the agile approach created the following user story: “As a customer, I want a new functionality so that I can achieve a 50% increase in sales”. The project manager found the user story to be deficient. So, they reached out to the product owner to explain to them that:

options.A: The user story should follow a common structure
options.B: The user story should be specific and testable
options.C: The user story should not include financial values
options.D: The user story should be time-bounded

explanation:
The user story written by the product owner is not specific and cannot be tested. Even if it’s written in a user story format it’s vague and unclear. The product owner must specify what new functionality they were looking to develop.
Option C: It’s possible to include financial values in a user story as long as they contribute to making it more clear and more understandable.
Option D: A goal can be time-bound, i.e., a SMART goal, but a user story is not bounded by time.

stem: A project manager is examining the investment efficiency of two potential projects. Knowing that the discount rate is unknown, what should the project manager do?

options.A: Select the project with the highest ROI
options.B: Select the project with the lowest ROI
options.C: Select the project with the highest NPV
options.D: Select the project with the lowest NPV

explanation: Calculating a project’s Net Present Value (NPV) requires knowing its discount rate (i): Net Present Value (NPV) = Future payment (F) / [ (1 + Discount rate (i) ) ^ number of periods in the future the cash flow is (n) ]. Since this is not an option in the described scenario, the project manager should rely on the Return On Investment (ROI) and pick the project with the highest value.

stem: A project manager is leading an agile project. Their daily 10-minute standup is at 9 am. In the last meeting, the project manager noted a 5-minute delay. Then, the team spent another 5 minutes chit-chatting before they actually started the meeting. After the standup, two team members stayed in the meeting room for another 5 minutes discussing an issue that had surfaced the day before. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Request from the team to come to the meeting on time
options.B: Request from the team to stop chit-chatting
options.C: Request from the team to leave the meeting room after the standup
options.D: Change the standup duration to 15 minutes

explanation:
Requesting the team to come on time helps maintain discipline and respect for the meeting's timebox.
Option B: After addressing the punctuality issue, the project manager can work on reducing or controlling chit-chatting.
Option C: Nothing wrong with the behavior of the team members who decided to dedicate another quick meeting to deep dive into a particular issue, which permits to keep the standup meeting focused and concise.
Option D: The scenario doesn’t include factors that could lead to a change in the standup duration.

stem: After facing multiple quality issues, the project manager decided to identify top-priority defects by applying the 80/20 rule (aka the Pareto Chart). What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Find out the impact of each quality issue
options.B: Find out the frequency of each quality issue
options.C: Find out the urgency of each quality issue
options.D: Find out the cause of each quality issue

explanation: A Pareto diagram is a histogram that ranks issues from the ones with the highest frequency to the ones with the lowest frequency. The diagram is created according to Pareto’s Law, which states that 80 percent of the problems come from 20 percent of the issues (also known as the 80/20 rule).

stem: A project manager is leading a project using an adaptive approach. During the sprint review, the product owner asks for an acceptance document to sign off in order to demonstrate their approval of the deliverables. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Create an acceptance document and share it with the product owner to sign off.
options.B: Ask the product owner to create a task in the product backlog and prioritize it, so that the development team can create the acceptance document.
options.C: Ask the product owner to create the acceptance document and sign it off.
options.D: Inform the product owner that an acceptance document is unnecessary.

explanation: A sprint review is conducted to demonstrate the accomplished work, solicit feedback, and foster collaboration rather than seeking formal approval through the sign-off of an acceptance document (Essential Scrum by Rubin, Kenneth S, page 372). Besides, formal approvals are more common in predictive environments.

stem: A project manager is leading a team that is not familiar with the adaptive approach. After several weeks, the project has reached a point where there is an accumulation of Work In Progress (WIP). What should the project manager do to figure out whether the team is properly following procedures?

options.A: Perform a process evaluation
options.B: Review the notes of the previous retrospective meetings
options.C: Check the Kanban board
options.D: Check relevant Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

explanation:
Process evaluation involves quality assurance activities and process audits to ensure procedures and processes are being followed and are generating the intended outcomes (PMBOK 7th edition, page 72).
Option B: Process evaluation can also include reviewing the notes of the previous retrospective meetings as they can reflect the type of issues that were encountered in the past and how they were handled. Therefore, process evaluation involves more than just reviewing the previous retrospective meetings’ notes.
Options C & D: KPIs and the Kanban board can only determine whether WIP is beyond the acceptable level, without identifying the causes. Finally, process evaluation can take place during a retrospective meeting or a lessons learned session, and it can require further investigation that could go beyond those meetings.

stem: An organization asked the project manager to send a report on the cost of quality. The report stated that the total cost was $30,000, detailed as follows: According to the above table, how much is the appraisal cost of the project?
explanation: Appraisal costs, also known as inspection costs, are part of the Cost of Conformance as they represent the costs of identifying defective products before they are delivered to clients. This comprises testing, inspecting, auditing, evaluating, and measuring the deliverables, product, or service the project is producing. Appraisal costs are set up to implement a series of activities to determine work results’ degree of conformance to quality requirements. This means that the project appraisal cost involves inspection costs which are $5,000. Training falls under prevention activities. Rework and scrap costs, on the other hand, are part of the Internal Failure Costs, whereas Warranty charges fall under External Failure Costs.

stem: Mid-project, a project manager is notified by the information security department that they just came to know about the design changes that were made lately. The information security department also expressed their concern about these changes’ compliance with the organization’s standards since they did not take part when these changes were made. What should the project manager do to overcome this issue?

options.A: Undo all design changes since the information security department wasn’t involved in the process.
options.B: Allow the information security department team to attend all of the following daily stand-ups to ensure all made changes comply with security requirements.
options.C: Ask the information security department to raise the issue with the product owner.
options.D: Conduct a meeting with the information security department to go over all design changes and ensure compliance with the organization’s standards.

explanation:
The project manager should first try to resolve the issue through collaboration by conducting a meeting with the information security department to go over the design changes and implement the appropriate process to ensure compliance with security requirements.
Option A: If certain design changes are found to be critical and unfixable, then those should be reverted.
Option C: The product owner could be involved in the problem resolution process, but transferring the issue to them wouldn’t work since compliance with the organization’s standards requires understanding security concerns and setting up the appropriate processes by the project manager and their team.
Option B: Standup meetings are used for daily work synching between team members, not for examining changes.

stem: During the sprint review of the project’s final iteration, the product owner expressed their satisfaction with the product and described it as “fit for purpose”. However, a senior team member stated that another iteration is needed to fix some bugs and improve the user experience. The sponsor, who is also attending the meeting, said that further work on the product will resume if more funding is received in the next quarter. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Close the project, but keep one developer to fix any major bugs.
options.B: Keep the project open since work could be resumed in the next quarter.
options.C: Continue work on fixing bugs to satisfy the client, then close the project.
options.D: Release all resources.

explanation:
Since the client requested the project closure, even though they are aware of the bugs and the required improvements, the project manager should proceed with the decision.
Option A: Properly closing the project entails releasing all resources.
Option B: Continuing work on bugs after the project closure is inappropriate.
Option C: Working on bugs to satisfy the client is considered gold plating. A project cannot be kept open until receiving new funding. It should be closed and, when funding is obtained, a new project should be launched to fix bugs and do whatever the customer requires.

stem: The project sponsor informed the project manager that they have doubts about whether the resulting product will satisfy business demands. Therefore, the project sponsor is looking to keep costs to a minimum. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Identify and implement the requirements for making a Minimum Viable Product (MVP).
options.B: Gather all requirements and execute the project using an incremental approach.
options.C: Exclude certain stakeholders from the scope definition process in order to limit requirements.
options.D: Sign a fixed-cost contract with the sponsor to limit project costs.

explanation:
The Minimum Viable Product (MVP) is used to define the scope of the first release by identifying the requirements that would deliver value to customers (PMBOK 7th edition, page 243).
Option B: An incremental approach is not suitable for the described scenario since the client won’t get a usable product until the end of the project.
Option C: It’s not appropriate to exclude certain stakeholders in order to limit requirements. The project manager should involve all stakeholders in the process of collecting and prioritizing product features.
Option D: Finally, a fixed-cost contract will not solve the problem in the described scenario since the main concern of the sponsor is verifying the product’s business demand.

stem: Mid-project, the project manager noticed that stakeholders’ engagement was fading out and felt the need to measure their satisfaction. What tools or techniques could the project manager use? (Select two)

options.A: Net Promoter Score
options.B: Mood chart
options.C: Power/interest grid
options.D: Engagement assessment matrix

explanation:
Stakeholder satisfaction can be measured with surveys or by looking at related metrics such as Net Promoter Score (NPS) and Mood chart (PMBOK 7th edition, page 103). The Net Promoter Score is a numerical measure of the stakeholder’s satisfaction with your product, service, or workplace and their willingness to recommend it to others. The score ranges from -100 to +100. A high promoter score reflects high business loyalty and job satisfaction. Mood charts, on the other hand, are used to track the daily mood of certain key stakeholders, where they can use colors, emojis, or numbers to express how they’re feeling. This method can help the project manager anticipate and identify potential issues and work on improving certain areas, such as in the described scenario where engagement is fading.
Option C: The power/interest grid is created in order to categorize stakeholders based on their power or influence levels and has nothing to do with measuring their satisfaction.
Option D: The Engagement Assessment Matrix is a stakeholder management technique that is used to monitor the engagement levels of stakeholders and therefore identifies involvement issues. This tool might have helped the project manager detect the stakeholders’ engagement problem but it can’t help them figure out satisfaction levels.

stem: A project manager is leading the second phase of a project using a hybrid approach. During the first phase of the project, the project manager faced some challenges with defining the requirements. Therefore, at the beginning of the new phase, the project manager wants to proactively manage stakeholders’ expectations in order to find common ground and diminish any differences. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Send a questionnaire to all of the involved stakeholders in order to determine the project requirements.
options.B: Set up a meeting with each stakeholder to identify their needs.
options.C: Invite all concerned stakeholders to a requirements workshop to develop user stories.
options.D: Conduct a survey of the project’s current users.

explanation:
The project manager wants a way to proactively manage stakeholders’ expectations and find a common ground while collecting requirements for the second phase of his hybrid project. For that, the project manager should invite all concerned stakeholders to a requirements workshop to develop user stories. Facilitating a workshop is the best option in this situation to identify the project requirements and diminish stakeholder differences. The interaction occurring during a workshop can help everyone involved find common ground and reach consensus when it comes to project requirements.
Options A, B, D: Sending a questionnaire, setting up one-on-one meetings, and conducting surveys could help collect data and get insights, but stakeholders should communicate with one another to bridge any disagreements.

stem: To keep up with everything going on with their project, a project manager relies on emails as a medium to communicate with the project team and stakeholders. To write efficient emails, the project manager uses the following techniques, except:

options.A: Brief, right-to-the-point expressions
options.B: Consideration of the reader’s needs
options.C: Words and ideas fluency
options.D: Tone variation

explanation: In order to reduce misunderstandings when using written communication mediums, the project manager can rely on the 5 techniques or the 5Cs of written communication, which represent: Correct grammar and spelling, Concise expression and elimination of excess words, Clear purpose and expression directed to the needs of the reader, Coherent, logical flow of ideas, and Controlled flow of words and ideas. Tone variation is a verbal communication technique.

stem: A customer informed their project manager that they are going to launch a new project and they will assign it to the same product owner of the current ongoing project. How should the project manager react in response to the customer’s decision?

options.A: Ask the customer to reconsider their decision since a product owner should handle one product at a time.
options.B: Ask the customer to reconsider their decision to avoid a conflict of interest situation.
options.C: It’s ok to have the same product owner for both products as long as they can fulfill their duties.
options.D: Ask the customer to add another product owner to the current project as a backup.

explanation: A product should only have one product owner, considering they’re the one responsible for deciding which features to build and in which order (Essential Scrum by Rubin, Kenneth S, page 15). When multiple products are being developed, it’s possible to either have a product owner for each of them or have one product owner for all of them. This depends on the projects’ size as well as other factors such as the connection between projects. But, in all cases, the product owner should fulfill their role and be available to respond to queries from the development teams.

stem: During product validation, a key stakeholder refuses to sign off the acceptance document, claiming that some of the functionalities do not meet their expectations. What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation?

options.A: Involve the key stakeholder during the quality control phase
options.B: Involve the key stakeholder during the project initiation phase
options.C: Involve the key stakeholder during the planning phase
options.D: Involve the key stakeholder during all project phases

explanation: Stakeholders need to get involved early on during project planning and sometimes during the project initiation as well. Key stakeholders should also be involved during the quality control phase so that they can assess the project deliverables and recommend any changes before the official acceptance. Since the concerned key stakeholder is responsible for signing off the acceptance document, their power is considered high. Therefore, stakeholders who are identified to have high power using the power/interest grid should be managed closely and/or kept satisfied throughout the whole project.

stem: While working on identifying risks, a project manager noticed that there was a disagreement among team members concerning the appropriate way to execute an important work item. What can the project manager do to mitigate this risk?

options.A: Outsource the concerned work item.
options.B: Enroll the team in training about the technologies related to executing that work item.
options.C: Let the team self-organize and figure out how to execute the work item.
options.D: Escalate the issue to the functional manager.

explanation:
Providing training on technologies related to the work item will help the team fully understand how it should be executed. This strategy aims to mitigate the risk by reducing conflict between team members.
Options A, C, D: The other options involve avoiding the risk by outsourcing the work item, accepting it by letting the team figure out a solution on their own, or escalating the risk to the functional manager.

stem: A project manager is in charge of a software development project that follows an Agile approach. During the project execution, the project manager receives a request from the customer to alter a requirement. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Block the change request
options.B: Welcome the change request
options.C: Avoid the change request
options.D: Take the change request to the Change Control Board (CCB)

explanation:
Flexibility is one of the most important aspects of the Agile approach; the scope of work can change in response to new requirements. An Agile, adaptive, or change-driven approach encourages collecting feedback from stakeholders on a regular basis.
Option D: Unlike the predictive approach, the Agile approach doesn’t involve a Change Control Board (CCB).

stem: A project manager joins a project to replace the former project manager who has abruptly left the organization. During the first week, they noticed that team members do not trust or support each other's ideas and that the work climate is counterproductive. According to Tuckman's model, at which development stage is this team?

options.A: Adjourning
options.B: Norming
options.C: Forming
options.D: Storming

explanation:
The project manager’s team is in the storming phase. Tuckman’s team development ladder identifies five stages: forming, storming, norming, performing, and adjourning (PMBOK 7th edition, page 166). Storming is the most difficult and critical stage a team can go through. Different personalities emerge during this phase, resulting in conflict and rivalry. At this point, the team's performance will suffer tremendously since their energy is diverted to disputes and arguments.
Option A: In the adjourning phase, tasks are completed, the team breaks up, and members move on to other assignments.
Option B: The norming stage comes after storming; this is when team members begin to work together and trust each other. In the performing phase, teams begin to function as a unit; they get the job done smoothly and effectively without inappropriate conflicts or the need for supervision.
Option C: Forming is the first stage of a team’s development where members start to know each other and form first impressions. Team members usually avoid controversies or conflicts in this phase.

stem: A project manager is in charge of leading a ground-breaking medical research project. During a meeting with the sponsor, the project manager discusses how he’s going to handle the project, explaining that he wants to encourage self-awareness, listening, and coaching. The project manager adds that helping the project team grow is among his top priorities. What type of leadership does the project manager intend to adopt?

options.A: Servant leadership
options.B: Authentic leadership
options.C: Transactional leadership
options.D: Transformational leadership

explanation:
The project manager intends to adopt a servant leadership style. The Agile Practice Guide distinguishes servant leadership with the following characteristics: promoting self-awareness, listening, serving teammates, assisting people in their development and growth, coaching rather than controlling, and promoting security, respect, and trust. Servant leaders prioritize the needs of others, helping them reach their best performance and potential (PMBOK 7th edition, pages 17-18).
Option B: Authentic leaders focus on the self-development of themselves and their followers. Option C: Transactional leaders focus on supervision, organization, and performance, using incentives and penalties as motivation tools.
Option D: Transformational leaders focus on motivation as well as creating an atmosphere of innovation and creativity.

stem: A project manager who works in a national bank decides to use the power/interest grid to plan stakeholder engagement. How should he deal with an interested stakeholder with little authority?

options.A: Monitor
options.B: Manage closely
options.C: Keep informed
options.D: Keep satisfied

explanation:
The project manager should keep stakeholders with high interest and low authority informed. He should proactively plan how to regularly communicate the project status to this group of stakeholders and check in with them to make sure they are not experiencing any issues or problems.
Options A, B, D: The project manager should closely manage stakeholders with high levels of power and interest, keep stakeholders with high power and low interest satisfied, and monitor stakeholders with low levels of power and interest.

stem: A project manager is managing a branding project for a fast-food restaurant chain. During the project, two team members have an argument about a design task. The project manager decides to have a meeting with the two members. Upon discussing the issue, they all come to the conclusion that the best course of action would be outsourcing this activity. Which conflict resolution technique did the project manager use?

options.A: Forcing
options.B: Collaborating
options.C: Compromise
options.D: Smoothing

explanation:
Since the project manager chose to meet with the concerned team members to discuss their conflict and make the best decision accordingly, then the situation implies problem-solving or collaboration, which leads to a win-win situation (PMBOK 7th edition, page 168).
Options A, C, D: Other problem-solving techniques include: - Forcing: which leads to a win-lose situation. - Smoothing: which leads to a yield-lose situation. - Withdrawing: which leads to a lose-leave situation. - Compromising: which leads to a lose-lose situation. Reference: Guan, D. (2007). Conflicts in the project environment. Paper presented at PMI Global Congress 2007.

stem: Organizations often attempt to deliver projects with limited budgets and incomprehensive requirements. An Agile approach can be adopted to address such complexities. However, without proper communication, this approach won’t achieve its goals. Under this context, how should a project manager communicate?

options.A: Informally
options.B: Formally
options.C: Frequently
options.D: Daily

explanation:
Agile frameworks are known for their frequent and straightforward communication where a project manager is continuously checking in with the team to accordingly decide what could be alternatively done to improve the work pace and boost the team’s morale.
Option D: Daily communication should not be confused with daily standup. Daily standup meetings are held by the agile team members who follow a scrum framework. The project manager or scrum master is not required to attend this meeting, but even if they do, the daily standup meeting should not be their only channel of communication with the team.
Options A & B: Whether you adopt a predictive or an adaptive approach for your project, you have to use formal and informal communication according to the situation.

stem: A senior team member expresses his concerns to the project manager about a new member. The senior member believes that the new member lacks the technical proficiency to properly accomplish their assigned work. Having worked together for several years, the project manager has confidence in the senior team member’s judgment. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Release the new team member.
options.B: Nothing should be done since the new team member has already been assigned.
options.C: Provide the new member with training and mentoring.
options.D: Keep the new team member, but reassign their tasks to someone else.

explanation:
The project manager should provide the new member with the needed training and mentoring. When you realize a team member lacks the required competencies or skills, the first step is to use mentorship and training in order to improve their competencies (PMBOK 7th edition, page 18).
Option A: Releasing the team member should be the last resort when every other option fails to put them on track.
Options B & D: Doing nothing or reassigning their tasks to someone else will not help the team member improve their competency; it will only lead to their demotivation and negatively impact the project.

stem: Shortly after starting a new project, a project manager noticed that a team member who was also on the last project was not as productive as she used to be. The project manager invited her to a one-on-one meeting, where she admitted that her frustration was due to the fact that she had expected a performance bonus in the last project, but did not receive it. What should the project manager do first?

options.A: Explain to the team member that performance bonuses are outside of the project manager’s control.
options.B: Escalate the issue to the HR department for further resolution.
options.C: Acknowledge her frustration and provide recognition for her contributions to the last project.
options.D: Explain to her how performance was evaluated and how bonuses were awarded in the last project.

explanation:
Acknowledging her frustration shows empathy, and offering recognition helps to re-engage her in the current project. While the bonus issue may not be within the project manager's control, providing recognition for ongoing work can boost morale and productivity.
Option A: While bonuses could be outside the project manager's control, deflecting responsibility doesn't address the emotional aspect of the team member’s frustration.
Option B: Escalating to HR is possible in case the project manager finds out that the team member deserves a performance bonus. This step could be done after showing empathy, listening to the team member, and reviewing the grounds and the correctness of the bonus decision.
Option D: The project manager should clarify any misunderstanding, but this should be after acknowledging her frustration and providing recognition for her contributions to the last project.

stem: One month into project execution, the project manager notices that the sponsor is always late for their weekly meetings. However, the project manager chooses not to address the sponsor’s behavior. Instead, the project manager documents the frequent tardiness in the meetings’ notes. Which conflict resolution technique is the project manager using?

options.A: Problem-solving
options.B: Smoothing
options.C: Information recording
options.D: Withdrawal

explanation:
The unwillingness to deal with a conflict is referred to as withdrawing. This conflict resolution technique is acceptable when some time to cool off is needed in order to achieve a better understanding of the situation, or when the other party is unassailable or uncooperative (PMBOK 7th edition, page 169).
Option A: The situation does not imply problem-solving since the project manager didn’t point out the issue to the sponsor in order to find a solution.
Option B: The project manager didn’t smooth the conflict either since there was no discussion with the sponsor to diminish their differences.
Option C: Information recording, taking notes, or documenting the situation is not a conflict resolution technique.

stem: A project manager is in charge of an educational project. After analyzing the power level of each of the project’s four stakeholders, the project manager finds out that Monica and Markus have high power, while Ravi and Sergio have low power. For a deeper insight, the project manager created the stakeholder engagement assessment matrix below. Based on this analysis, which stakeholder should be prioritized in terms of engagement?

options.A: Monica
options.B: Markus
options.C: Ravi
options.D: Sergio

explanation:
The priority in engagement should be given to stakeholders with a high level of power (PMBOK 7th edition, page 12). Monica and Markus have high power, but Monica is Neutral, while Markus is unaware. Having an unaware stakeholder with a high level of power is more dangerous than a neutral stakeholder with a high level of power since the first type can cause a lot of trouble when they become aware at a late stage of the project. The project manager should prioritize engaging Markus by sharing the project details with him. Then, they should try to win his support and bring him to the leading level if possible.
Options A & D: Monica and Sergio should be the project manager’s second priority. It’s preferable to have either supportive or leading high-power stakeholders. So, the project manager needs to make more effort to bring Monica to one of these two levels. On the other hand, even though Sergio has low power, the project manager needs to work on moving him out from the resistant level since his level of power can change at any time throughout the project.

stem: An organization in need of accounting software conducts a make-or-buy analysis. The organization decided to go for in-house development since the analysis shows a payback period of fewer than 3 years. However, when acquiring resources, the project manager finds out that the developer's rate included in the make-or-buy analysis is only half the current rate in the market. What should the project manager do first?

options.A: Submit a change request.
options.B: Inform the sponsor about the findings.
options.C: Nothing; as long as the project’s SPI and CPI are on track, this shouldn’t be a problem.
options.D: Update the make-or-buy analysis report.

explanation:
The project manager should notify the sponsor of any identified risks that may impact the business value of the project. Business value measurements are used to ensure that the project deliverables remain consistent with the business case and benefits realization plans. Business value can be financial or non-financial (PMBOK 7th edition, page 102).
Option A: If the sponsor agrees to carry on the project and increase its budget according to the new findings, then a change request should be issued. However, when following an adaptive approach, no change requests, SPI, or CPI are used. In this case, the project manager should inform the sponsor or the product owner about their findings and discuss whether it’s still possible to achieve the project goals or not.
Option C: If the project is following a predictive approach, it can show assuring SPI and CPI, especially at the beginning of its execution. However, since the developer’s rate was underestimated, the project will get off-track in terms of cost later on.
Option D: A make-or-buy analysis is considered a tool for measuring financial business value. The project manager should not update the make or buy analysis report without consulting or referring to the sponsor first. The sponsor can determine whether to continue the investment or not if the payback period turns out to be more than 3 years after updating the make-or-buy analysis.

stem: Two agile teams are working on developing the same product. Team A is made of 5 members and uses 2-week sprints, while Team B involves 4 members and uses 3-week sprints. Team A completed all sprint backlog items with a velocity of 50 story points. Team B, on the other hand, reached 70 story points, without completing all of the sprint’s backlog. Which team has better performance?

options.A: Team A, since they completed all sprint backlog items
options.B: Team A, taking into consideration their velocity, they can achieve 75 story points in a 3-week sprint, which is better than what Team B achieved
options.C: Team B, since they have a better velocity
options.D: Team B, since they achieved more story points with fewer team members

explanation:
The team that has better performance is the team that fulfills its sprint engagement by completing all of its backlog items. This means that the performance of Team A was better than the performance of Team B.
Options B & C: Velocity should not be used to compare teams’ performance.
Option D: Likewise, the number of completed user stories per sprint and team size can not indicate whether a team’s performance is good or not.

stem: During a project status meeting, the project manager updated the sponsor on the project performance by informing them that the SPI is 0.75 and the CPI is 1.05. What does this indicate?

options.A: The project is over budget but on schedule
options.B: The project is within budget but behind schedule
options.C: The project is on schedule and within budget
options.D: The project is behind schedule and over budget

explanation: A Schedule Performance Index (SPI) of less than 1 indicates that the project is behind schedule. A Cost Performance Index (CPI) greater than 1 means that the project is within the predetermined budget.

stem: A product owner and team members have different interpretations of a particular user story. To resolve the disagreement, the project manager suggests the creation of personas. What’s the most probable reason for creating personas?

options.A: To use it as a wireframe to help clarify project outcomes
options.B: To engage stakeholders who don’t know much about the project
options.C: To help the development team empathize with the users of the solution
options.D: To identify and describe real users of the solution

explanation:
A persona is a fictional representation of the ideal potential users of a product or service. This description helps the team understand and empathize with the users’ need for the solution. Thus, the team can better adapt the solution to help and satisfy its users in real-life situations.
Options A & B: Persona does not have a role in stakeholder engagement, nor is it a wireframe for clarifying project outcomes.
Option D: Even though a persona involves a set of real-life characteristics, it does not identify or describe the real users of the solution.

stem: After introducing a new foreign developer to the team, the project manager noticed that a senior team member seemed to be avoiding any interaction with the new developer. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Talk to the senior team member privately to try and find out the reason behind their behavior while making it clear that discrimination is neither tolerated nor accepted.
options.B: Notify the functional manager of the senior team member’s behavior and ask them to take the appropriate disciplinary action.
options.C: Look past the senior team member’s behavior since no conflict between the two has occurred and work seems to be going just fine.
options.D: Address the issue in the next team meeting by scolding the senior team member and lecturing everyone about the importance of an inclusive work environment.

explanation:
The project manager should talk to the senior team member privately to get to know the reason behind their behavior. Besides, the project manager should be clear about not tolerating any kind of discriminating behavior towards the new team member and the potential consequences and disciplinary procedures the senior team member will face in case their behavior persists.
Option B: The project manager should talk directly to the concerned party with no need to escalate the issue to the functional manager at this stage.
Option C: Such behavior should not be ignored, even when it seems to have no tangible impact on work progress.
Option D: It’s not appropriate nor professional to scold a team member in a meeting and in the presence of their colleagues, regardless of their behavior.

stem: After the organization’s recent transition to the agile approach, the project manager expected the project team to become self-organized. However, team members still wait for the project manager to assign them work. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Take a few weeks off to force the team to act on their own
options.B: Mentor the team on how to make their own decisions
options.C: Ensure that the team includes different functional expertise
options.D: Support the team by removing encountered impediments

explanation:
The project manager can help their team get self-organized by mentoring them on how to make their own decisions. This will empower them to pick their own tasks without waiting for assignments or asking for permission or direction from the project manager every time.
Option A: Taking a vacation is a passive approach to dealing with the problem and it won’t solve it since the team will get back to relying on the project manager as soon as they come back.
Option C: Ensuring that the team includes different functional expertise will help the team be cross-functional rather than self-organizing.
Option D: Supporting the team by removing encountered impediments is part of the agile project manager’s duties and won’t help make the team self-organizing.

stem: A project manager is leading a multi-year software project. After a few months, a senior team member started losing motivation and complaining that their assigned work could be easily done by a junior team member. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Incentivize the senior team member by increasing their salary or rate.
options.B: Increase the engagement of the senior team member by holding team-building activities.
options.C: Be proactive and start looking for a replacement for the senior team member.
options.D: Find more challenging tasks for the senior team member to tackle.

explanation:
The reason behind the team member’s demotivation is intrinsic. The senior team member is looking for challenging work and will respond well to stretch goals and problem-solving (PMBOK 7th edition, page 25).
Options A & B: Increasing their salary or holding team-building activities will not help address the original problem.
Option C: Looking for a replacement should be the last resort if all other options fail to motivate the concerned team member.

stem: A project manager is facilitating a meeting attended by his project team as well as key stakeholders to prioritize all product backlog items according to their business value and risk level. Drag and drop each category of items in the right placement in the product backlog:

A project manager is contractually engaged to present a monthly report on what was done the previous month and what preventive measures will be taken the following month. The project manager used to deliver the status update presentation himself, but now that he is on vacation, a team member has volunteered to do the task. Later, the project manager received feedback from key stakeholders saying that the latest presentation was not good. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Advise the team member to never volunteer for tasks that he’s not up to
options.B: Send an email to the team member requesting an explanation and use his reply as proof for potential disciplinary decisions
options.C: Ask the team member what happened with the presentation that resulted in the stakeholders’ dissatisfaction
options.D: Ignore the issue since it only occurred once and it won’t happen again now that the project manager is back from his vacation and will be delivering project status presentations as usual

explanation:
The best way to address this issue is to have an informal discussion with the team member to understand what happened and provide them with the appropriate guidance. Option B: Since the issue is neither severe nor recurrent, it does not necessitate formal communication.
Option A: It’s not appropriate for the project manager to advise the team member not to volunteer again for similar tasks.
Option D: They also shouldn't ignore the situation because it’s their responsibility as the project manager to develop, coach, and mentor their team.

stem: During the last three daily standup meetings with the team, the project manager notices that a new team member is struggling with one of their assigned tasks as he seems to be making no progress towards completing it. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Ask an experienced team member to take over the task.
options.B: Check whether other team members can help their new colleague with the task after the standup meeting.
options.C: Express his disappointment to the new team member and encourage him to make more effort.
options.D: Ask the new team member to check the team ground rules.

explanation:
Asking another team member to help mentor the new member and guide them through getting their task completed and overcoming the challenging aspects of their assignment is the right course of action. Since the member is new and they might lack certain skills or experience dealing with certain types of tasks, they will get the chance to learn and overcome any impediments by collaborating with more experienced team members.
Option A: Assigning someone else to get the task done will only have a bad impact on their self-esteem and motivation and make them miss out on a learning opportunity.
Option C: Similarly, expressing their disappointment at the new member’s performance will do more harm than actually resolving the issue.
Option D: Checking the team ground rules is irrelevant to this situation.

stem: A project manager is leading a project within a functional organization. Halfway through the project implementation, a team member left the organization. What should the project manager do first?

options.A: Collaborate with the functional manager to get a replacement
options.B: Update the project’s resource breakdown structure
options.C: Reassign their workload to the project team member
options.D: Evaluate the impact of the team member’s departure on the project

explanation:
First, the project manager should understand the impact of the team member's departure on the project. It might have a big impact therefore the leaving member needs to be promptly replaced with an experienced member. Or, their departure might have a limited impact and the project can proceed without their contribution.
Options A & C: Based on the evaluation findings, a decision should be taken on whether to get a replacement or reassign the workload.
Option B: The project’s resource breakdown structure should be updated later on to reflect the new changes.

stem: Before starting the project, and after identifying all of the individuals and groups involved or affected by the project, the project manager took a step further by classifying stakeholders according to their level of power, interest, and influence. This step is referred to as:

options.A: Stakeholder analysis
options.B: Stakeholder identification
options.C: Stakeholder monitoring
options.D: Stakeholder engagement

explanation:
Since the question states that stakeholders were already identified and that the project hasn't started yet, stakeholder analysis is the right answer. Stakeholder analysis refers to the classification of all project stakeholders in order to ensure efficient engagement later on.
Option D: Stakeholder engagement takes place in the execution process group and it involves: communicating and collaborating with stakeholders to meet their expectations, addressing issues, and fostering appropriate stakeholder involvement.
Option C: Stakeholder monitoring implies assessing stakeholders’ satisfaction and whether their engagement plan is effective or needs to be updated (PMBOK 7th edition, pages 11-12-14).

stem: A project manager is developing the business case of a green transportation project. To do so, they decide to use the SWOT technique. How should the project manager apply this technique?

options.A: Follow a Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle (PDCA Cycle)
options.B: Assess the business model using expert judgment
options.C: Identify the project's strengths and weaknesses
options.D: Conduct a benefit/cost analysis

explanation:
SWOT stands for Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats. It’s a tool that project managers use to assess the opportunities and threats they might face, as well as their projects’ strengths and weaknesses (PMBOK 7th edition, page 177).
Option A: The PDCA cycle is a quality management technique to control and continuously improve processes and products.
Options B & D: Assessing the project’s business model or conducting a benefit/cost analysis could be part of developing the business case, but both methods have a different purpose from the SWOT technique.

stem: A project manager is managing an online e-learning platform. The project team is following the Scrum framework and every few weeks they release a new version that includes more features, user interface changes, bug fixes, security patches, etc. In order to avoid confusing users with the continuous changes, the project manager decides to make all release information accessible to the platform members under the “News” section on the website. What type of communication does the project manager plan to use?

options.A: Push communication
options.B: Interactive communication
options.C: Pull communication
options.D: Proactive communication

explanation:
Pull communication is a communication type where access to the information is provided, however, the receiver must proactively seek out and retrieve this information. When the communication is solely for informative purposes, pull communication should be used. It will have little to no impact on the project if the recipients do not read it. According to the PMI process groups guide: “Pull communication is used for large complex information sets, or for large audiences, and requires the recipients to access the content at their own discretion subject to security procedures. These methods include web portals, intranet sites, e-learning, lessons learned databases, or knowledge repositories.” (PMI Process groups Guide, page 253)
Option D: PMBOK defined three types of communication: interactive, push, and pull. Proactive communication is a made-up term.

stem: A project manager canceled a Lessons learned review meeting due to time constraints. The potential consequences of this decision might implicate:

options.A: Issues faced through the project could reoccur due to the missed opportunity to identify preventive actions.
options.B: Project management will get more difficult.
options.C: Project cost will be greater.
options.D: The project may not be accepted by the Project Management Office (PMO).

explanation: The knowledge acquired from the process of carrying out a project is referred to as "lessons learned." This covers both the positive and negative aspects. The aim is to replicate good practices and avoid repeating errors. By failing to examine or go over past lessons learned, the project manager risks making the same errors as in previous projects. Therefore, the earlier the lessons are identified and embedded into a project, the more value they will provide. So ideally, a project manager should conduct reviews on an ongoing basis to allow for continuous improvement. Such a review will capture in-depth inputs from the project team, sponsors, stakeholders, etc. Capturing and going over lessons learned on a regular basis helps keep the project on track. In the long term, it will also help organizations continuously develop and enhance the way they conduct projects.

stem: Even though the project management plan was perfectly elaborated, the project manager thinks that unforeseen events could have a big impact on the whole project. What should the project manager do next?

options.A: Identify these events and update the project management plan
options.B: Ensure that a management reserve is allotted
options.C: Discuss these events with the sponsor in order to develop a fallback plan
options.D: Perform a qualitative risk assessment to define the priority of each of these events

explanation: Unforeseen events are “unknown unknowns”, meaning that they cannot be previewed or identified beforehand. Therefore, it is not possible to discuss or prioritize these events. The only action to take against this type of risk is to set up a management reserve to respond to these events when they occur.

stem: During a planning session, a project management team determined that they needed to purchase new IT equipment in November. The project manager thought it would be a good idea to take advantage of Black Friday’s discounts since it takes place in the last week of November. What should the project team do to not miss this opportunity?

options.A: Exploit the opportunity
options.B: Share the opportunity
options.C: Enhance the opportunity
options.D: Accept the opportunity

explanation:
The project team should exploit this opportunity by taking specific actions and preparing the required conditions to take advantage of the opportunity (PMBOK 7th edition, page 220). For example, before Black Friday, the project team can prepare a list of sellers, contact them to verify if they’re planning to have any Black Friday discounts, subscribe to their newsletters to be notified of any opportunities, etc.
Option B: The project team can exploit this opportunity without having to share it with a third party.
Option C: While exploiting the opportunity consists of acting to ensure that it occurs, enhancing it means acting to increase the probability of its occurrence or impact. For instance, the project team can enhance the opportunity by purchasing the needed IT equipment during the last week of November. However, this does not ensure that they’ll find discounts on the equipment they want to purchase, thus they could miss the opportunity.
Option D: Finally, accepting the opportunity without taking any action means that the team can end up buying the equipment at any time during November and they can miss the opportunity, i.e., the Black Friday discounts.

stem: An agile team is working on developing an innovative digital product. The product owner added a user story in the product backlog and noted that it should be implemented in the next release. During a refinement session with the product owner, the development team stated that they are not sure about the user story implementation since it requires particular inputs from the current release. What should the development team do next?

options.A: Further study the different implementation scenarios of the user story.
options.B: Prioritize the user story since it involves a high level of ambiguity and risk.
options.C: Stop spending more time trying to figure out how to implement the user story until they collect more information.
options.D: Give the user story a final estimation based on the current understanding and available information.

explanation:
The agile approach follows Lean principles. Among these principles is “deciding as late as possible”; when it’s difficult to make a decision or plan an activity, you should delay it or postpone it until you have enough information or data for you to be able to make an educated decision. This practice is known as the last responsible moment concept.
Option A: In this case, since determining how to implement the concerned user story requires inputs from the current release, the development team should wait until they are able to know more about these inputs.
Option B: The product owner is the one responsible for prioritizing work. Needless to say, prioritizing user stories should be based on values in addition to their ambiguity or risk.
Option D: Final estimates are usually assigned during sprint planning, or whenever the user story implementation is clearly decided upon.

stem: A project manager is leading a project with remote team members in different geographical areas. During a virtual fortnightly retrospective meeting, the project manager finds out that some members either forgot, missed, or did not fully understand what was discussed in the previous meeting. What should the project manager do? (Select two)

options.A: Ask all team members to try to speak English with an American accent.
options.B: Create a new group norm requiring meeting attendees to raise their hands when they don’t understand something.
options.C: Record meeting sessions and send the recordings to everyone involved.
options.D: Change the meeting frequency to weekly rather than fortnightly so that team members do not forget what has been discussed.

explanation:
To solve the issue, the project manager can create a group norm inciting attendees to raise their hands when they have questions. They can also record meeting sessions and send recordings to all attendees. Raising hands is practical in physical meetings as well as in video conferences. If a team member raises their hand to ask a question and still doesn’t understand a particular point, or if they missed part of the discussion, they can refer back to the recording.
Option A: The project manager cannot force team members to speak with an American accent. If someone has an unclear accent, then the project manager could offer to provide them with training, if the team member is willing, in order to improve their accent.
Option D: The meeting frequency should not be changed just because participants tend to forget meeting outputs. Meeting minutes and recordings are effective tools to address such an issue.

stem: A project manager is leading a software project. A team member is in charge of developing the User Interface (UI). Even though this member is doing a great job, their work pace is way slower than expected, which can cause the whole project to miss its deadline. What should the project manager do first in this situation?

options.A: Delegate some of the team member’s tasks to other team members
options.B: Remove the team member from the project
options.C: Find out the cause of the team member’s slow work pace
options.D: Give the concerned team member other non-critical tasks

explanation:
Before taking any corrective measures, the project manager should determine the underlying cause of the problem.
Option A: If it turns out that the concerned team member is overallocated, it might be better to assign some of their work to other members.
Option B: Regardless of their slow work pace, the concerned team member is doing a great job. Therefore, removing them from the project can have a negative impact on the quality of the deliverables.
Option D: Assigning non-critical tasks to the team member can have a bad impact on their motivation, plus it does not resolve the main problem, i.e. their slow work pace.

stem: Since switching to the agile approach, a project manager has been encouraging their team to be self-organizing by allowing them to decide how to execute their assigned work. What is the main aspect of a self-organizing team?

options.A: It gives more responsibility to the project manager
options.B: It gives more responsibility to the Agile team
options.C: It allows the team to deliver a working product without external dependencies
options.D: It gives team members higher visibility of the product

explanation:
Unlike conventional teams, self-organizing teams do not wait for their supervisors to assign them tasks. Instead, they determine which tasks must be accomplished, prioritize those tasks, and handle their schedules and deadlines on their own. Self-organizing teams tend to have a greater sense of ownership, engagement, and responsibility (PMBOK 7th edition, page 249).
Option C: A Cross-functional team consists of team members with all the needed skills to produce a working product without external dependencies.
Option D: Higher visibility of the product could only be developed by the product owner through backlog refinement.

stem: A project manager works for an organization that uses extrinsic motivators to improve team morale and productivity. What incentives should the project manager offer the team in order to comply with the company’s policy? (Select three)

options.A: Create an “Employee of the month” award
options.B: Offer a $10,000 bonus for the most performant team members
options.C: Allow team members to work on tasks they enjoy
options.D: Praise team members for their hard work

explanation:
Extrinsic motivation is described as actions motivated by external factors such as grades, popularity, money, and praise. This form of motivation arises from external factors, as opposed to intrinsic motivation, which comes from within the person.
Option C: Allowing each team member to work on things that they genuinely love to do presents a form of intrinsic motivation (PMBOK 7th edition, page 24).

stem: Now that the project is nearly finished, a key stakeholder asked the project manager about the project deliverables approval process. The project manager replied that he was confident that the customer would be satisfied with the result. What can ensure the satisfaction of the project’s customer?

options.A: The project’s low running costs.
options.B: How good the project manager’s relationship is with the project’s end-users and stakeholders.
options.C: The efficiency of the warranty service.
options.D: Delivering value and conforming to project requirements.

explanation: It’s not enough to complete a project on time and under budget. You need to deliver value by creating a suitable product for your stakeholders’ needs. Customer satisfaction is about making sure that the people who are paying for the end product are happy with what they ultimately get. Conformance to requirements and usability of deliverables is the basis of customer satisfaction as they allow you to measure how well your product meets expectations.

stem: 4 months into project execution, the project manager noticed that the performance of some of the team members was deteriorating, while others continued to perform well. What should the project manager do to get the whole team back on track?

options.A: Openly discuss the poor performance of certain team members with the whole team in order to come up with a joint solution.
options.B: Motivate underperforming team members by incorporating a competitive reward system that offers a bonus for top performers.
options.C: Avoid interfering in order to give team members a chance to improve their performance.
options.D: Identify the causes of bad performance, solicit systematic feedback, and implement adequate solutions based on findings.
